Participant groups and methodology are clearly described. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and the study should be included in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

Full text provided appears incomplete (only title and abstract/metadata). Based on the abstract, the study meets some inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (task involves inhibition — go/no-go animal detection), and I8 (within-group task contrast: targets vs distractors). However, I cannot verify key required criteria from the incomplete text: I7 (presence of a group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked statistical map) and I10 (clear reporting of whole-brain results in coordinates/figures/text). The abstract reports activations in multiple brain regions but does not provide enough detail to confirm a voxelwise group analysis or that whole-brain results are reported in a usable form. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are clearly met from the abstract. Because the full text is incomplete, I must exclude this record pending full-text review; the exclusion is due to inability to confirm I7 and I10 from available content.

This fMRI study used a task-based N-Back working memory paradigm (an executive function domain) and reports voxelwise, group-level SPM analyses. The methods describe creation of SPM{T} maps and a random-effects, within-subject one-way ANOVA using task contrasts (e.g., 3-back minus 1-back) and report MNI coordinates for significant clusters. Although the authors limited the search volume to an a priori ROI and applied small-volume correction, voxelwise group-level task-evoked maps and within-group contrasts are clearly reported. Participants are a defined group of smokers. Core article content (introduction, full methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function) in healthy adults. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise random-effects analyses contrasting task periods (retrieval/manipulation) against maintenance, corrected for multiple comparisons (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures), and also reports within-group contrasts (manipulation vs retrieval and task vs maintenance). Thus it provides qualifying within-group task activation maps from a task in the executive-domain. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/rest-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met.

Full text provided is incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata). The abstract indicates the paper reports PET and fMRI data and discusses vigilance/sustained attention (so I5 and I6 appear satisfied). However, I cannot verify crucial eligibility requirements: there is no available information to confirm whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked maps (I7), nor that any within-group task contrast is reported (I8). I also cannot confirm reporting format (I10) or participant/contrast details (I9). Because the full text is incomplete and key inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed, the study is excluded from the meta-analysis at this stage. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are positively met based on the provided content.

This study reports task-related changes in mutual information (functional connectivity) during an N-back working memory task but does not present any group-level, voxelwise task-evoked activation maps. Instead analyses are ROI-based (90-region parcellation) connectivity comparisons between rest and task. Therefore it meets exclusion criteria E4 (connectivity-only analyses without task activation maps) and E3 (analyses are region-based rather than voxelwise whole-brain activation). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI task study), I6 (working memory task = executive function), I8 (within-group task contrast comparing rest vs N-back for connectivity), I9 (healthy participant group). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no group-level, voxelwise task-evoked statistical activation map reported). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This fMRI study assesses planning (Tower of London) in healthy adults and reports within-subject contrasts (Difficult vs Control; Easy vs Control) and group comparisons, so I5, I6, I8 and I9 are satisfied. However, the paper does not present a group-level voxelwise task activation map; analyses are based on individually-derived t-maps quantified within manually defined volumes-of-interest (VOIs) and between-group comparisons were performed on VOI summary measures (spatial extent percentages). Thus it reports ROI-based/group ROI statistics rather than a voxelwise whole-brain group-level activation map. Exclusion criterion E3 is therefore met. Inclusion criterion I7 (at least one group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical map) is not met. Full text appears complete. Decision: EXCLUDED (reason: E3).

The study is an empirical task-based fMRI investigation using n-back working memory tasks (letters, shapes, locations), which directly addresses executive function (working memory). The abstract describes voxelwise statistical comparisons of activation patterns across stimulus types, implying group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses and within-group task contrasts. Therefore it appears to meet inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. However, the provided ‘full text’ is incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata are present), so I cannot verify detailed methods/results or confirm tables/figures of whole-brain results; thus I flag fulltext_incomplete=true and assign moderate confidence.

This manuscript is a methodological/review-style paper that illustrates covariance-based analyses (structural equation modeling and PLS) using PET data examples, rather than reporting standard task-evoked, group-level voxelwise activation maps. It focuses on connectivity/covariance analyses and does not provide conventional within-group, voxelwise task activation contrasts or coordinate-based whole-brain activation tables required for inclusion. Therefore it meets exclusion criteria for connectivity-only/methods focus and being non-empirical/methods-review in nature.

The abstract reports an empirical task-based fMRI study using the Counting Stroop (an inhibition/cognitive-interference task) with within-subject interference vs. neutral contrasts and group-level fMRI results (significant ACC activation reported). This satisfies inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (executive function - inhibition/cognitive control), I8 (within-group task contrast), and I9 (within-group adult sample). The abstract also reports group-level statistical results (P ≤ 10^-4) consistent with a voxelwise group contrast and reports activation loci, meeting I7 and I10 likely; however, the full article text/figures/tables are not provided here. Full text is incomplete (only abstract/metadata available), so confidence is moderate. Full text should be obtained to verify voxelwise whole-brain maps and coordinate reporting before final data extraction.

This is an H2(15)O PET study using a task-based N-back working memory paradigm (executive function). It reports voxelwise, group-level SPM99 analyses (2-back minus 0-back) for within-group contrasts in both healthy controls and schizophrenic patients, with whole-brain activation maps, coordinates, and figures. Methods, results, and discussion are present in full. Thus all inclusion criteria for task modality, executive-domain task, whole-brain voxelwise analysis, within-group contrasts, participant groups, and reporting of whole-brain results are met. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply.

This is an fMRI task study that includes an established executive-function task (incongruent color-word Stroop — inhibition/cognitive control) performed during scanning, and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level activation contrasts. The paper provides within-group task contrasts (e.g., distraction-specific map (PD+HD)>(P+H), pain-specific contrasts (P−H), (PD−HD), and (PD−HD)>(P−H)), uses voxelwise SPM99 analyses across subjects, and reports whole-brain results in the text and tables. Participants are a within-group sample of healthy volunteers. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5–I10. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using an emotional counting Stroop, a well-established inhibition/cognitive-control (executive function) paradigm. The paper reports group-level voxelwise nonparametric (KS) statistical maps and provides coordinates and corrected p-values for within-group contrasts (negative vs neutral; fixation vs task), satisfying whole-brain voxelwise reporting even though slice coverage was partial. Participants are a within-group sample of healthy adults and results are presented in text/figures/tables. All inclusion criteria for the review are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is an empirical fMRI task-based investigation using the Stroop task (inhibition/selective attention), which falls within executive function domains. The paper reports voxelwise, group-level statistical parametric maps (SPM99) and provides within-group task contrasts for both TBI patients and healthy controls (group activation maps, tables and figures). Whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (group pooled maps), and results are reported in tables/figures. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures).

Full text is incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). From available information: inclusion criteria met - I5 (PET task-based study), I6 (tasks involve working memory/time estimation within executive domains), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported: e.g., counting no auditory stimulation vs counting with auditory stimulation). However I7 (clear evidence of whole-brain, group-level voxelwise statistical maps) cannot be verified from the provided content, nor can I10 (reporting of whole-brain results in tables/coordinates/figures) be confirmed. No exclusion criteria E3-E6 are clearly met based on available info. Because the full text is incomplete and the key requirement I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results) cannot be confirmed, the study cannot be included at this stage.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (a core executive function). It reports within-group voxelwise contrasts (e.g., Load 7 vs Load 3) analyzed at the group level using whole-brain voxelwise statistics (voxel-level threshold with cluster-level correction) and provides tables/figures of activated/deactivated clusters. Participants are healthy adults (within-group contrasts reported). The manuscript includes full methods, results, and discussion (complete full text). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-groups-only, not non-empirical). Therefore it satisfies all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based cognitive control paradigm (occluded target switching visual search) that probes executive functions (working memory, cognitive flexibility/switching, response preparation). The paper reports whole-brain, voxel-wise group-level contrasts (e.g., target switching vs. non-switching) with FDR correction, tables and figures of voxel-wise results, and within-group task contrasts. Participant sample is healthy adults. Reporting includes voxel-wise maps/coordinates. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of executive function (planning) using the Tower of London task (I5,I6). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (SPM5; second-level ‘planning vs. baseline’ and ‘task load’ contrasts) with voxelwise thresholds and cluster tables/figures (I7,I10). It includes within-group task contrasts (main effects of task and task-load across subjects) and within-pair comparisons (paired contrasts) satisfying the requirement for a within-group activation map (I8). Participant type (monozygotic twins, including some meeting OCD criteria) is acceptable per inclusion criteria (I9). No exclusion criteria apply: not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, and not only between-group contrasts. Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and violates none.

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study of executive function (interference suppression and response inhibition) using a task-based paradigm (combined flanker and go/no-go). The paper reports within-group, voxelwise task contrasts (incongruent > neutral; no-go > neutral) analyzed with SPM99 and random-effects group analyses. Results include whole-brain voxelwise contrasts and regression analyses, with coordinates and cluster reports, and separate within-group maps for children and adults. Partial-brain acquisition is acceptable under I7 because voxelwise analyses were performed. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for task-based fMRI executive-function activation maps and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, and detailed experimental procedures).

The study is a PET task-based investigation of the WCST in healthy subjects and thus appears to meet I5 (PET, task-based), I6 (executive function: WCST - cognitive flexibility/working memory), I8 (within-group task contrasts vs control/baseline), and I9 (participant group qualifies). However, only title/abstract and metadata are provided here (full text incomplete), so I cannot verify that at least one group-level voxelwise whole-brain analysis or coordinate reporting is present (I7 not confirmed) nor confirm details required by I10. Because I7 cannot be confirmed from the supplied content, the study cannot be confirmed to meet all inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met based on available information.

This is an event-related fMRI Stroop study of cognitive control with healthy adults that reports within-group task contrasts and coordinate results, but all voxelwise statistical testing was conducted within an a priori ROI mask (BA 24/32, 8/9/46, 7/40) rather than as whole-brain, group-level voxelwise maps. Therefore it does not provide qualifying whole-brain voxelwise activation results. Exclusion ID E3 applies (reports only ROI/masked analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI task of executive control), I6 (inhibition/cognitive control domain), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported), I9 (eligible participant group), I10 (results reported with coordinates/tables). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level task-evoked map; analyses confined to ROIs). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based fMRI study of inhibitory control using a stop-signal paradigm (executive function: inhibition). The full text includes Introduction, Methods (task details, subjects, image acquisition, analysis), Results (group-level voxelwise activation maps, Bonferroni-corrected voxelwise threshold, coordinates table), and Discussion. The paper reports within-group task contrasts (GO ONLY vs GO/STOP; parametric STOP-likelihood analysis; correct vs incorrect STOP trials) at the group level using voxelwise statistical maps and provides coordinates and figures. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study reports behavioral task-switching data collected in three testing environments (including participants tested inside an operating MRI scanner) but explicitly states that brain-imaging data are not reported in this paper. Thus it does not provide any within-group, voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps or any reported fMRI/PET activation contrasts that could be pooled in the meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (task falls within executive function domain: cognitive flexibility/task switching) and I9 (participant groups are acceptable). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no reported fMRI/PET activation results reported in the paper), I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps provided), and I8 (no within-group task activation contrast reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) directly apply. Full text appears complete and includes methods, results, and discussion, but lacks imaging results needed for this meta-analysis, so the study must be excluded.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (N-back), an executive function domain. It reports within-group voxelwise analyses (2-back > 0-back) with group-level whole-brain random-effects results (FWE-corrected maps) and ROI/SVC follow-ups. Methods, results, and discussion are present (full text complete). Therefore it meets all applicable inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using the Stroop task, which assesses inhibition/action-monitoring (executive function), satisfying I5 and I6. The paper reports voxelwise, whole-brain group analyses using SPM (fixed- and random-effects), and provides within-group task-versus-control contrasts (one-sample t-tests) for both patients and controls, meeting I7 and I8. Participant groups include clinical OCD patients and healthy controls, acceptable per I9. Whole-brain results are presented in figures and tables of coordinates, satisfying I10. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical paper) apply. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present; fulltext_incomplete is false.

This is an empirical, event-related fMRI study using a Sternberg verbal working memory task (an established executive-function domain). The authors performed voxelwise, group-level random-effects analyses (one-sample t-tests) contrasting task vs control within participants for encoding, maintenance, and retrieval periods, and reported whole-brain activation foci (tables/figures), despite restricting reporting to ROIs and having incomplete inferior cerebellar coverage. These analyses satisfy within-group task contrasts and voxelwise group maps required by the review. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study using a graded n-back working memory paradigm (an established executive function). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise GLM deactivation maps (random-effects t/maps thresholded at p=0.001) and group-level ICA components derived from whole-brain EPI data, and describes within-group task contrasts (task vs baseline and load-related effects across 0-, 1-, and 2-back). Participants are healthy volunteers (acceptable). Thus all required inclusion criteria are met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function), I6 (working memory task), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (whole-brain results clearly reported). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of planning (an executive function) using the Tower of London paradigm. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (GLM, random-effects, FWE-corrected p<0.05, cluster extent threshold), contrasts of ToL versus two active control conditions (within-group task contrasts), and parametric within-group analyses across planning complexity; results are reported as coordinates/tables and figures. Participants are a within-group sample of healthy adults. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a Stroop paradigm (cognitive control/inhibition) in healthy participants. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (e.g., IC vs CC contrasts), including tables/coordinates and ROI follow-ups, and presents within-group task contrasts (incongruent vs congruent and emotional word contrasts). These meet the meta-analysis requirements for executive-function task activations and do not violate any exclusion criteria. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, allowing assessment of methods and contrasts.

The study reports task-based fMRI of verbal working memory (n-back) in healthy adults, with group-level voxelwise analyses and a within-group task contrast (n-back vs sensorimotor control). The paper describes whole-brain multislice acquisition, voxelwise sinusoidal regression and regression analyses relating fMRI response power to reaction time, and reports peak coordinates for activations. These satisfy the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for executive-function task activations. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and includes within-group contrasts). Note: the provided full text appears incomplete (title and abstract/metadata only), so I flagged fulltext_incomplete=true and applied the inclusion criteria based on the available abstract and metadata.

This is a task-based fMRI study using the CPT-IP (a sustained attention/vigilance task), reporting within-group contrasts (CPT-IP vs control) and group composite voxelwise t-maps with voxel-by-voxel comparisons and cluster-based multiple-comparison correction. Whole-brain acquisition (24 contiguous slices covering most of the brain) and voxelwise analyses are described, and results are reported in figures/tables/text for both bipolar and healthy groups. Thus it satisfies I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (vigilance/executive domain), I7 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (participant groups acceptable), and I10 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that examines working memory (n-back) and visual attention tasks with parametric load manipulations in 22 healthy adults. It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM2) with corrected thresholds and conjunction/subtraction contrasts, including within-group task contrasts (e.g., 2-back vs 0-back; 4-balls vs 2-balls) and ROI follow-ups. Working memory is an established executive function domain, satisfying the review focus. The manuscript contains full methods, results, and discussion, and whole-brain results are described and thresholded appropriately. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This study is an empirical task-based fMRI investigation of executive function (working memory) using the Reading Span Test. It reports group-level, voxelwise random-effects analyses (SPM99) with voxelwise thresholds and presents within-group task contrasts (Read+Memory and Recognition phases) and reported activation clusters/coordinates for young and elderly groups. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion sections. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and it is empirical). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a digit n-back paradigm (working memory), an established executive function domain. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise activation maps (group correlation analysis after stereotaxic transformation, thresholded and displayed), and within-group contrasts (0-, 1-, 2-back versus baseline/control) for multiple participant groups (euthyroid, hyperthyroid, SCH, hypothyroid). Whole-brain activation maps and figures are presented and described in the text. Therefore all inclusion criteria for task-based, within-group, whole-brain voxelwise activation reporting are met, and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that probes emotional conflict resolution — a form of cognitive control/inhibition — using a modified Stroop paradigm. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise SPM random-effects contrasts (e.g., incongruent vs congruent; high vs low conflict-resolution), whole-brain/search-volume analyses, and within-group task contrasts in healthy volunteers. It therefore meets all inclusion criteria for an executive-function activation meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function domain) that reports voxelwise whole-brain group analyses and within-group contrasts. The paper presents voxelwise ANOVAs, planned within-group contrasts (e.g., combination > object/location in young adults), Talairach coordinates, figures, and tables of activations. Although only 21 axial slices were acquired, the analyses are voxelwise (partial-brain acquisition is allowed). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study reports task-based fMRI using a go/no-go variant probing inhibition and timing (executive function/cognitive control). It includes within-group one-sample voxelwise SPM analyses (controls) comparing unpredictable vs. predictable events and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results with coordinates and statistics. Thus it provides voxelwise task-evoked maps and within-group contrasts for at least one participant group (controls), satisfying the meta-analysis requirements. Participant groups (ADHD, unaffected siblings, controls) are reported and any group is acceptable. No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and not limited to between-group contrasts. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (N-back), an executive function. The paper reports group-level voxelwise analyses (group t-maps for 1-, 2-, 3-back vs 0-back) and provides within-group task contrasts for patient and control groups, with whole-brain voxelwise thresholding and reported peak coordinates. Methods, results, and discussion are present in full. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

Full text incomplete. From the abstract, this is a PET task study of rapid visual information processing (sustained attention and working memory) and reports task vs rest activations in healthy volunteers, so it appears to meet I5 (PET task-based), I6 (vigilance/working memory), I8 (within-group task contrast), I9 (within-group healthy volunteers), and I10 (whole-brain results described in text). However, the provided full text is incomplete/missing, and I cannot verify that a group-level, voxelwise whole-brain statistical analysis/map was performed or reported (I7). Because I7 cannot be confirmed from the incomplete full text, I exclude the study pending full-text verification.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: (I5) it is an fMRI task-based study of executive function (working memory 2-back); (I6) the task falls within an executive function domain (working memory); (I7) voxelwise whole-brain analyses were performed (SPM-99, group-level maps reported; acquisition covered the brain with contiguous axial slices—partial or whole-brain acquisition allowed); (I8) within-group task contrasts are reported (WM vs vigilance within controls and within high-risk relatives; Figure 2 and text present these within-group activations); (I9) participant group is acceptable (adolescents/young adults; clinical high-risk relatives are permitted); (I10) whole-brain results are reported with coordinates and detailed tables/figures. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, and within-group contrasts are provided). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore include the study for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). From the abstract it is clear this is an event-related fMRI GO/NOGO task addressing inhibition and cognitive control, so inclusion criteria I5 and I6 are satisfied. However the supplied content does not allow confirmation of required whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked maps (I7) or explicit within-group task contrasts (I8). No exclusion criteria (E3-E6) are evident from the abstract, but because not all inclusion criteria can be verified from the incomplete full text, the study cannot be included at this stage. Recommend obtaining the complete article to confirm I7 and I8 (and I10, if relevant).

This is an empirical fMRI study using an n-back working memory task (executive function domain) with healthy participants. The paper reports both within-group contrasts (parametric linear trend of load n within subjects and ROI time-series analyses) and a group-level, voxelwise random-effects map-wise analysis (normalized t-maps with whole-brain correction), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results. The task and analyses clearly fall within the executive function domain (working memory), and results are reported in standard formats (text, figures, tables). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical).

This is an fMRI task-based study using an auditory verbal N-back (working memory) paradigm (executive function domain). The paper reports voxelwise, group-level random-effects SPM analyses (two-back vs zero-back), with within-group contrasts presented for each genotype and whole-brain results summarized in tables/figures including MNI coordinates and cluster statistics. Methods describe whole-brain preprocessing/normalization and voxel-by-voxel GLM analyses. Therefore it meets I5 (fMRI task-based executive function), I6 (working memory), I7 (voxelwise whole-brain analyses reported), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (whole-brain results presented in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). The provided full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive control (modified flanker) reporting group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses and within-group task contrasts. The paper describes BOLD fMRI methods, SPM99 voxelwise contrasts (INC>CON, NOGO>CON and INC>NEU/NOGO>NEU), random-effects group analyses, and reports activation maps/tables and correlations. Participants (n=57 healthy adults) are acceptable. Results are presented in text, figures and tables. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion.

This is an fMRI, task-based study of context processing (AX-CPT) relevant to executive function (working memory/inhibition), with voxelwise group-level analyses reported (cluster-thresholded coordinates). However, the paper reports primarily between-group ANOVAs and group differences (B-cue, delay, and interaction) and does not present or describe a within-group task activation contrast (e.g., main effect of B cue vs implicit baseline) for any single group. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I9, and I10 but violates exclusion criterion E5 (only between-group contrasts reported with no within-group task activation contrast). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a modified Stroop task (an inhibition/selective-attention executive function paradigm). The paper reports within-group voxelwise activation maps (SPM99) for both patients and controls (Stroop activation vs rest), includes group-level random-effects comparisons, and provides whole-brain results in tables and figures. Although slice coverage was limited (15 slices), analyses were voxelwise and reported comprehensively. All required inclusion criteria for task, modality, within-group contrasts, and whole-brain voxelwise reporting are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of working memory (an executive function domain) using a task-based Sternberg paradigm. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM99 one-sample t-tests and random-effects ANOVA) with FDR-corrected thresholds and tables/figures of activated clusters/coordinates. At least one within-group task contrast is presented (memory task vs sensorimotor control and parametric contrasts of load and delay). Participants are human (healthy adults). Whole-brain results are clearly described in text, tables, and figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing extraction of voxelwise task activation data for meta-analysis. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of cognitive control/executive function (working memory, response selection/conflict). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses and within-group task contrasts (e.g., Repeat-Unexpected vs Repeat-Expected; Refresh vs Repeat), with coordinates and ROI analyses. Participants are a within-group healthy adult sample. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore it satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of semantic (category) verbal fluency that explicitly examines executive components (response inhibition, working memory, sustained attention) associated with paced vs. unpaced and overt vs. covert generation. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (one-sample t-tests, cluster-corrected p<.05) and within-group task contrasts (word generation overall and condition contrasts versus control/saying “nothing”). Participant group is healthy adults (acceptable). Results are reported in text, tables, and figures; full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study of cognitive set-shifting (WCST variant) that reports group-level, voxelwise task-evoked statistical analyses and coordinates. It satisfies: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (cognitive flexibility/set shifting — an executive domain), I7 (group-level voxelwise analyses reported; partial slice coverage was used but voxelwise analysis was performed), I8 (within-group task contrast: shift-related activity vs pre-shift baseline), I9 (healthy adult participant group reported), and I10 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates and figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion and references; fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical fMRI task-based study (MSIT) probing cognitive control/interference in healthy adults. The paper reports within-group voxelwise interference vs control contrasts at both individual and group levels, including group-averaged voxelwise t-tests in Talairach space and tables/figures of whole-brain activations. The task falls squarely within executive function/inhibition and cognitive control domains, and results include behavioral (RT, errors) and imaging maps. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References, so the full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Full text is incomplete/unavailable (JSON error: API rate limit exceeded). Although the title mentions neural and cognitive measures of executive function, the methods and results are not accessible, so I cannot verify any required inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria not verifiable: I5 (no confirmation of fMRI or PET task-based imaging), I6 (task domain not clearly described as working memory/inhibition/etc.), I7 (no evidence of a group-level voxelwise whole-brain analysis), I8 (no confirmation of a within-group task contrast), I9 (participant groups cannot be evaluated but this alone would not exclude the study), I10 (no reporting of whole-brain results in text/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) can be confidently applied from the available metadata. Because the full text is incomplete, the study must be excluded at this stage; inclusion can be reconsidered if a complete full text is provided.

This fMRI study uses a task-based 2-back working-memory paradigm with facial stimuli (an executive function: working memory) in patients and matched controls. The methods report voxelwise whole-brain group-level random-effects analyses (SPM99) and present within-group task activation results and tables/coordinates for each group, satisfying requirements for whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level maps and within-group contrasts. Participants include clinical samples (schizophrenia) which are acceptable. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and not limited to between-group contrasts. Therefore inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that includes the Tower of London (planning) task, which is an established executive function domain. The paper reports group-level (random-effects) voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM) with results thresholded across the whole brain and presents activation maps and coordinate results for within-group contrasts (TOL easy and difficult vs yoked baselines). Healthy participant within-group contrasts are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical). Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using the counting Stroop (inhibition/cognitive control) that reports voxelwise, whole-brain group analyses (AFNI, Talairach normalization, cluster-thresholding) and a within-group contrast (incongruent vs. congruent). Healthy adult participants were tested and results are reported in text/tables/figures (including coordinates and cluster results). The full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for a meta-analysis of executive function task activations and should be INCLUDED.

This paper reports an empirical task-based fMRI study of verbal working memory (two-back), an established executive function domain. Methods describe whole-brain EPI acquisition and voxelwise, group-level random-effects SPM99 analyses; results include within-group task contrasts for patients and controls, between-group contrasts, coordinate tables and figures. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Limitations. Thus all required inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using the n-back working memory task (an executive function domain). It reports within-group voxelwise whole-brain analyses (n-back conditions vs 0-back), trend analyses across loads, and presents group and within-group activation maps and coordinates. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using an n-back working memory paradigm (executive function domain). It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM2 random-effects one-sample t-tests) with coordinates/tables and figures for within-group task contrasts (e.g., L2–L1, NI–LI, NC–LC). Tasks fall within working memory domain; participant group (healthy adults) is included. Results include whole-brain statistical maps and ROI analyses but are not limited to ROI-only reporting. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an empirical PET activation study using the Tower of London planning task (an established executive function: planning). The full text contains Introduction, Methods (PET acquisition, SPM voxelwise preprocessing and statistical analyses), Results (group-level category contrast: planning vs rest; correlation analyses of complexity and movement; tables/figures of whole-brain SPM results), and Discussion. The study reports within-group voxelwise task contrasts (planning minus rest and parametric correlations) suitable for inclusion. Whole-brain voxelwise analyses are performed and reported; partial brain coverage (field-of-view note) does not preclude inclusion per review criteria. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and should be included.

Full text unavailable/incomplete: provided full-text content returns an API error and core article content (methods, results) is missing. Therefore I cannot verify required inclusion criteria. Unable to confirm: I5 (task-based fMRI/PET assessing executive function), I6 (task falls within established executive domains), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group-level maps), I8 (within-group task contrast reported), I9 (participant groups acceptable but within-group contrast unverified), I10 (results reported in coordinate/figure/text). No exclusion criteria (E3-E6) can be determined from the incomplete record. Because core information is missing, the study cannot be confirmed to meet ALL inclusion criteria and is excluded pending full text. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met/unknown: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using the n-back working memory task (an established executive function domain). The full text reports voxelwise, whole-brain group-level statistical maps (mixed-effects FLAME analyses) and provides within-group contrasts (e.g., 2-back>1-back, 2-back>0-back, 1-back>0-back) for both MDD patients and healthy controls. Results include cluster thresholds, Z-statistics and coordinate tables/figures. Although acquisition used 24 axial slices, analyses were voxelwise rather than ROI-limited. The study therefore meets all inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10) and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E6). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a PET task study of motor planning (planning is an executive domain), with voxelwise parametric maps reported for a subject, but it does not provide a group-level, voxelwise task-evoked statistical map. The report is a single-subject proof-of-principle (parametric maps and ROI results for one subject) rather than a group-level within-group contrast. Therefore it fails to meet I7 (group-level voxelwise map) and I8 (within-group task contrast at the group level). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based PET), I6 (planning task within executive domains), I9 (participant group acceptable), I10 (voxelwise/parametric results presented in text/figures). Exclusion criteria met: none. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function domain). It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (fixed-effect in Experiment 1; random-effect in Experiment 2) using SPM, with thresholding and cluster inference and peak coordinates provided. Within-group task contrasts (working memory task versus control) are reported and used in the group analyses. Results are presented as voxelwise subtraction images and coordinate tables/figures. The study is not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and includes complete methods, results and discussion. Therefore it fulfills all inclusion criteria for task activation meta-analysis.

This is an event-related fMRI study that manipulates working memory load (two-back) and perceptual load using a task-based paradigm, and reports voxelwise whole-brain group analyses (with coordinates) comparing task conditions (e.g., two-back vs one-back). The study thus provides within-group task contrasts, includes working memory as an executive function domain, reports whole-brain voxelwise results (coordinates and thresholding), and includes participant group results. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical).

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study of a working memory (executive function) task comparing structured vs unstructured sequences. The paper reports within-group, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FDR-corrected, peaks and coordinates reported) and supplementary ROI analyses; behavioral and control experiments are included. All required inclusion criteria are met (fMRI task-based executive function; working memory domain; whole-brain voxelwise group analyses with reported coordinates; within-group contrasts; participant group reported). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, and experimental procedures).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that includes an executive function paradigm (color-naming Stroop, an inhibition/selective-attention task) and reports voxelwise, group-level statistical maps. The paper reports a within-group random-effects one-sample t-test for the motor task in controls, and reports group-level voxelwise two-sample (bipolar vs control) random-effects analyses for both motor and Stroop contrasts. Analyses were whole-brain SPM2 voxelwise maps with cluster correction and results presented in tables/figures. Participants include clinical (bipolar) and control groups; individual subject contrasts (task vs control conditions) were computed. Therefore the study meets I5 (task-based fMRI including an executive task), I6 (Stroop falls in inhibition/executive domain), I7 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain maps), I8 (at least one within-group task contrast reported), I9 (clinical sample allowed), and I10 (results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that reports whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level activation maps for mental arithmetic. The task includes a working-memory component (retaining intermediate results) and thus falls within an executive-function domain (working memory). The paper reports within-group contrasts (active math vs control) for musicians, non-musicians, and all subjects combined, with voxelwise random-effects analyses and figures/tables of coordinates. Results are whole-brain (composite activation maps and coordinate tables) rather than ROI-only or connectivity-only. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI task study using a counting Stroop (inhibition/response conflict) paradigm with button-press responses. The paper reports within-group, voxelwise group-level activation contrasts (Stroop vs control) with whole-brain cluster correction and provides tables/figures of significant clusters. Although slice coverage is limited (19 sagittal slices), analyses were voxelwise and thus satisfy the partial-brain allowance. A within-group task contrast is clearly reported for healthy adult participants. Functional connectivity analyses are also present but do not preclude inclusion since task activation maps are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets I5–I10 and qualifies for inclusion.

Exclusion E3 met: the manuscript performs and reports ROI-based extractions/analyses of basal ganglia activation and volumetry, with statistical tests on ROI-derived measures (PAUC and volumes). While individual voxelwise timecourses were computed, the paper does not present or report group-level, voxelwise whole-brain (or partial-brain) task-activation statistical maps or coordinate tables; results and inferential statistics are ROI-focused. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI study of executive/response control), I6 (task falls within executive domains — inhibition/set-shifting), I8 (within-group task contrast: correct target trials vs baseline/event-related activation), I9 (within-group contrasts reported for participant groups). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no clear group-level, voxelwise task-evoked statistical map reported). Therefore the study must be excluded per E3.

This is a task-based fMRI study using an n-back working memory paradigm (executive domain) with healthy participants. The full text reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (one-sample t-test random-effects for 2-back vs 0-back and between-group ANOVA), including tables and figures of activations and cluster statistics. A within-group task contrast (2-back vs 0-back) is explicitly reported. The paper is empirical and contains complete sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and violates no exclusion criteria.

Exclusion E3 applies: the study reports fMRI working-memory task data but all reported analyses were ROI-based (authors state explicitly: “All the analyses reported... were performed with ROIs”), and no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps are presented. Inclusion met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (working memory is an executive function), I8 (within-group task contrasts and paired t-tests reported), I9 (healthy participant group). Inclusion not met: I7 (no group-level voxelwise whole-brain statistical map reported). Therefore the study must be excluded under E3.

The abstract describes an empirical task-based fMRI study of spatial working memory (a canonical executive function) using a 2-back and match-to-center paradigm. The paper reports whole-brain fMRI activation patterns and explicitly describes within-group activation contrasts and patterns for both alcoholics and control groups, indicating voxelwise task-evoked maps. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (working memory), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analysis), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (clinical participant group acceptable), and I10 (results appear reported in text/figures). However, only the abstract/metadata were provided here (no full methods/results/discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=true and there is some uncertainty (request full text to confirm voxelwise statistical maps/coordinate tables). Recommend retrieval of the complete article for definitive extraction and coordinate verification.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based verbal n-back working memory paradigm (executive function domain). It reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (random-effects GLM, voxelwise ANOVA, conjunctions) and within-group task contrasts (e.g., 2B>1B, task vs 0-back baseline, BSD>BRW). Participants are a within-group healthy adult sample. Results are reported as voxelwise maps and ROI/peak coordinates. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10) and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory (n-back), an established executive function domain. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise SPM analyses (one-sample t-tests, full-factorial and paired t-tests) with whole-brain thresholds and MNI localization, and explicitly reports within-group task contrasts (2>0 and 3>0 back) for patients and controls. Clinical sample (severe diffuse TBI) is acceptable. Results are reported as activation maps/clusters and described in the text. All required inclusion criteria (I5–I10) are met; no exclusion criteria apply. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (N-back) for emotional prosody and lexico-semantic emotion in healthy adults. It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM5 parametric and random-effects second-level analyses) with coordinates and thresholds, and includes within-group task contrasts (linear parametric increases with load; paired t-tests and conjunctions). Whole-brain acquisition and voxelwise results (tables/figures) are provided. Participants are a within-group sample of healthy young adults. Thus the study meets all inclusion criteria for task-based executive function fMRI and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of inhibitory control (executive function) using a simple warned RT paradigm (inhibition domain). The paper reports within-group, voxelwise, group-level contrasts (one-sample t-tests, random-effects models) with whole-brain coverage and tables of coordinates and thresholded voxelwise results. Contrasts include within-group comparisons (e.g., cued vs no-cued; short vs long SOA) suitable as task activation maps. Full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10) and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of thought suppression, which constitutes an executive-control/inhibition paradigm. The paper reports within-group voxelwise, group-level statistical contrasts (e.g., SUPPRESS vs FREE-THOUGHT; CLEAR vs FREE-THOUGHT) analyzed with SPM99 and thresholded t-maps, with whole-brain coverage. Participants are healthy adults and results are described at the group level (brain regions/BA reported). Thus the study satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10, and none of the exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of attentional control/conflict (Simon and spatial Stroop), which falls within executive functions (inhibition/conflict). It reports voxelwise, random-effects group analyses (whole-brain contrasts: Simon Incongruent > Simon Congruent; Stroop Incongruent > Stroop Congruent), conjunction/disjunction and direct contrast maps, and describes cluster thresholds and peak locations (tables/figures). Within-group task contrasts are clearly reported for the healthy participant group. Results are presented as whole-brain activation maps and tables/figures rather than ROI-only or connectivity-only analyses. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study of non-perceptual attentional set-shifting (cognitive flexibility), meeting the review objective. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise SPM96 analyses (conjunctions and contrasts such as A–R, A–T, A–W, A–L) with whole-brain statistical thresholding and coordinates described. It reports within-group task contrasts (task vs rest and condition subtractions), uses healthy adult participants, and presents whole-brain results in the text (with coordinates). It is empirical and not ROI-only or connectivity-only. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an original, task-based fMRI study examining contextual inhibition (an executive function: inhibition). The paper reports within-group voxelwise whole-brain analyses (ACT vs REST, INH vs REST, conjunctions) with corrected statistical maps and tables/figures, and provides group-level results. Participants are healthy adults and contrasts are within-group. Whole-brain results are reported in text, figures, and tables of coordinates. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for an executive-function activation meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of inhibition (Go/Nogo) in schizophrenia that directly addresses executive function/cognitive control. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (complete). The study reports voxelwise, group-level statistical maps and corrected cluster thresholds (AFNI 3dDeconvolve and voxel-wise t tests), with tables of coordinates and figures for contrasts. It includes within-group task contrasts (e.g., Nogo–Go, Go/Cue–Go/Noncue, Cued-Nogo–Uncued-Nogo) and reports task-effect activations (task main effects) and correlations, satisfying within-group contrast requirement. Participants include a clinical sample (schizophrenia) and healthy controls; at least one within-group contrast is reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest, not only between-group contrasts, not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for pooling executive-function task activations.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using the N-back working memory task (an executive function domain). The paper reports voxelwise, whole-brain group-level analyses using SPM99 (thresholds and cluster criteria described), and contrasts of task vs control (0-back vs 2-back) were estimated at each voxel producing within-subject and group contrast images. Within-group task activations are described (e.g., severe cases showing bilateral parietal/OFC activations) and results are reported in tables/figures with coordinates. Participant groups include a clinical OCD sample and matched controls. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using an n-back working memory task (executive function). The paper reports group- and within-subject voxelwise SPM99 analyses (random-effects ANOVAs), with whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (on-periods vs off-periods) and reported activation coordinates and clusters. Although slice coverage excluded the cerebellum, analyses were voxelwise rather than ROI-restricted. Results include within-group task activation maps for participants (MDMA users and controls) and coordinates are reported in the text and figures. Thus all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) are satisfied, and none of the exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study (3T BOLD) that investigates Stroop-like inhibition paradigms (colour, number, shape), directly addressing the executive function domain of inhibition. The paper reports within-group, voxelwise first-level contrasts (congruent vs neutral; incongruent vs neutral) and a random-effects, second-level group analysis using SPM2, with whole-brain voxelwise results thresholded and coordinates reported in tables and text. Although ROI analyses are also performed, whole-brain voxelwise group maps and between-modality voxelwise comparisons are presented. Participant sample is a within-group (healthy adults). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study using a 2-back working memory paradigm (executive function domain), with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2, FDR-corrected) and multiple within-group task contrasts (e.g., Binding, Sign, Speech vs rest; Sign>Speech; 2Binding>Sign+Speech). Participants are a defined within-group (hearing native signers). Results are reported in tables and described in detail in the text. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Appropriate for inclusion in a meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using a Stroop paradigm (inhibition/conflict-monitoring), clearly within executive-function domains. The paper reports voxelwise, group-level SPM analyses with whole-brain coverage and provides activation coordinates and corrected thresholds (FDR), and presents within-group task contrasts (conflict/incongruent vs congruent; conflict-level contrasts) and group-level task activation maps. EEG connectivity is additional but does not replace task activation reporting. Thus it meets I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and within-group contrasts are reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an event-related fMRI study (1.5T) reporting whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses of within-group task contrasts comparing normal vs malingered recognition responses. Although the primary task is recognition memory, the experimental manipulation and contrasts specifically target cognitive control processes (response suppression/inhibition, response generation, working memory/monitoring) during deceptive responding. The paper reports brain activation patterns in response to increasing working memory load in MTBI patients and healthy controls and describes group-level activation differences and load-related modulation, which implies within-group task contrasts and voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked analyses typical for NeuroImage fMRI reports. Therefore inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 appear satisfied. However, the provided content is limited to title/abstract/metadata (no methods/results figures/tables), so the full text is incomplete; I recommend obtaining the full PDF to confirm voxelwise statistical maps and coordinate reporting. No exclusion criteria are met based on the abstract.

The article reports an empirical fMRI study using the counting Stroop (a well-established inhibition/cognitive-control executive task). It provides whole-brain, voxelwise GLM contrasts (e.g., number Stroop vs neutral during no-stimulation) and reports activation coordinates; within-group task contrasts are explicitly analyzed. Participants are healthy adults. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

Full text is incomplete (only title/abstract metadata provided), so key inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed. Based on the abstract, the study is an empirical task-based fMRI study (I5) that uses categorization tasks engaging executive processes (working memory, inhibition, attention) consistent with executive function domains (I6). The abstract reports within-group task contrasts (rule-based vs similarity-based; degraded vs similarity) satisfying I8, and participants are young adults (I9). However, I7 (presence of whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps) cannot be verified from the abstract alone, and I10 (acceptable reporting of whole-brain results in coordinates/figures/text) likewise cannot be confirmed. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are clearly met. Because the full text (methods/results) is missing, I cannot verify ALL inclusion criteria; therefore the study is excluded pending full-text review.

This is an empirical fMRI study using the stop-signal task (an inhibition/cognitive-control paradigm). The paper reports within-group, voxelwise whole-brain SPM analyses (FWE-corrected and uncorrected maps), contrasts of interest (post-go speeding > post-go slowing) at the group level, and presents results in figures/tables. Participants are healthy adults and the task falls squarely within executive-function (inhibition) domain. Full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion and References. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (an established executive function domain). The experiment reports within-group task contrasts (MAT, PREP, EXEC) with group-level statistics (ANOVAs and t-tests) and GLM-based voxelwise modeling. Although much analysis was ROI-focused, the authors also examined delay-period activity unconstrained by ROIs (whole-brain/unconstrained voxelwise search) and used a voxelwise FFA localizer, indicating voxelwise group-level analyses were performed. Participants are a within-group sample of healthy volunteers. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using an N-back working memory task (an established executive function domain). The paper reports voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM99) with within-group contrasts (working memory levels vs 0-back) and random-effects group-level statistical maps; results are described in text and figures (with SVC applied for multiple comparisons but based on voxelwise maps). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for task-based whole-brain executive-function activation reporting. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This paper reports an event-related fMRI study of working memory (an executive function domain) in healthy adults, with task-based within-group contrasts and group random-effects (voxelwise) analyses and reported stereotactic coordinates and whole-brain maps. The full text contains introduction, methods (including whole-brain acquisition and GLM/group analyses), results, and discussion, so the article meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory (modified PASAT) in TBI patients and controls, reporting voxelwise, group-level random effects analyses using SPM96 with whole-brain coverage. The manuscript presents within-group task contrasts (mPASAT vs control/baseline) for each group, reports activation maps and tables of coordinates (Table 2 and figures), and describes laterality and dispersion indices derived from voxelwise activation. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for executive-function task activations (working memory) and provides whole-brain, within-group, voxelwise task-evoked results. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references).

This is an event-related fMRI empirical study of cognitive flexibility (task-switching) in OCD using a task-based paradigm. The paper reports voxelwise, group-level whole-brain analyses (SPM2) including within-group contrasts (task-switch minus task-repeat) for each group, with coordinates and figures/tables of activations. The task falls squarely within the executive function domain (cognitive flexibility). Partial-brain acquisition (25 axial slices) is reported but voxelwise group analyses are provided, which meets I7. Results include within-group maps, between-group contrasts, ROI supplemental analyses, and coordinate tables. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text is complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study of auditory verbal working memory (an executive function). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and reports voxelwise, group-level SPM analyses (within-group WM vs vigilance contrasts and whole-brain/random-effects analyses). Partial-brain acquisition (15 axial slices) is present but voxelwise analyses were performed, satisfying whole-brain/voxelwise requirement. Within-group contrasts are reported for groups. No exclusion criteria are met.

The full text reports an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive function (Stroop interference; inhibitory control) with healthy developmental participants. The paper includes within-group contrasts (incongruent vs congruent) and reports voxel-wise, group-level whole-brain (voxel-wise) analyses and maps/tables of age and performance correlations (voxel-wise regression with cluster thresholding). Although slice coverage was partial (only 6 slices used for all subjects), analyses were voxelwise rather than ROI-only. Thus all inclusion criteria are met (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Abstract reports an event-related fMRI study using three conflict tasks (including Stroop) with within-subject, within-group contrasts (incongruent vs congruent) and reports significant activations in anterior cingulate and prefrontal cortex, indicating task-based executive control (inhibition/conflict). This satisfies I5 (fMRI task-based), I6 (executive/inhibition tasks), I8 (within-group task contrast), and I9 (participant group acceptable). Full text is not provided (only abstract and metadata), so I cannot confirm whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses or the form of reported results (coordinates/figures) required by I7 and I10. Therefore I include the study provisionally for the meta-analysis, but with low confidence and fulltext_incomplete=true; recommend obtaining full article to confirm whole-brain voxelwise group maps and reporting details before final inclusion.

This is a task-based fMRI study that examines working memory (maintenance) and reasoning processes relevant to executive function. It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM99) with standard contrasts (reasoning vs rest, maintenance vs rest, reasoning vs maintenance) and provides coordinate-based results. Participants are a within-group sample of healthy adults. Thus all inclusion criteria are met (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and no exclusion criteria apply. The provided full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

Full text incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided); cannot verify required whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation maps. Based on abstract, study is an empirical fMRI working-memory task and reports within-group task contrasts: it satisfies I5 (fMRI study of executive function), I6 (working memory task), I8 (within-group task contrast), and I9 (participant group acceptable). However I7 (at least one group-level voxelwise whole-brain analysis) cannot be confirmed from the provided content, and I10 (clear reporting of whole-brain results via coordinates/figures/text) also cannot be confirmed. No exclusion criteria (E3,E4,E5,E6) are met based on available information. Because core article content (methods/results/discussion) is missing, I exclude pending full-text availability.

This is an event-related task-based fMRI study of verbal working memory (phonological rehearsal), which falls within the executive function domain (working memory). The paper reports single-subject and group-level voxelwise GLM analyses contrasting delay-period activity (L6 vs L1) and describes whole-brain group results (voxelwise), satisfying the requirement for a within-group task contrast and whole-brain task-evoked maps. Participants are healthy adults. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article appears complete for screening.

Although the study tested participants in an fMRI scanner, the article reports behavioral performance results (working memory and long-term memory) and does not present any task-evoked neuroimaging analyses, group-level voxelwise statistical maps, or within-group task activation contrasts. Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria requiring a task-based fMRI/PET activation study with whole-brain voxelwise results (I5, I7) and a within-group task contrast (I8). The paper does meet that the tasks fall within an executive function domain (working memory; I6) and that it includes participant groups (young and elderly; I9). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The article reports an empirical fMRI study using a stop-signal task (inhibition — an executive function), with whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses and within-group contrasts (successful vs failed stop trials) reported in tables/figures and text. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text, and the study provides coordinates and group-level SPM results. Thus it satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E6). Full text appears complete.

This is a Nature Protocols methods paper describing the emotional counting Stroop task and how to implement it in fMRI; it does not present original empirical task-activation results or report group-level voxelwise statistical maps or within-group task contrasts. Therefore it is non-empirical/methods-only and does not provide the required whole-brain task activation analyses. Exclusion ID met: E6 (non-empirical/methods-only without original human neuroimaging data). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (task falls within executive function domains—Stroop-style inhibition/cognitive control). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no original fMRI/PET study reporting task activations), I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise results reported), I8 (no within-group task contrast reported). Full text appears complete for a protocol paper (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an fMRI task study of cognitive control (meets I5, I6) with within-group task contrasts reported and a healthy participant sample (meets I8 and I9). However, the imaging analyses reported are restricted to a priori ROI analyses (ACC and lPFC) rather than group-level, voxelwise whole-brain activation maps. The paper does not report voxelwise, whole-brain group analyses or coordinate tables for such maps, so it fails I7 and therefore meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses with no voxelwise results). Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study using the color–word Stroop task (an inhibition/cognitive control/executive function paradigm) with within-group Stroop vs baseline contrasts. Group-level voxelwise statistical maps and Talairach-coordinate tables are reported; although slice coverage was limited, analyses were voxelwise and group-averaged label- and activation-maps are presented. Results include coordinates and figures of whole-brain (partial coverage) activation maps. All required inclusion criteria are satisfied (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: it is a task-based fMRI study of executive function (visuospatial working memory n-back) (I5, I6), reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with corrected coordinates (I7, I10), and includes within-group task contrasts (2-Back minus Match-to-Centre; random-effects analyses) (I8). Participant group (young adults) is acceptable per I9. The full text contains introduction, methods, results and discussion (fulltext_complete). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met: the paper includes whole-brain voxelwise activation results (not ROI-only), is not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and reports within-group contrasts rather than only between-group comparisons. Therefore INCLUDE.

This study reports task-based BOLD fMRI of a working memory task (an executive function domain). Methods describe voxelwise individual and group-level statistical parametric mapping (stimulus vs rest contrasts), whole-brain coverage (18 axial slices stated to encompass whole brain), group-average activation maps and thresholded voxelwise group analyses reported in tables and figures for each group. Therefore it provides within-group task contrasts and whole-brain voxelwise results for clinical groups (AD, MCI, controls). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical).

This is an empirical fMRI study of verbal working memory (n-back tasks), which is an established executive function domain. The paper reports within-group task contrasts (0-,1-,2-back; 1+2-back vs baseline; 2-back vs 1-back) using voxelwise, whole-brain random-effects analyses (SPM99), with cluster- and voxel-level inference and tables/figures of activation coordinates. Sample: 30 healthy adults.
