Therefore it satisfies I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (working memory), I7 (voxelwise whole-brain analyses), I8 (within-group contrasts), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (results reported in maps/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (2-back), an established executive function domain. It reports within-group, voxelwise GLM analyses at the group level (N=18), using whole-brain gradient-echo EPI (group one-sample t-tests and ANOVA), with activation maps described and shown. The contrast is task vs rest/implicit baseline (2-back vs rest), meeting the within-group task-evoked map requirement. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using the Tower of London planning task (an executive function: planning). It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM99 random-effects models, cluster-level correction) and within-group task contrasts (e.g., six- vs four-move planning/execution; correct vs incorrect trials). Results include coordinates and tables/figures. Participants are a healthy student sample (within-group contrasts reported). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

The study is an event-related fMRI empirical investigation of planning (an executive function domain) using a task-based paradigm (Grid of Pittsburgh/Tower of Hanoi adaptation), satisfying I5 and I6. Analyses include group-level voxelwise tests of an ACT-R-derived task regressor (coefficient B2) and spatial t maps with coordinates and tables, meeting I7 and I10 (partial slice coverage reported but voxelwise group analysis performed). The reported group-level voxelwise contrasts correspond to within-group task effects (parametric modulation of planning load), satisfying I8. Participant sample is an adult within-group cohort (I9). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and this is original empirical neuroimaging data. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures). Therefore include.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that investigates response inhibition using somatosensory go/nogo tasks (executive function domain: inhibition). The paper reports voxelwise, group-level random-effects analyses (SPM2) with whole-brain normalization, thresholding, and tables of activated coordinates for within-group contrasts (Movement Nogo vs baseline; Count Nogo vs baseline), satisfying requirements for task-evoked statistical maps. Results are presented in text, figures, and tables and the full article includes methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (visual object and spatial delayed-recognition tasks), meeting the executive-function domain. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise GLM analyses and spatially normalized group-average statistical maps (e.g., Delaylocation/no secondary task – baseline; Delayobject/no secondary task – baseline), and presents within-group task contrasts and group-level results (figures, tables, and coordinates). Participants are healthy adults and within-group contrasts are reported. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I10 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This paper reports an empirical fMRI study using an n-back working memory task (executive function domain) with voxelwise, group-level SPM2 analyses. The methods describe whole-brain preprocessing and random-effects group analyses; a conjunction of within-group contrasts ([3-back – 1-back] and [1-back – rest]) identified load-sensitive regions and results are reported in text, figures, and tables. Thus it provides within-group task contrasts, whole-brain voxelwise results (reported threshold and clusters), and qualifies across participant groups (young high/low and older adults). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the record is complete for screening. No exclusion criteria (only ROI, only connectivity, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) are met.

Full text provided is incomplete (only title/metadata/redirect notice). From the title and metadata, the study appears to be an fMRI task examining semantic and phonological maintenance (likely working memory), so I5 (fMRI task) and I6 (working memory domain) appear satisfied. However, the methods and results are not available to confirm critical inclusion criteria: I7 (presence of group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses), I8 (at least one within-group task contrast), and I10 (reporting of whole-brain results). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are identifiable from the available content. Because key inclusion criteria cannot be verified from the incomplete full text, the study is excluded pending access to the full article for verification.

This is an fMRI study with group-level, voxelwise within-group contrasts (semantic task vs control) and reports whole-brain results. However, the experimental paradigm is a lexico-semantic association/decision task, not an explicit executive function/cognitive control task. Although the authors discuss possible working memory demands, the task was not designed to probe established executive domains (working memory was neither manipulated nor the primary target). Therefore the study does not meet I5 (task assesses executive function/cognitive control) and I6 (task falls within established EF domains). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analysis), I8 (within-group task contrast), I9 (participant group acceptable), I10 (whole-brain results clearly reported). No exclusion criteria are triggered (E3–E6 not applicable). Full text appears complete. Exclusion summary: excluded because I5 and I6 are not satisfied; other inclusion criteria (I7,I8,I9,I10) are satisfied.

This is an event-related fMRI study using a Stroop task (executive function: inhibition/cognitive control) with voxelwise, group-level random effects analyses reported (thresholded maps, cluster extent) and multiple within-group task contrasts (oddball vs baseline neutral; incongruent vs neutral; eligible vs ineligible). Partial slice coverage (10 slices) is present but the analyses are voxelwise at the group level, which qualifies under I7. Whole-text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Behavioral and imaging results are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

Exclusion E3 applies: the study reports ROI-based percentage signal change analyses and VOI/ROI statistics rather than a group-level voxelwise whole-brain task activation map or coordinate table. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI assessing executive function/working memory), I6 (working memory n-back task falls within executive function domain), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported, e.g., 1-back vs 3-back, single vs dual), I9 (within-group healthy adult sample reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no evidence of a group-level voxelwise whole-brain statistical map; analysis was confined to anatomically-defined ROIs/VOIs), I10 (no voxelwise whole-brain results reported as coordinates/figures/tables that would qualify). Full text appears complete. Because E3 is met, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis per the criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using task-based antisaccade (inhibition) and ocular motor delayed response (working memory) paradigms that clearly probe executive function. The paper reports a voxelwise, group-level one-sample t test (whole-brain clustered map) comparing volitional saccade blocks vs fixation (task-evoked activation map), and reports within-group task effects (regions showing increased BOLD during volitional saccades) as well as group comparisons. Tasks fall within established executive domains (inhibition, working memory). Whole-brain voxelwise analyses and voxelwise thresholding/cluster correction are described. A within-group task contrast (task vs fixation) is reported (main effect of task), and clinical and healthy groups are included. The full text (background, methods, results, figures, discussion) is present. Therefore all required inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an event-related fMRI study of task switching (executive function: cognitive flexibility) that reports group-level, voxelwise random-effects statistical maps (switch vs stay contrasts) with coordinates and thresholding; it also includes within-group task contrasts (switch>stay) for healthy participants. Partial slice coverage (20 slices) was used but voxelwise whole-brain analyses were performed and reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function) using an event-related paradigm with distractors. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise SPM analyses and a random-effects group-level contrast (memory-delay correct trials in distractor-plus vs control), with thresholding and activation coordinates reported. At least one within-group task contrast is presented; participants are healthy adults. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, not a review). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and the study is eligible for inclusion.

This article reports an empirical task-based fMRI study of planning (Tower of London), an executive function, with both within-group (TOL vs fixation) and group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM99). The methods describe whole-brain preprocessing and group random-effects contrasts, and results include within-group activation maps, tables of coordinates, and figures. Partial slice coverage was used but voxelwise analyses were performed (acceptable per protocol). Thus it satisfies all inclusion criteria for task-based fMRI executive function studies (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and within-group contrasts are reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of cognitive control (cognitive reappraisal) using a task-based paradigm. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level SPM analyses (thresholded, coordinates in tables/figures) and within-group task contrasts (increase>look; decrease>look), with adult participants. Results include whole-brain activations and small-volume amygdala analyses but are not limited to ROIs. Therefore it satisfies I5 (fMRI cognitive control task), I6 (task involves cognitive control/executive processes such as interference resolution/inhibition/working-memory-like processes), I7 (voxelwise whole-brain group maps reported), I8 (within-group contrasts reported), I9 (participants reported), and I10 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study of deception that engages cognitive control/inhibitory processes. The paper reports within-group voxelwise whole-brain random-effects SPM analyses (contrasts: lie>truth, lie>control, etc.) across 14 healthy adults, with coordinates and thresholding described and results reported in text/figures. Thus it satisfies I5 (task-based fMRI of cognitive control), I6 (task involves inhibition/cognitive control), I7 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain analysis), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (whole-brain results reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI task study of picture–word (lexical) interference and language production, not an executive-function task. While the study includes whole-brain, voxelwise, within-group contrasts and reports results in tables/figures, the experimental task does not fall within established executive function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criteria I5 and I6. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analyses), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (participant group reported), I10 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (does not assess executive function/cognitive-control as primary task), I6 (task is language/lexical processing, not an EF domain). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study directly addressing cognitive control/executive function (temporal integration, sustained maintenance, strategy representation). It uses whole-brain, voxelwise GLM analyses (state/item mixed design) with group-level random-effects tests and reports clusters/coordinates; within-group task contrasts are reported (task vs fixation; W2 vs W12; WIN×DYN interactions). Participants are healthy adults. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical simultaneous EEG–fMRI study using a task-based mental arithmetic paradigm that probes central executive processes (working memory, manipulation, sequencing). The paper reports voxelwise group-level fMRI analyses (SPM99 preprocessing, one-sample t-tests across n=8, whole-brain normalization and smoothing) and presents task contrasts (arithmetic vs rest) and phase-synchronization–related regressors producing statistical maps and tables of activated/deactivated regions. Thus it provides within-group task contrasts and whole-brain voxelwise results relevant to executive function activations. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, allowing assessment against inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical).

This is an empirical fMRI study of task-switching (cognitive flexibility), reporting within-group task contrasts (switch vs repeat) and group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (group t-tests on normalized beta-maps) that identify a left superior parietal region. The paper contains complete methods, results, and discussion enabling extraction of task-evoked activation loci. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function fMRI studies and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study using a verbal working memory (n-back/2-back style) paradigm in schizophrenia and healthy controls. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. It reports voxelwise, whole-brain analyses (FPQ maps, generic brain activation maps, voxelwise ANOVA and permutation testing) and presents within-group task contrasts (activation vs baseline) for each group, with regional coordinates and figures/tables. Thus it satisfies I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (working memory = executive function), I7 (voxelwise whole-brain analyses, partial coverage is acceptable), I8 (within-group task contrast reported), I9 (participant groups acceptable), and I10 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables/text). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical whole-brain fMRI study using a task-based oddball paradigm that probes attentional control and working-memory updating (executive domains: vigilance/working memory). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise one-sample t-test analyses (familywise error corrected) and within-group task contrasts (targets and novels vs implicit baseline) as well as parametric modulation by target/novel interval. Participants are a within-group sample of healthy adults. Results are reported as whole-brain statistical maps and peak coordinates. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of phonological working memory (an executive function domain). It reports within-group, voxelwise, group-level contrasts (WM vs control) using SPM2 random-effects whole-head analyses, with results described in tables and figures (stimulus-encoding, maintenance, comparison phases). Participants are healthy adults. The paper includes full methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Full text is incomplete (API error message provided), so core article content (methods/results) cannot be verified. From title/metadata, this appears to be an fMRI working-memory task study, satisfying inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI/PET assessing executive function) and I6 (task is working memory). However, I cannot confirm required criteria: I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group-level statistical maps), I8 (a within-group task contrast reported), I9 (within-group contrast present for at least one participant group), or I10 (reporting of whole-brain results in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are demonstrably met from the available information (E3–E6 not confirmed). Because the full text is missing and critical inclusion criteria cannot be verified, the study is excluded pending access to the complete article.

The study reports a task-based fMRI investigation of working memory (an established executive function domain). It provides within-group, voxelwise group-level contrasts (memory vs control; manipulable vs non-manipulable) and reports whole-brain results with coordinates and figures. Although functional acquisition used limited axial slices, I7 allows partial-brain acquisition so long as voxelwise analyses are reported — which they are (random-effects, Talairach-transformed z-maps, cluster criteria). All required inclusions are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so appears complete.

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study that directly assesses working memory (an established executive-function domain) and episodic memory using task-based paradigms. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise random-effects analyses and mapwise thresholds across the whole brain (with stereotactic coordinates and conjunction analyses), and presents within-group task contrasts (encoding, delay, recognition phases vs. ITI/baseline). Participant group (healthy adults) is included and qualifying. Results are reported as whole-brain maps and coordinate tables. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 and is appropriate for inclusion in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an event-related and blocked-design fMRI study that explicitly investigates executive functions (attention-switching and response inhibition) using task-based paradigms. The paper reports within-group, voxelwise, random-effects whole-brain analyses (switch−nonswitch; incompatible−compatible; High-Switch−Low-Switch) with FDR correction and provides peak coordinates/tables and figures. Participants are a human within-group sample (undergraduates). Results are reported at the group level and voxelwise and thus meet the meta-analysis requirements. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This is a task-based fMRI study of task-switching and endogenous control (executive function: cognitive flexibility/working memory). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain random-effects contrasts (e.g., transition cue vs task cue) with Z-maps, cluster thresholds, and tables of coordinates; within-group task contrasts and main effects are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This fMRI study used a task-based, within-group word-retrieval (verbal fluency/word generation) paradigm that engages executive processes (initiation, search, sustained attention/working memory). The paper reports whole-brain, random-effects, voxelwise group analyses (task vs baseline and difficulty contrasts) with coordinates and figures, meeting requirements for group-level voxelwise maps. Participants are a defined within-group (healthy adults). Results and methods are fully reported (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so full text appears complete. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria for executive-function-related activation (initiation/attention), whole-brain voxelwise analyses, and within-group contrasts.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that probes top-down attentional control and deliberate shifts of attentional set between feature dimensions. The paradigm directly assesses cognitive control/set-shifting (cognitive flexibility), an established executive-function domain. The study reports within-group, voxelwise, group-level contrasts (e.g., shift vs hold) analyzed with a random-effects GLM across whole-brain volumes and provides Talairach coordinates and figures of activations. Participants are healthy adults and the paper includes full methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not a non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

The study is an empirical PET (15O-water) task-based activation study using the N-back verbal working memory task in healthy volunteers and reports activation maps across working-memory load. Based on the abstract, it meets inclusion criteria: I5 (PET task-based study), I6 (working memory in established executive domain), I8 (within-group task contrast / parametric N-back effects), I9 (participant group reported), and I10 (whole-brain results reported as activation maps). I7 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain evidence) appears to be met because the abstract refers to activation maps from ECAT HR+ across volunteers, but the full text is not provided here to unequivocally confirm voxelwise group-level statistics. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) appear to apply. Because only the abstract/metadata are available, fulltext_incomplete is set to true and confidence is moderate.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that reports group-level, voxelwise activation maps and within-group contrasts relevant to executive function. The working memory (W) task clearly falls within the executive function domain (working memory). The paper reports whole-brain acquisition and group statistical parametric maps (SPM t/Z maps) with voxelwise thresholding and presents within-group contrasts (W–C, T–C, T–W). Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using a Go/NoGo inhibition task (executive function: inhibition). It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses and multiple within-group task contrasts (false alarms–hits; correct rejections–hits; false alarms–correct rejections). Results are presented as voxelwise contrasts and interrogated with small-volume corrections but whole-brain voxelwise analyses are explicitly described, satisfying reporting via tables/figures/text. The methods, results, and discussion are present in full text. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This FDG-PET study uses a Stroop task (executive/inhibition domain) in schizophrenia patients and controls, but its analyses are ROI-based from limited slice sampling and do not report any group-level voxelwise task-evoked (within-group) activation maps or contrasts. Therefore it fails the whole-brain / voxelwise requirement and within-group task-contrast requirement. Exclusion ID met: E3 (only ROI analyses / no voxelwise results). Inclusion IDs met: I5 (PET task-based study), I6 (Stroop = inhibition/executive function), I9 (clinical participant groups reported). Inclusion IDs NOT met: I7 (no group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical map / whole-brain evidence), I8 (no within-group task contrast reported). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of cognitive control/attentional control over threat-related distractors (executive function domain). It reports group-level, voxelwise random-effects analyses (voxel-wise comparisons with whole-brain correction and ROI small-volume corrections) and provides coordinates for activations. Key reported contrasts are within-group task contrasts (threat-related vs neutral distractor trials; start trials vs others) and regressions against state anxiety. Participants are healthy adults. Thus all inclusion criteria are met (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria apply: the study does not report only ROI/SVC results (whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported), is not solely connectivity/resting analyses, includes within-group contrasts (not only between-group), and is empirical data (not a review). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of cognitive control (task-switching/cognitive flexibility) with healthy adult participants. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (e.g., bivalent > univalent; switch > repetition) with thresholding and coordinates, and within-group contrasts are explicitly presented. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical PET study using a task-based Stroop paradigm (inhibition/cognitive control), reporting voxelwise, whole-brain group-level activation maps (incongruent vs congruent) for both patients and controls, and within-group contrasts. The methods explicitly describe voxel-by-voxel t-tests, voxelwise multiple regression, Talairach normalization, and tables/figures of activations. Thus it satisfies all inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function activations (I5–I10). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

Although this is an empirical, whole-brain fMRI study with within-group voxelwise contrasts (MI vs LI) in healthy adults and reports results in-text and figures, the primary task is visual object categorization manipulated by stimulus impoverishment. While the authors interpret activations as reflecting top-down control and implicate working memory and attention, the fMRI task itself does not directly implement or manipulate a canonical executive-function domain listed in the inclusion criteria (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). The explicit working-memory manipulation was behavioral (Experiment 2) and not a whole-brain fMRI task contrast. Therefore I6 (task within established executive function domains) is not satisfied, so the study does not meet all inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis.

This study reports task-based fMRI of executive function (2-back working memory) with clinical groups, employing voxelwise whole-brain analyses (voxelwise t-tests/ANOVAs) and reporting within-group task>fixation contrasts for each group. The paper provides complete methods, results, and discussion, and clearly describes clusterwise thresholding and voxelwise maps. All required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met (fMRI executive task; working memory domain; voxelwise whole-brain analyses; within-group task contrasts reported; clinical participant groups included; results described in text/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not solely between-group contrasts, and is empirical).

(a) Exclusion IDs met: none. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (voxelwise whole-brain analyses reported), I8 (within-group task contrast: decision > no-decision and group-average one-sample t-test), I9 (participant groups include clinical samples), I10 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I6 — task domain. The task is a modified Iowa Gambling Task probing decision-making and reward processing; the review requires tasks to fall within explicit executive-function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Although IGT involves aspects of decision-making and may engage executive processes, it is primarily a reward-based decision-making paradigm and is not clearly within the listed EF domains. Therefore it does not meet I6 and must be excluded. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an event-related fMRI study that directly investigates response inhibition, an executive function (inhibition). Methods report whole-brain acquisition (contiguous slices covering entire brain) and voxelwise group analyses (one-sample t tests across 14 subjects) time-locked to lure (No-Go) events, constituting a within-group task contrast. Results are reported with cluster maps, figures, and Talairach coordinates (Table 1 and figures). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10.

This paper reports an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (object working memory) with healthy adult participants. The authors performed group-level, voxelwise whole-brain random-effects analyses (SPM99), reporting within-group task contrasts (high vs low memory load; high vs low reward; interactions) with coordinates, tables and figures. The methods, results, and discussion are present in full. Therefore it satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion requirements for fMRI task-based executive function, working memory domain, whole-brain voxelwise results, within-group contrasts, and permissible participant groups. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of spatial working memory (an executive function) with event-related design. The paper reports voxelwise whole-brain GLM analyses (FDR-corrected), activation maps and Talairach coordinates, and explicit within-group task contrasts (delay-related maintenance activity examined within patients and controls, and correct vs. error trials). Participant groups include clinical (schizophrenia) and control samples. All required core sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) are present, so the full text is complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5–I10 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This fMRI study reports task-evoked whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses for cognitive tasks relevant to executive function. The Paced Auditory Serial Addition Test (PASAT) probes sustained attention, information processing speed, and working memory (an established executive domain); the study also included a recall (memory retrieval) task. The paper reports within-group one-sample SPM99 contrasts for patients and controls, between-group two-sample contrasts, multiple regression correlations with lesion load, and tables/figures of coordinate results — satisfying whole-brain voxelwise reporting. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not non-empirical, and includes within-group task contrasts). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function domain). It reports within-group voxelwise contrasts (e.g., [Delay Forward 5 − Delay Forward 2] and [Delay Forward 5 − baseline]) and conducts a group-level SNGA second-level GLM (voxelwise whole-brain maps), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion, and reports voxelwise group maps and coordinates. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of task activations in executive function.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of an executive function (working memory n-back). It reports within-group voxelwise contrasts (0-back vs fixation; 2-back vs 0-back) and group-level random-effects SPM analyses with whole-brain voxelwise results (tables, figures, cluster-corrected thresholds). The task falls within the executive domain (working memory). Results are presented as within-group and between-group voxelwise activation maps and coordinate tables. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion, refs) is present. Therefore it satisfies I5–I10 and should be included.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of visual working memory (an executive function domain). It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (group SDM and t-statistic maps), within-group task vs control contrasts, and presents maps and a table of local maxima. Participants are a within-group sample of 20 healthy adults. These satisfy inclusion criteria I5–I10. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, figures/tables and references).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (N-back and item-recognition), which falls squarely within executive function domains. The paper reports group-level voxelwise analyses (spatial F-maps, voxelwise ANOVAs) and within-group task contrasts (e.g., high vs low load; verbal vs nonverbal). Results include whole-brain voxelwise findings and coordinates reported in the text/tables. Participant group is healthy adults and within-group contrasts are provided. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study of an antisaccade task (inhibition), which is an established executive function (inhibition). The paper reports voxelwise, group-level mixed-effects statistical parametric maps contrasting antisaccade vs prosaccade (within-group contrasts), includes tables of Talairach coordinates and figures of maps/time courses, and uses whole-voxel GLM/deconvolution rather than ROI-only analyses. Although imaging used limited axial slice coverage, the protocol and analyses are voxelwise and partial-brain acquisition is acceptable per criteria. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing verification of criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of visual working memory (an executive function domain) using task-based maintenance vs manipulation contrasts. The authors report group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise GLM analyses (what vs where; maintenance vs manipulation), thresholded with FDR, with coordinates and figures/tables of activation. Within-group task contrasts are provided (e.g., maintenance vs manipulation, color vs spatial) for the healthy adult sample. Thus the study meets I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function), I6 (working memory), I7 (voxelwise whole-brain group analyses — partial 16-slice coverage but voxelwise maps reported), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (within-group results in a participant group), and I10 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that directly examines short-term storage and comparison of auditory durations—a working memory operation within executive function. The paper reports a within-group contrast (discrimination minus identification) analyzed at the group level using voxelwise SPM99 procedures with whole-brain coverage, and presents voxel coordinates and activation figures/clusters. Participants are healthy adults (acceptable). Results and methods (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are present in the full text provided. None of the exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for inclusion in the meta-analysis of executive function activations.

This is an empirical, task-based event-related fMRI study of cognitive control (Preparing to Overcome Prepotency task) in healthy adults. The paper reports group-level task-related activation effects in the locus coeruleus and prefrontal cortex with figures and tables (including supplementary tables), indicating voxelwise, whole-brain (or partial-brain with voxelwise analysis) results. Within-group task contrasts and main effects of task are reported, and results are presented as cluster maps/tables. Core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present in the provided text. Therefore all inclusion criteria for task-based whole-brain fMRI executive-function activations are satisfied, and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that directly reports voxelwise, whole-brain group-level activation analyses across tasks. It includes a working memory task (an established executive function domain), a visual attention (vigilance) task, and an episodic retrieval task. The manuscript describes SPM99 whole-brain preprocessing and group-level contrasts (within-group activations vs implicit baseline and task contrasts), reports coordinates in tables and figures, and presents behavioral and imaging results. Participants include healthy younger and older adult groups (acceptable per I9). The study is not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and it reports within-group task contrasts rather than only between-group contrasts. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of verbal working memory (manipulation and maintenance), which falls squarely within executive function domains. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise task-evoked analyses using SPM96 (random-effects/general linear model) with contrasts comparing within-group conditions (lag-1 digit span vs digit span; digit span vs simple number detection) and a conjunction. Although slice coverage was limited (15 coronal slices), analyses were voxelwise (partial-brain acquisition is allowed). Results are reported in tables and figures with coordinates. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met.

This article reports a task-based fMRI study (Multi-Source Interference Task) probing cognitive control/executive function in both healthy and opiate-dependent participants. It includes whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (within-group I>C contrasts reported for controls and opiate users, with cluster-wise correction and figures/tables) and reports metabolite and behaviour associations. All core sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are present, so the full text appears complete. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria for fMRI task activation meta-analysis of executive function.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (an established executive function domain). The paper reports voxelwise multiple-regression Z-score maps, Talairach-normalized group results, and coordinates from whole-brain coverage. It includes within-group task contrasts (e.g., sustained memory-delay vs control delays) and reports group-level voxelwise activation loci. Participants are a within-group healthy adult sample. Results are reported as coordinates/figures and described in text. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion and appears complete.

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study employing a picture-word (Stroop-like) paradigm that probes semantic interference and the resolution of distractor-related competition via attention/inhibitory control. The task therefore indexes cognitive control/inhibition (an executive function domain). The paper reports a within-group voxelwise contrast (semantically-related distractor vs lexical control) analyzed with SPM99, whole-brain correction and volume-of-interest corrections, and reports coordinates of differential activations (Table II, figures). Participants are healthy adults. Thus it satisfies I5 (task-based fMRI of cognitive control), I6 (inhibition/attentional control domain), I7 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses with reported coordinates), I8 (within-group task contrast), I9 (acceptable participant group), and I10 (coordinates reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI task-based study using the n-back working memory paradigm (an established executive function domain). It reports group-level, voxelwise SPM analyses (thresholded, whole-brain maps, inclusive/exclusive masking) and within-group contrasts (1-/2-/3-back vs 0-back; rewarded vs nonrewarded). Acquisition covered contiguous axial slices and results are described in methods, results, tables and figures. Therefore it meets I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (working memory), I7 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain analysis), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (whole-brain results clearly reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that directly examines cognitive control during a gambling/decision-making task manipulating uncertainty. It meets inclusion criteria as follows: I5 – uses task-based fMRI to assess cognitive control/executive function (decision uncertainty, resource allocation); I6 – the task probes cognitive control/conflict and decision processes (authors frame it as control-related and compare conditions of differing control demands); I7 – whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses and exploratory whole-brain contrasts are reported (maps/voxelwise contrasts and figures described); I8 – within-group task contrasts are reported (e.g., uncertain wins vs probable wins, probable wins vs probable losses, all trials vs fixation); I9 – reports within-group results for a healthy adult sample (acceptable participant group); I10 – whole-brain results are presented in figures and described in text (coordinates available). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study using a parametric verbal working memory task (executive function domain) with whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (SPM2). The paper reports within-group task contrasts (load vs control) for healthy controls and patient groups, and provides voxel coordinates/tables and figures of whole-brain results. Thus it meets all required inclusion criteria for task-based fMRI of executive function with within-group voxelwise maps and reports whole-brain results. The full text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, Tables, References) is provided, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based working memory paradigm (delayed-recognition), testing reward modulation of top-down control. It reports within-group, voxelwise, group-level task activation maps (encoding/main effect of task reported at FDR p<0.05) and provides whole/near-whole-brain coverage (voxelwise GLM and group analyses coregistered to MNI). The task falls within the executive function domain (working memory). Therefore it satisfies all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (I5–I10). Full text is complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of visual working memory (an executive function domain). It reports group-level, voxelwise statistical analyses (cortex-based GLM), projected statistical maps and Talairach coordinates, and within-group task contrasts (load predictors and contrasts versus baseline), meeting whole-brain/partial-brain voxelwise reporting. Participants are a within-group healthy adult sample. Results and methods (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are present, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a 2-back working memory task (an established executive-function domain). The paper reports group- and within-group voxelwise SPM analyses (WM vs control CPT-X), with whole-brain thresholding and reported significant activations (p<0.05 corrected across the brain) as well as tables/figures of coordinate results. Clinical sample (schizophrenia) is acceptable. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the review are met (I5–I10). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, Tables, and References). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive function (working memory manipulation) that reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation contrasts. The paper tests segmenting and binding operations with a 2×2 factorial design and reports within-group contrasts (e.g., ACROSS > WITHIN; 2ST-ACROSS − SUP-ACROSS interaction), thresholded with FDR/FWE and presented with coordinate tables and figures. Participants are a within-group healthy adult sample. The methods, results, and discussion are present in the supplied full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so the full text appears complete for screening. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10; no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a working memory (N-back) task (executive function domain). It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (voxelwise regression, cluster-level permutation tests) and presents within-group task contrasts (task vs baseline; load and repetition parametric contrasts), with results in figures/tables. Partial slice coverage (21 near-axial slices) is present but the analysis is voxelwise and thus meets I7 per criteria. Participants are healthy adults (I9). Whole-brain results are reported in tables and figures (I10). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study that probes voluntary inhibition of the micturition reflex via an experimental pelvic-floor contraction paradigm (full vs empty bladder) and reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain activation maps (with coordinates and cluster statistics). The task targets inhibition (an established executive-function domain), includes within-group contrasts (FBC > EBC), reports voxelwise group analyses and coordinates, and uses healthy participants. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an event-related fMRI study using a delayed-response working memory task (executive function). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise random-effects analyses and within-group task contrasts (e.g., face > scrambled face; emotional > neutral), with tables/figures listing activation peaks. It therefore meets all inclusion criteria for an executive-function task activation meta-analysis and does not violate any exclusion criteria. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present and complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive processes (verbal response initiation and suppression), reporting group-level, voxelwise activation maps and within-group contrasts (response initiation vs control; response suppression vs control; suppression vs initiation). Although slice coverage was partial (14 non-contiguous planes), analyses were voxelwise and group GBAM results with coordinates are reported in tables/figures. Participants are healthy adults. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion included).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of spatial working memory (an executive function domain). It reports group-level, voxelwise activation maps (whole-brain composite maps and Talairach-transformed group maps), ROI analyses, and time courses; includes within-group contrasts (No-HF vs No-LF, nonmatch vs match) and reports coordinates/figures. Participants are a within-group healthy adult sample. All required inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10) are met; no exclusion criteria apply. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references and appears complete.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). Based on the abstract, the study is an event-related BOLD fMRI task-switching investigation addressing attentional control (meets I5 and I6) and reports condition comparisons consistent with within-group task contrasts (meets I8). However, the available content does not allow verification of critical inclusion criterion I7 (that at least one group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked analysis/map is reported); it is unclear whether results are from whole-brain voxelwise analyses versus ROI-only analyses, and I10 (format/location of whole-brain results) cannot be confirmed. No exclusion criteria are clearly met from the abstract alone, but because not all required inclusion criteria can be confirmed from the incomplete full text, the study is excluded pending full-text availability.

This paper reports original task-based fMRI data using well-established executive function paradigms (n-back working memory and the Iowa Gambling Task). It includes within-group contrasts (1/2/3-back vs 0-back; gambling vs control) and reports group-level voxelwise analyses using SPM99 with whole-brain statistical mapping and corrected thresholds. The n-back clearly falls within the executive domain (working memory), satisfying task-domain requirements; the IGT provides additional decision-making-related activation. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (acquisition and voxelwise analysis), Results (within-group activation maps and parametric analysis), and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) are met.

Full text content appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). Abstract indicates a PET task-based Stroop study, so I5 (PET/fMRI task-based) and I6 (executive function – inhibition/Stroop) are met, and the paper reports within-group contrasts (Stroop vs control), so I8 is met. However, I cannot verify I7 (presence of group-level voxelwise whole-brain statistical maps) or I10 (reporting of whole-brain results/coordinates) because methods, results, and figures/tables are not available in the provided content. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are clearly triggered from the abstract. Because critical information (voxelwise whole-brain analyses and reporting format) cannot be confirmed from the incomplete full text, the study is excluded pending provision of the complete article.

The study is an fMRI working-memory task and reports within-group contrasts (correct vs incorrect), but it reports ROI-based parameter estimates rather than group-level voxelwise whole-brain statistical maps. Exclusion met: E3 (only ROI analyses with no voxelwise results). Inclusion met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (working memory falls within executive domains), I8 (within-group task contrast reported), I9 (healthy adult participant group). Inclusion not met: I7 (no group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked statistical map), I10 (no whole-brain results reported as coordinates/figures/tables). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of cognitive control/executive function (inhibition/response suppression, preparatory control) using delayed discrimination tasks with high- and low-control conditions and incentive manipulations. Group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported (mixed-effects ANOVA, cluster correction, timeseries, coordinates/ROIs reported and supplementary data referenced). Within-group task contrasts (HC vs LC, Incentive vs No-Reward/Reward/Penalty, preparatory interval contrasts) are explicitly described. Participant sample (healthy adults) is reported. Reporting of voxelwise results and coordinates, and full methods, results, and discussion are present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10 and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study reporting group-level, voxelwise SPM2 analyses (whole-brain and ROI) with within-group contrasts (task > rest; uncertainty > certainty). The paradigm manipulates selective vs divided attention with explicit working-memory/attentional control demands (implicit standard, monitoring, and response selection), fitting established executive domains (working memory/cognitive control). Participants are healthy adults and results are reported as whole-brain contrasts in text/figures. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function domain) using an event-related parametric paradigm. The paper reports within-group, voxelwise second-level analyses (e.g., L1>Control, L2>L1, L3>L2) with voxel-level thresholds and cluster correction, whole-brain normalization and coordinates in tables and figures. Results include group-level statistical maps and Talairach/MNI coordinates, satisfying whole-brain reporting. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met and no exclusion criteria apply. The provided full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion and References, so the full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI, task-based empirical study of hypothesis generation that the authors link to working memory and higher-order inferential processes (meets I5 and I6). The paper reports whole-brain, random-effects voxelwise analyses with tables of Talairach coordinates and surface maps (meets I7 and I10). Within-group task contrasts are reported (hypothesis generation vs baseline; and pre- vs post-training within the trained group), satisfying I8. Participants are healthy undergraduates (acceptable per I9). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical).

This study reports task-based fMRI of an executive function (PASAT; working memory) in MS patients and controls. Methods describe voxelwise whole-brain preprocessing and GLM analyses, with group-level random-effects and within-group one-sample t tests for task activation (P<0.005, cluster threshold), and between-group two-sample contrasts. Results present whole-brain activation tables with Talairach coordinates and figures. Neuropsychological and task performance data are provided. The paper therefore meets all required inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and does not meet any exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical study; within-group contrasts are reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that probes decision-making under uncertainty and explicitly examines working-memory and related executive processes. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise random-effects analyses (z-maps, thresholded and reported with Talairach coordinates and tables/figures) including within-group contrasts (uncertain prediction conditions vs control; parametric uncertainty regressors). Tasks fall within the executive domain (working memory/mnemonic search) and participants are a healthy adult group. Whole-brain voxelwise results are presented in tables and figures. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; thus full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based paradigm that manipulates working-memory/task difficulty in a visuospatial paired-associate task (executive function domain: working memory). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM random-effects one-sample and two-sample t-tests), thresholded maps and tables of coordinates, and within-group task contrasts (e.g., RET6 vs RET3, parametric load regressors, zero/first/second-order contrasts). Participant groups are healthy young and older adults (within-group contrasts reported). Results are presented in tables, figures and text. Full article includes introduction, methods, results, discussion and references. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply.

The study reports task-based fMRI of a spatial working memory task (meets I5, I6). The abstract states that statistical maps from 5–8 subjects per site were made available, aligned in stereotactic space, and common regions of activation were examined, indicating group-level voxelwise task-evoked maps (I7) and reporting within-group task activations (main effect of task vs baseline) (I8). Participants are healthy adults, which is acceptable (I9). Results are reported as statistical maps and described in the text (I10). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Note: only the abstract/metadata are provided here rather than the full article (methods/results/discussion are not present), so fulltext_incomplete is set to true; this reduces certainty that all methodological details fully satisfy inclusion criteria, hence confidence=0.75.

This is an event-related fMRI study of working memory (executive function) in schizophrenia and healthy controls, using a Sternberg task (encoding, maintenance/manipulation, retrieval). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group- and within-group analyses (SPM2 preprocessing, random-effects second-level analyses), including within-group task contrasts (correct retrieval vs baseline) and between-group contrasts; results and coordinates are described. It therefore satisfies: task-based fMRI assessing executive function (I5), task within executive domains (working memory) (I6), whole-brain voxelwise analyses (I7), within-group task contrasts reported (I8), includes clinical and healthy participant groups (I9), and reports whole-brain results in text/tables (I10). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical study). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based fMRI study of executive function (working memory manipulation) using a modified Sternberg paradigm. The full text reports voxelwise, whole-brain group-level analyses (one-sample t-tests and ANOVAs) and provides coordinates/tables and figures for within-group contrasts (encoding vs baseline; alphabetize vs forward) and between-group contrasts. Analyses were performed with SPM2 across the whole brain with familywise error correction reported for within-group maps and voxelwise group comparisons reported with coordinate tables. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that assesses working memory (an established executive function domain) in concussed athletes and controls. The paper reports within-group voxelwise task contrasts (working memory minus baseline) and constructs group-level t-maps using whole-brain voxelwise analyses (with explicit thresholding and mixed-effects models). Whole-brain coverage was acquired (noting limited coverage of the very topmost parietal and rostral ventral temporal lobe), and results are reported as group-level statistical maps and coordinate tables/figures. Therefore all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met, and none of the exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, figures/tables).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (n-back) in adolescents and adults and reports within-group task contrasts (task vs fixation) and task-domain comparisons (I5, I6, I8, I9, I10 satisfied). However, the paper uses a region-of-interest (ROI)-based analysis approach (spherical ROIs derived from prior literature) to interrogate task effects, and the reported results are from these ROI statistics. Although single-subject voxelwise GLMs were estimated, the group-level results presented are ROI-based rather than group-level, voxelwise, whole-brain statistical maps. The manuscript does not present a voxelwise group-level task activation map or whole-brain voxelwise statistical analyses that would meet I7. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI analyses with no voxelwise group maps) and must be excluded.

This is an event-related fMRI study that investigates pro- and anti-saccade tasks, which probe inhibitory control (anti-saccade requires suppression of a prepotent response) — an established executive function domain (inhibition). The paper reports task-based, voxelwise analyses identifying activated voxels (t-test corrected for multiple comparisons) and provides Talairach coordinates for activations. Within-group contrasts are reported (e.g., pro-saccade vs fixation localizer; anti- vs pro-saccade comparisons; task vs baseline), and statistical analyses are conducted across subjects. Although imaging used partial slice coverage (focused on frontal and parietal cortex), the meta-analysis inclusion criterion allows partial-brain acquisition provided voxelwise analyses are reported. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an event-related fMRI study using a visual three-stimulus oddball task assessing selective/sustained attention (vigilance), which falls within the executive domain of vigilance. The full text reports within-group voxelwise task contrasts (one-sample random-effects t-tests for targets, distractors, standards) and presents whole-brain, voxelwise statistical maps and clusterwise-corrected results (figures and tables). Analyses include both fixed- and random-effects group-level voxelwise maps (voxelwise thresholds and clusterwise correction), satisfying whole-brain evidence. Participants are a defined human sample (older postmenopausal women). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-group contrasts, and is an empirical neuroimaging paper). Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10.

This is an fMRI task study of working memory in healthy adults (meets I5, I6), and it used within-subject task contrasts (encoding/maintenance vs baseline) and group-level summary statistics on those contrasts (meets I8 and I9). However, the paper does not present a group-level, voxelwise task-evoked statistical map or coordinates for within-group activations; primary results are reported as counts of suprathreshold voxels within an a priori mask and focal ROI analyses rather than voxelwise group maps. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I7 (no voxelwise group-level activation map reported) and meets exclusion criterion E3 (reports ROI/aggregate voxel-count metrics without providing voxelwise group statistical maps). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that directly probes inhibitory control using antisaccade and nogo paradigms (executive function: inhibition). It reports within-group, voxelwise mixed-effects contrasts (e.g., anti_response > pro_response, pro_response > baseline) and provides group-level statistical maps, tables of coordinates, and figures. Although slice coverage was limited (axial slices to dorsal caudate), analyses were voxelwise rather than ROI-restricted, which meets the allowance for partial-brain acquisition (I7). Participants are a within-group healthy adult sample, and multiple within-group contrasts are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the record appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI task-based study of working memory (2-back) in children and adults, directly addressing executive function (working memory). The paper reports within-group voxelwise contrasts (digit vs. letter+face; letter vs. digit+face; face vs. digit+letter) using random-effects group analyses and provides whole-brain results with peak coordinates and tables/figures. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, or only between-group contrasts). The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References, so the full text appears complete.

This is an empirical BOLD fMRI study using a task-based n-back working-memory paradigm (an executive function domain). The manuscript reports within-group, memory-load-dependent contrasts and group-level, voxelwise whole-brain random-effects analyses (with corrected results reported), and additionally provides coordinate/SVC results. Participants are healthy adults (acceptable per I9). Thus all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present and interpretable. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply: the study did not report only ROI/SVC analyses (whole-brain voxelwise results are reported), did not restrict to connectivity/resting analyses, and includes within-group task activation contrasts. Sample size is small but this affects quality not eligibility.

This is a PET task study of sustained attention (CPT/vigilance) in schizophrenia (meets I5: PET task-based; I6: vigilance; I9: clinical and control groups). However, the manuscript reports region-of-interest (ROI) analyses (60 predefined ROIs) and statistical comparisons on ROI-normalized metabolic rates rather than presenting any group-level, voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps or whole-brain voxelwise analyses. No within-group task-versus-baseline voxelwise contrasts are reported for any group. Therefore it fails I7 (no voxelwise/whole-brain analysis) and I8 (no within-group task contrast). This invokes exclusion criteria E3 (only ROI analyses with no voxelwise results) and E5 (no within-group task activation contrast reported). Full text appears complete. Accordingly the study is excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an event-related fMRI study using the Stroop task (inhibition/cognitive control) with drug-free depressed patients and healthy controls. The paper reports voxelwise, group-level GLM analyses (univariate contrasts: incongruent vs congruent) and within-group task contrasts, with whole-brain preprocessing and second-level SPM analyses. Although the paper also presents DCM connectivity analyses, it clearly includes task activation maps and within-group contrasts suitable for pooling. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met.

This paper presents a computational neural model of working memory and a proposed event-related fMRI design; it does not report any task-evoked, group-level voxelwise fMRI/PET activation results or within-group task contrasts. Although it addresses an executive function domain (working memory), it fails to provide empirical whole-brain activation maps or within-group contrasts. The manuscript explicitly states that fMRI data analysis is still ongoing and results will be presented elsewhere. Therefore it does not meet the key empirical imaging inclusion criteria and fits the exclusion of a non-empirical paper without original task activation results.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a 2-Back working memory paradigm (an established executive function domain). Whole-brain BOLD echoplanar imaging was acquired and group-level voxelwise analyses (2-Back vs 0-Back; conjunctive maps and voxel-wise paired t-tests) are reported. At least one within-group task contrast is presented (2-Back > 0-Back and similarity vs standard 2-Back), and results are described with cluster-level findings and ROI/voxelwise statistics; coordinates/regions and group summary maps are provided. Participants are a within-group sample of healthy adults. The study therefore satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10, and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E6). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory manipulation (executive function domain). It reports within-group voxelwise contrasts (manipulation > fixation and manipulation > maintenance) using a GLM and second-level group analyses, and supplements ROI analyses with an exploratory whole-brain voxelwise analysis (p<.001) identifying clusters and reporting coordinates/tables. The paper includes full methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5 (task fMRI), I6 (working memory), I7 (group-level voxelwise maps / whole-brain analyses), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (participant groups reported), and I10 (results presented in text/tables). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based verbal working memory paradigm (working memory = executive function domain). The full text includes introduction, detailed methods (task design, imaging parameters, preprocessing, GLM/FLAME group analysis), behavioral and voxelwise group-level results (whole-brain cluster-thresholded Z images and ROI follow-ups), and within-group contrasts (encoding, maintenance, retrieval each vs. baseline; probe-type contrasts). Thus it provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation maps and within-group contrasts in a healthy adult sample. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (includes methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based working memory paradigm (face vs voice delayed-recognition), which falls within executive function domains (working memory). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (multiple regression, group Z-maps, cluster-correction), and within-group contrasts (face vs control, voice vs control, and direct face vs voice comparisons). Results are reported in tables and figures. Participants are healthy adults and analyses meet inclusion requirements. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using task-based paradigms of working memory (object and spatial WM), which is an established executive function domain. The paper reports voxelwise, whole-brain, group-level statistical maps (Z-maps transformed to Talairach space, corrected thresholds) and multiple within-group task contrasts (e.g., object vs spatial delays, task vs sensorimotor control). Participants and methods are described and results are reported at the group and single-subject level. Reporting includes voxelwise maps and region-wise analyses consistent with inclusion requirements. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study that used task-based paradigms targeting inhibition and initiation of movement (executive domains listed in I6). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (cluster-thresholded Z-statistic images, FLAME group analysis) and provides within-group task contrasts (e.g., ballistic vs smooth; stepwise vs ballistic) with coordinates and thresholding described. Participants are a within-group sample of healthy adults. Results are reported as whole-brain maps and coordinate tables/figures. Thus all inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function activations are met, and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, refs).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of cognitive control (task switching/cognitive flexibility). It reports group-level, voxelwise task contrasts (Stage 3 vs Stage 1 and other within-group contrasts) using whole-brain acquisition and random-effects analyses, with tables/figures of coordinates and ROI and whole-brain results. Participants are neurologically normal adults and within-group contrasts are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, not non-empirical). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory updating (an executive function). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise mixed-effects group analyses (GLM contrasts such as update > cued maintenance and memory block > category discrimination), satisfying within-group task contrasts. Results are reported in text and supplementary tables, and full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a visual N-BACK working-memory paradigm (executive function). Whole-brain EPI acquisition and group-level voxelwise analyses of task contrasts (each N-BACK level vs 0-BACK) are reported (voxel-wise thresholding and cluster correction described), providing within-group task activation maps. Participants are a within-group sample of healthy adults. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This is an event-related fMRI study of a three-back working memory task with high-interference (lure) trials assessing attentional control/executive function. The paper reports voxelwise, group-level whole-brain analyses (voxelwise thresholds, cluster criteria, atlas-space normalization) and within-group task effects (event-related and sustained task activity versus fixation baseline and trial-type contrasts). Results are reported across the whole brain and as coordinates/region tables. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for task domain (working memory/executive control), modality (fMRI), whole-brain voxelwise reporting, and within-group task contrasts; no exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study that examines visual working memory (multiple object permanence tracking — MOPT), addressing dynamic updating and feature binding (falls within the working memory executive-function domain). The paper reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (random-effects SPM99; significance thresholds and cluster-level correction) and provides coordinates (Table 1) and activation maps. Within-group task contrasts are reported (MT−MC and ST−SC planned subtractions), comparing test and control conditions. Participants are healthy adults (within-group contrasts reported). Results are presented as voxelwise maps and tables/figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, behavioral and fMRI results, ROI analyses, discussion, and references, so the provided full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical imaging data). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is a task-based fMRI study that investigates executive-related processes (spatial working memory and elements of verbal executive function/perseveration) in perimenopausal/recent postmenopausal women.
