The study is a PET task-based study with an active vigilance task, so it meets I5 (PET task-based), I6 (vigilance is an executive domain), I8 (within-group activation reported for patients during the vigilance task) and I9 (clinical participant group allowed). However, the abstract does not explicitly confirm that at least one group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked statistical map was reported (I7). Because I7 cannot be verified from the provided content and full text is incomplete, I cannot confirm all inclusion criteria are met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are clearly met. Recommend obtaining full text to confirm voxelwise whole-brain analyses before including.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study with group-level voxelwise maps and within-group contrasts, but the tasks (lexicosemantic decision, tone discrimination, and visuomotor sequence learning) do not target established executive function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore it fails the core inclusion criteria I5 and I6 required for a meta-analysis of executive function activations. It does meet criteria for whole-brain voxelwise analysis and within-group contrasts, and participant sampling is acceptable, but the cognitive domains assessed are outside the review scope.

The study is an fMRI event-related item-recognition (verbal working memory) task, so it clearly meets I5 (task-based fMRI) and I6 (working memory). However the provided full text is incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata). The abstract mentions linear regression to locate activation and subsequent ROI analyses but does not explicitly confirm a group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task activation map (I7) nor explicitly report a within-group task contrast (I8). Because ALL inclusion criteria must be verifiable and I7 and I8 cannot be confirmed from the incomplete text, I exclude the study. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met based on available information.

This is an empirical PET study using task-based activation (H2(15)O PET) that directly tests an executive function (counting Stroop — cognitive control/inhibition). The paper reports within-group, voxelwise, group-level SPM99 analyses contrasting incongruent vs. neutral conditions (a within-group task contrast), and it includes both whole-brain analyses and ROI/small-volume-corrected results with coordinates and tables reported. Participants are a defined group of healthy volunteers. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that reports voxelwise, group-level task-evoked activation maps (SPM analyses) and within-group contrasts (task vs rest and task comparisons). The PHONO task explicitly engages phonological working memory (phonological loop) and the PUZZLE task requires visuospatial manipulation and motor executive processes, which fall within executive-function domains (working memory / planning/manipulation). Although slice coverage was partial, analyses were voxelwise and therefore qualify under whole-brain evidence criteria. Results are reported in the main text with activation maps and quantitative comparisons across tasks. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present and sufficient for screening.

This is an event-related task fMRI study of working memory (spatial vs. object) with within-group task contrasts and appropriate task-based design. However, all analyses were performed using regions-of-interest (caudate nucleus, DLPFC, M1, PPC) and group analyses extracted ROI-based t-values rather than reporting a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical map. The manuscript explicitly states that all analyses were performed with ROIs and used ROI-based correction, and group tests collapsed across voxels within ROIs. Therefore it does not provide the required group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps (I7 not met) and meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI analyses). Full text appears complete (includes methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of cognitive control using a stop-signal (inhibition) paradigm in healthy adults. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses (SPM2) with family-wise error correction and provides voxel coordinates and contrasts (e.g., SE vs. SS, SS vs. G, pSE vs. pG), satisfying within-group task contrasts. Results are reported across the whole brain (including thalamus, ACC, SMA, etc.). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and conclusions. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This is an empirical PET study that used a task-based immediate serial recall paradigm probing working memory (an executive function domain). It reports group-level, voxelwise SPM analyses (whole-brain normalization, smoothing, voxelwise contrasts and thresholding) and provides within-group task contrasts (e.g., main effect of working memory, irrelevant speech contrasts, and interaction contrasts). Coordinates and statistic peaks are reported. Participants are a within-group sample of healthy adults. Thus all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study reports task-based fMRI (and EEG) of an executive function task (intradimensional/extradimensional rule shifts; cognitive flexibility). It includes within-group, voxelwise whole-brain group-level contrasts (negative>positive feedback for ID and ED conditions) analyzed with SPM2 and reported with coordinates and cluster results. The task falls within executive function/cognitive control (cognitive flexibility), and whole-brain voxelwise analyses and ROI analyses are described. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for a meta-analysis of task-evoked executive function activations. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, and tables/figures) is provided and appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (2-back CPT) in healthy adults, reporting voxelwise whole-brain SPM analyses contrasting 2-back vs 0-back (a within-group task contrast). Results include coordinates and cluster statistics (BA10) and methods indicate whole-brain voxelwise analysis. Thus the paper meets all inclusion criteria for executive-function task activations and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of a two-back working memory task (an established executive function domain). The paper reports within-group, epoch-related GLM contrasts (task vs rest) and presents group-level voxelwise SPM results (figures and tables of activations/deactivations), satisfying whole-brain, task-evoked map requirements. Participants are healthy adults (acceptable sample). The full text includes Introduction, Methods (image acquisition, GLM), Results (voxelwise activations, tables, figures) and Discussion, so the article is complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are violated. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study investigating inhibition of return (an inhibitory attentional effect). It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses (random-effects ANOVA; cluster-level correction) with standard within-group task contrasts (e.g., Long_SOA (Cued+Uncued) > Short_SOA; cued vs uncued), and provides coordinates/tables and figures. Participants are healthy adults. The full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided. Therefore it meets I5–I10 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

Full text is incomplete (HTML skeleton only). Title and metadata indicate an event-related fMRI study of context processing in dorsolateral prefrontal cortex in patients with schizophrenia, so I5 (fMRI task-based study) and I6 (executive-function domain: context processing/working memory) appear met. However core article content (methods, results) is missing, so critical inclusion criteria cannot be verified: I7 (whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked map) cannot be confirmed, I8 (within-group task contrast) cannot be confirmed, I9 (while participants are clinical, within-group contrast reporting cannot be verified) and I10 (reporting of whole-brain results in coordinates/figures/text) cannot be confirmed. No exclusion criteria (E3-E6) are demonstrably met from the incomplete content. Because the full text is incomplete and key inclusion criteria cannot be verified, the study is excluded pending a complete full text.

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study of interference resolution and working memory (executive control). It reports task-based within-group voxelwise contrasts (interference vs control) at the group level with whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses and tables of stereotaxic coordinates. The tasks fall squarely within executive-function domains (working memory/inhibition). Partial slice coverage is acceptable per criteria and voxelwise group contrasts are provided and described in text/tables. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present, so fulltext is complete.

This is a PET study with whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM99) comparing syntactically complex (SO) versus simple (OS) sentences within groups; coordinates and within-group contrasts are reported. However, the study’s primary focus is language/syntactic processing and individual differences in working memory and processing speed, not an executive function or cognitive control task per se. Although working memory was measured as an individual-difference variable, the experimental task is a plausibility judgment for sentence comprehension rather than a task designed to probe established executive domains (working memory task paradigms, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criteria I5 and I6. Inclusion criteria met: I7, I8, I9, I10. Exclusion criteria met: none. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that investigates internal initiation/modulation of externally cued motor sequences. It meets inclusion: (I5) uses fMRI and assesses cognitive control aspects (internal initiation/modulation), (I6) examines initiation/internal pacing (an accepted executive domain here), (I7) reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level SPM analyses, (I8) includes within-group task contrasts (e.g., task vs baseline and condition contrasts like TATA vs 1 Hz), (I9) uses a participant group (healthy volunteers) and reports within-group results, (I10) whole-brain results are described in text/tables/figures. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore include.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study probing working memory and selective attention (executive-function domains). The methods describe voxelwise, group-level statistical maps (NT–CT and TO–RS contrasts), normalization to CMNI and thresholded z-statistics, and tables/figures of activation — satisfying whole-brain, voxelwise reporting. Within-group task contrasts are computed and used to generate group maps (i.e., task > control/rest contrasts), and results are reported in text/tables/figures. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References, so appears complete. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that directly investigates cognitive control/conflict (processing of semantic–prosodic incongruence) using a within-group, voxelwise whole-brain analysis. Group-level random-effects SPM2 contrasts are reported (e.g., CONF vs NOCONF, main effect vs baseline), with whole-brain correction and voxelwise inference. The paradigm requires overriding task-irrelevant semantic information to identify prosody (inhibition/response selection), which maps onto executive function domains. Participants are healthy adults and within-group contrasts are provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Full article content (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, Conclusions) is present. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Exclusion E3 met: the paper uses an ROI-based analysis pipeline (voxels were selected within anatomically defined ROIs based on a per-subject main effect of time and subsequent ROI-averaged time-course ANOVAs) and the main reported results are ROI-averaged time courses and across-subject ROI statistics. The manuscript does not present a group-level, voxelwise task-activation statistical map (i.e. no whole-group voxelwise contrast/SPM-style maps are reported), so criterion I7 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked map) is not satisfied. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI study of cognitive control), I6 (task involves inhibition/countermanding), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported, e.g. STOP vs GO, STOP-success vs STOP-fail), I9 (within-group healthy volunteer sample reported), I10 (task activation results are described in text/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (no group-level voxelwise task map reported).

This is an empirical fMRI study that (1) uses a verbal working memory task (an established executive function domain) and reports group-level, voxelwise random-effects analyses (verbal working memory > rest). The paper provides whole-brain, spatially normalized voxelwise analyses, a within-group task contrast, and reports results from healthy participant groups; results are described in detail across methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the review are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study using an executive-function task (two-back working memory) and reports within-group task vs fixation measures, so it meets I5, I6, I8, and I9. However, the paper’s analyses are focused on thalamic ROI-based task activation measures and do not present any group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps in this full text (the authors note whole-brain exploratory analyses were published elsewhere). Therefore it fails I7 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI analyses reported with no voxelwise results in this article). Full text contains methods, results, and discussion so fulltext_incomplete=false.

Excluded because study reports only ROI/SVC-based analyses rather than presenting a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map (Exclusion E3). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI study of cognitive tasks), I6 (includes an executive-domain task: working memory), I8 (within-group task contrasts were computed), I9 (healthy adult participant group). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map is reported; analyses are restricted to pre-defined ROIs with small-volume correction). I10: reporting of whole-brain voxelwise results as coordinates/figures is not evident in the full text provided. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded under E3.

This is a task-based PET study using FDG with a numerical calculation paradigm and reports group-level, voxelwise SPM contrasts (task vs baseline) showing task-evoked activations. Numerical calculations engage working memory/executive processes and elicited prefrontal activation, satisfying the review’s executive-function domain requirement. The paper includes whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (SPM) and within-group task contrasts; results are reported in text, figures, and tables. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) apply. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that manipulates the central executive component of working memory using a number-subtraction task (meets I5). The task targets working memory/central executive executive-domain processes (meets I6). Imaging methods and analyses are whole-brain and voxelwise (SPM99 preprocessing, normalization, second-level random-effects one-sample t tests with voxelwise thresholds and cluster extent), and coordinates/figures/tables of activations are reported (meets I7 and I10). The paper reports within-group task contrasts (each subtraction condition vs baseline; high-demand vs low-demand; interaction contrasts) at group level (meets I8). Participants are a within-group sample of healthy adults (meets I9). No exclusion criteria are violated (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive control/dual-task processing in healthy adults. It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-head analyses (e.g., DM>SM, SM>SP), Time×Group and Time×Group×Condition interactions, and provides coordinates and statistical maps in the text/tables. The methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

Full text is incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). Based on the abstract, this is an fMRI task study addressing cognitive processing with a contrast between two motor tasks differing in sustained attention, so I5 (fMRI task study), I6 (task involves vigilance/sustained attention), I8 (within-group task contrast) and I9 (any participant group — within-group contrast reported) appear to be satisfied. However, I cannot verify I7 (presence of a group-level voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked statistical map) or I10 (acceptable whole-brain reporting in coordinates/figures/text) from the provided material. No exclusion criteria are clearly met (e.g., not clearly methods-only or ROI-only). Because critical inclusion criteria (I7 and I10) cannot be confirmed from the incomplete full text, I exclude the study pending full-text availability.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that reports within-group, whole-brain voxelwise activation contrasts for reasoning tasks. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI task-based study assessing cognitive control/executive processes — reasoning tasks engage executive processes), I6 (tasks involve maintenance and manipulation of information consistent with the working memory/executive domain), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analyses with group-level reporting of activated ROIs and Talairach coordinates), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported: conditional vs baseline, relational vs baseline, conditional vs relational), I9 (healthy adult participant group; within-group contrasts reported), I10 (whole-brain results reported with coordinates and Z-scores in text/tables/figures). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so it appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

Exclusion criteria met: E4 (study reports only connectivity/resting-state analyses without reporting a task-evoked voxelwise activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI study including a task paradigm) and I6 (task = working memory, an established executive function domain). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical map is reported), I8 (no within-group task contrast voxelwise activation map is presented; analyses focus on connectivity differences between rest and a continuous 2-back task rather than task-evoked activation maps), and I10 (no whole-brain voxelwise task activation coordinates or maps reported for a within-group task contrast). The full text appears complete. Therefore the study is excluded because it only reports connectivity/resting-state analyses and does not provide the required task activation maps or within-group voxelwise contrasts required for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level activation contrasts for within-group task comparisons. Although the primary focus is implicit sequence learning, the authors explicitly interpret activations in terms of spatial working memory and response monitoring (executive/cognitive control processes). The study used voxelwise SPM analyses with cluster-level correction across the entire brain, and contrasts compare fixed-sequence vs random-order blocks (within-group). Participants are healthy adults. Results are reported in figures and tables. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a visual oddball paradigm that probes attention/vigilance and working memory (rehearsal/counting) — both established executive function domains. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain (near full coverage) activation maps and presents within-group task contrasts for low-risk and high-risk groups (task vs implicit baseline), with statistical maps and corrected results described in the text. Although a small portion of orbital frontal and anterior inferior temporal lobes were not imaged, the analysis was voxelwise and permutation-based, satisfying whole-brain (voxelwise) reporting. Thus the study meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function) in healthy adults. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Group-level, voxelwise SPM analyses are reported (e.g., manipulation vs maintenance, high vs low load) with statistical maps and tables; within-group contrasts are explicitly presented. Results are reported in tables and figures and described in the text. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not only between-group contrasts, and it is empirical). Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are violated.

Only the title and abstract (metadata) are provided; full article (methods, results, figures/tables) is not available, so key inclusion criteria cannot be verified. Inclusion criteria met based on abstract: I5 (event-related fMRI assessing working memory, an executive function) and I6 (task falls within executive function domain: working memory). Inclusion criteria not verifiable from provided content: I7 (cannot confirm a group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked statistical map is reported), I8 (cannot confirm a within-group task contrast is reported at group level), I10 (cannot confirm whole-brain results are reported as voxelwise maps or coordinates in text/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are clearly met from the abstract. Because essential methodological/results details are missing, I exclude this record pending full text access.

This study is excluded because it reports ROI-based analyses only and does not provide group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps (exclusion E3). Meets inclusion: I5 (task-based fMRI assessing executive function — Stroop, Go/No-Go, Sternberg), I6 (tasks fall within executive domains: inhibition and working memory), I8 (within-group task contrasts were computed at first level: NoGo vs Go, Incongruent vs Congruent, Retain6 vs Retain2, Finger tapping vs fixation), I9 (healthy participant group reported). Does NOT meet inclusion I7: no whole-brain group-level voxelwise task activation maps are reported — analyses are ROI summaries and paired ROI tests; and thus there are no voxelwise group maps or reported coordinates/figures that would qualify per I7. I10 (acceptable formats) is not applicable as no whole-brain voxelwise results were reported. Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study reports whole-brain, within-group task contrasts of an imitation paradigm (COPY vs INCONGRUOUS, COPY vs SPATIAL) in healthy participants and reports voxelwise results with coordinates. However, the experimental task assesses perception–action matching / imitation (social sensorimotor processes) rather than an established executive function domain. Although the authors discuss working memory and error-detection processes, the tasks do not constitute classical executive-function paradigms (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation) as required by the review inclusion criteria. Therefore I5 and I6 are not satisfied, while I7, I8, I9, and I10 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a Stroop task to probe attentional control/executive function (inhibition/selection). The paper reports within-group, voxelwise, mixed-effects group analyses (FLAME) with whole-brain cluster-based inference and tables of peak coordinates for contrasts (e.g., incongruent vs neutral; one-word vs four-word). Tasks clearly fall within executive function domains (inhibition/cognitive control). Thus it meets all inclusion criteria and violates none of the exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is a task-based fMRI study using a 2-back working memory task (an established executive function domain). Group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise analyses were reported (random-effects SPM2 analyses with FDR-corrected thresholds and coordinates/ROIs reported). Within-group task contrasts (task vs baseline and condition comparisons: Word, Cross, Within) are presented. Participants are healthy adults. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so core content is present. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and it is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive-function task activations.

This is an empirical PET study reporting task-based activation during executive/cognitive tasks (WCST and RPM). It includes within-group, voxelwise group-level contrasts (task minus control) using SPM and voxel-by-voxel analyses, with whole-brain coverage and reported statistical maps/tables. WCST is a canonical executive function (working memory/cognitive flexibility) satisfying the executive-domain requirement. Results are presented as group-level activation maps and tables/figures, and full methods, results, and discussion are provided in the full text. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-group contrasts). Full text appears complete.

Although this is an fMRI task study of sustained attention/pain (meets I5, I6) and it reports within-group task contrasts (no-pain vs pain/CPT conditions) in both healthy and OA groups (meets I8 and I9) with results described in the text/figures (meets I10), the analyses are confined to a hand-drawn anterior cingulate ROI. The paper does not present a group-level, voxelwise whole-brain (or partial-brain voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map outside an a priori ROI; the reported results are ROI-focused/IC-weightings within the cingulate. This constitutes an ROI-only analysis with no voxelwise, group-level activation map reported, triggering exclusion criterion E3. Inclusion criterion I7 (group-level voxelwise task map) is not satisfied. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using an n-back working memory task (executive function). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. The study reports voxelwise, whole-brain group analyses (SPM2) with within-group task contrasts (3-back vs OFF) and provides tables/figures with coordinates. Participant sample (healthy male social drinkers) is acceptable. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a verbal Sternberg working memory task (an executive function—working memory). It reports within-group, voxelwise, group-level analyses (FSL FEAT/FLAME) including contrasts of WM>rest and parametric linear [−1 0 1] and nonlinear [−1 2 −1] load-dependent effects, with whole-brain coverage and cluster-thresholded Z maps. Results are reported for children, adolescents, and young adults (within-group contrasts present for each). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and include within-group activation contrasts (not only between-group). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of visual working memory (an executive function: working memory) in healthy adults. The authors ran group-level voxelwise SPM analyses (e.g., a significant Task > fixation effect, P < 0.05 corrected) to identify ROIs and report within-group task contrasts and load/feature effects across the sample. Whole-brain coverage (except the bottom of the cerebellum) and voxelwise results are described in the methods and results. Thus the study meets I5 (fMRI task-based executive function), I6 (working memory domain), I7 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain analysis), I8 (within-group task contrast), I9 (participant group reported), and I10 (whole-brain results described). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of verbal working memory (2-back vs 0-back) in healthy adults. The paper reports within-group, voxelwise, group-level random-effects analyses (2-back minus 0-back) and interaction contrasts, with whole-brain voxelwise results presented as statistical maps and coordinates. Methods, results, and discussion are present in full text. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for executive-function task activations (working memory). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical).

This is an event-related fMRI study using a task-based arithmetic verification paradigm that probes cognitive control/working memory and interference resolution (executive functions). The study reports group-level, voxelwise random-effects analyses (SPM99) contrasting incorrect vs. correct equations (a within-group task contrast), with whole-brain coverage and results presented as significant clusters/figures/tables. Participants are a within-group sample of healthy subjects. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function fMRI with voxelwise whole-brain analyses and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

Full text is incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). From the abstract we can confirm: I5 (PET, task-based WCST), I6 (task is an executive function — WCST), I8 (within-group task contrast: WCST vs sensorimotor control), and I9 (participant groups, including patient and controls). However I7 (requirement for a group-level voxelwise whole-brain statistical map) cannot be verified from the available text, nor can I10 (clear reporting of whole-brain results in coordinates/figures/text). Because the full text is missing, I cannot determine whether analyses were voxelwise whole-brain or ROI-based (potential E3). Per screening rules, inability to verify required inclusion criteria (I7) and potential violation of E3 mandates exclusion. No exclusion criteria are explicitly met based on the abstract alone. Recommend obtaining full text to reassess.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that reports within-group, voxelwise, whole-brain task contrasts relevant to executive function. The tasks include spatial working memory (an established executive function domain) and sustained spatial attention/vigilance. The paper presents group-level voxelwise analyses (random-effects SPM), reports coordinates and statistical maps for contrasts such as WM delay vs control and attention delay vs control, and performs laterality contrasts (attend-right vs attend-left). Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (working memory and vigilance domains), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analyses and coordinates reported), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (healthy adult participant group within-group contrasts reported), and I10 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates and described in text). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory updating (executive function) with healthy adult participants. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Group-level, voxelwise task activation contrasts are reported (e.g., all-updates > hold; RULE > NMBR; NMBR > RULE) with whole-brain voxelwise thresholding and cluster correction; supplemental tables/coordinates are available. Analyses are within-group task contrasts. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, not non-empirical). Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria and should be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based operation span paradigm targeting verbal working memory and the central executive (executive function). The study reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2) with voxel- and cluster-level thresholds, provides within-group task contrasts (Concrete vs Abstract OST phases and task vs baseline), and reports coordinates/figures. Participants are healthy adults and the full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I5–I10 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical PET task-based study that explicitly probes spatial working memory and planning during covered maze traversal, which fall within executive function domains (working memory/planning). The study reports group-level, voxelwise SPM analyses and multiple within-group task contrasts (e.g., covered vs motor, covered vs visual, covered vs uncovered), with stereotactic coordinates and SPM{Z} maps described in the text. Participants (healthy adults) are a qualifying group and whole-brain results are reported in coordinates/tables. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study examining cognitive control/executive function (representation and maintenance of context, selection) during a missing-letter language production task. Inclusion criteria: I5 satisfied—uses fMRI and assesses cognitive control; I6 satisfied—task engages working memory/maintenance and selection (working memory domain of executive function); I7 satisfied—reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (random-effects GLM, AFNI; reported whole-brain activation maps/coordinates); I8 satisfied—reports within-group task contrasts (context vs neutral; context-appropriate vs context-inappropriate; selection demand contrasts); I9 satisfied—within-group contrasts on healthy adult participants; I10 satisfied—whole-brain results clearly described in text/tables/figures. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study that directly tests deception (pretending to know) which requires intentional response manipulation and cognitive control, consistent with executive function/inhibition domains. The study reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2; random-effects ANOVA) with coordinates and thresholding, and presents within-group task contrasts (e.g., Lie vs Truth, LN vs CR, FR vs CR). Participants are a within-group healthy adult sample. Results are reported as voxelwise activation maps and peak coordinates in the text/tables. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of working memory (an executive function) comparing individuals with schizophrenia and controls. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps (task–fixation and onset-transient correlations), and presents within-group task contrasts and regional time courses for each group. Tasks include working memory (2-back), encoding, and recognition — all within executive/cognitive domains. Whole-brain coverage and voxelwise analyses are described; results are reported in figures, tables, and text. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. The provided full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is a task-based fMRI study of cognitive control processes (conflict detection, selection, and suppression) during selective retrieval practice, directly addressing executive-function-related control and inhibition. The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise group-level task contrasts (e.g., successful vs. unsuccessful retrieval; first vs. third retrieval), provides coordinate-based results, and includes within-group analyses in a healthy adult sample. Thus it satisfies all inclusion criteria (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria apply (whole-brain voxelwise results are reported; not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

Full text appears incomplete (only chapter title/abstract/metadata provided). From available information, the study uses fMRI and a Stroop task, so it meets I5 (task-based fMRI on executive function/cognitive control) and I6 (task within established executive domain: inhibition). However, I cannot verify I7 (whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical map) because the full methods/results are not available; I8 (explicit within-group task contrast reported as voxelwise map) cannot be confirmed from the abstract alone; and I10 (clear reporting of whole-brain results in tables/figures/text) is not verifiable. Because key inclusion criteria (I7 and I8) cannot be confirmed from the incomplete full text, the study must be excluded pending receipt of the full article. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are clearly met based on provided content.

The study is an event-related fMRI investigation of orthographic/phonological facilitation in picture–word naming (language/word-production domain), not a task designed to assess established executive functions or cognitive control domains. Therefore it does not meet inclusion criteria I5 and I6. Inclusion criteria met based on available text: I7 (whole-brain voxelwise fMRI results reported), I8 (within-group task contrast: related vs unrelated distractors), I9 (within-group participant sample reported), I10 (whole-brain results described in text). No exclusion criteria are triggered. Note: full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided), so fulltext_incomplete=true and confidence is reduced accordingly.

This is a task-based fMRI study using a Go/No Go inhibition paradigm (executive function), with group-level, voxelwise SPM2 random-effects analyses and reported within-group contrasts (errors and correct rejects) for both OCD and control groups. Whole-brain preprocessing/normalization was performed and results are reported as voxel coordinates and figures; small-volume correction was applied to ROIs but voxelwise task-activation maps and coordinate tables are provided. Participants include a clinical sample (OCD) and matched controls. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study of a brief delayed matching-to-sample task that probes working memory and mismatch/conflict processing (executive function). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (contrast: incongruent vs. congruent), presents activation maps and ROI follow-ups, and reports statistical tests of within-group contrasts. Although slice coverage appears limited (12 axial slices), the analyses are voxelwise and thus meet the partial-brain allowance. Results are reported in the text and figures. Therefore all inclusion criteria for task-based fMRI executive-function activation maps are satisfied (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an original event-related fMRI study (re-analysis of five datasets) that assesses motor response inhibition (Go/NoGo), an executive function domain (inhibition). The manuscript reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (voxelwise t-tests, cluster thresholds, Talairach normalization) and presents within-group task contrasts (STOPS vs baseline/ongoing Go trials) and split-group contrasts; results are reported as activation maps and ROI analyses. The full text includes introduction, methods (task, scanning, preprocessing, voxelwise analysis), results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical or only between-group contrasts). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of task-evoked executive-function activations.

This is a task-based fMRI study of verbal working memory (an executive function domain). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM99 random-effects t tests) with within-group task contrasts (high vs low load for working memory and motoric rehearsal). Results are reported in tables of coordinates and figures and described in the text. Participants are human subjects and a within-group activation contrast is provided. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that investigates spatial working memory (an established executive function domain). It used whole-brain acquisition and reports voxelwise group analyses (ROI-based and normalized group-average/t-maps with coordinates and tables). Multiple within-group task contrasts are reported (e.g., delay-period contrasts [Delayfilled, Delayunfilled], lateralized contrasts), and results are reported for a within-group healthy adult sample. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text is complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical PET activation study using a task-based paradigm (Hayling Test) that directly probes executive functions (verbal initiation and suppression). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise statistical parametric mapping analyses (SPM) with within-group contrasts (Hayling part A vs reading, part B vs reading, and A vs B). Although the scanner had a limited field-of-view (notably excluding the cerebellum), analyses were voxelwise and therefore satisfy the partial-brain allowance. Participants were healthy adults (acceptable per I9). Results are described in the text and figures (activation foci and Brodmann areas), meeting reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion, so is complete.

This is an event-related fMRI study using a delayed-response working memory task (executive function domain: working memory) with emotional and neutral distracters. The paper reports group-level voxelwise analyses (random-effects group analysis to identify amygdala sensitivity to emotional > neutral, trial-based voxelwise correlations and across-subject paired t comparisons, conjunction and ANOVA results) and provides coordinates and figures. Within-group contrasts are reported (emotional vs neutral distracters; correct vs incorrect trials), meeting the requirement for within-group task contrasts. Participants are human (healthy young adults). Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I10 and violates no exclusion criteria (E3–E6). Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study that used a Stroop color-word interference task (an executive function/inhibition paradigm) and reports task-evoked, within-group voxelwise activation analyses. The paper describes group-level statistical maps (incongruent vs. neutral contrast, corrected P<0.001) transformed to stereotactic space for multisubject comparisons, satisfying whole-brain voxelwise reporting. Participants were healthy adults; at least one within-group contrast is reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical work) are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete.

The study reports original human fMRI data including a counting Stroop task (an inhibition/interference paradigm within executive function). It carries out group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (fixed-effect group analyses) with statistical parametric maps and reports coordinates/tables (FWER-corrected). Within-group contrasts are reported (counting vs rest; neutral and interference conditions). Participant groups are described (control group of healthy females) and results are presented for within-group contrasts. Therefore it satisfies I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (executive/inhibition task), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise maps), I8 (within-group contrasts), I9 (participant groups acceptable), and I10 (coordinates/tables reported). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical PET study using task-based paradigms that probe executive function (manipulation/updating component of working memory). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise SPM analyses (ANCOVA across subjects, SPM(t)→SPM(Z)), whole-brain contrasts (manipulation vs serial; memory vs reading; interaction; conjunction; post-hoc), and reports activations in Brodmann areas and regional loci. Within-group task contrasts are explicitly reported (e.g., alphabetical vs serial tasks, reading vs recall), satisfying the requirement for a within-group task activation map. Participants are healthy adult volunteers. Results are presented as whole-brain voxelwise analyses (thresholded SPM) and described in the text/tables, meeting reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function domain). It reports group-level, voxelwise analyses (random-effects), with whole-brain maps and Talairach/surface-based localizations. Within-group task contrasts are presented (Encode/Delay/Probe contrasts versus fixation and contrasts between delay conditions), and results are reported in tables and figures. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of verbal working memory (an executive function domain) that reports group-level voxelwise analyses. The paper includes within-group contrasts (high vs low load) for alcoholics and controls (Tables 2 and 3) and reports exploratory whole-brain voxelwise results (alpha=0.01) in addition to ROI analyses. Whole-brain acquisition and voxelwise statistical maps are described and tabulated, satisfying the requirement for at least one group-level voxelwise task-evoked map. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and violates no exclusion criteria.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). While the abstract indicates an fMRI study of working memory (so I5 and I6 are satisfied), the provided content does not allow verification of key inclusion criteria: I7 (presence of a group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked statistical map) and I8 (at least one within-group task contrast). These cannot be confirmed from the available text. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are clearly met. Because I7 and I8 are unverified and the full text is incomplete, the study is excluded pending access to the complete article reporting voxelwise group analyses and within-group contrasts.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based working memory (delayed item recognition) paradigm (executive function domain: working memory). The fMRI methods describe voxelwise first- and second-level GLMs (SPM99) and multivariate linear modeling (MLM)/sequential latent root testing on group-level data, yielding whole-brain load-dependent spatial patterns and within-group pattern expressions. Within-group contrasts (load-dependent slopes per phase) and group-specific pattern tests are reported. The paper therefore provides task-evoked, group-level voxelwise activation analyses (even though partial slice coverage was used, analyses were voxelwise). All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study reporting whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts (Rotation>Control; Intact>Scrambled; Saccade>Fixation). The mental rotation task engages visuospatial transformation and working memory/cognitive control processes, which fall within executive function domains (working memory/cognitive control). Whole-brain SPMs and coordinate tables are reported, and within-group voxelwise contrasts are presented. Participants are a within-group healthy sample. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full text contains methods, results, and discussion, so is complete for screening purposes.

This is an event-related fMRI study using a visual oddball task (targets vs baseline) that probes selective attention/vigilance, an established executive domain. The paper reports voxelwise GLM analyses and group-level mixed-effects (FLAME) whole-brain statistical maps (cluster-corrected Z>2.3) and presents within-group task contrasts (target-related BOLD vs baseline), with VOI analyses and group results described. Participants are healthy adults. All required inclusion criteria are met (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical content). The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete for screening purposes.

This is an event-related fMRI study of episodic associative memory encoding (face–name–city triplets). It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (e.g., hit discontinuous vs hit simultaneous; associative formation vs misses) and thus meets I7, I8, I9, and I10. However, the study’s primary aim and task probe episodic memory/associative encoding, not an established executive-function paradigm. Although the authors discuss working-memory and executive contributions, the task was not designed or analysed as a working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, or initiation task. Therefore it does not meet I5 and I6 (does not primarily assess executive function/cognitive control within established EF domains). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

The provided content appears to be an abstract/summary only (full text incomplete). The study uses task-based fMRI of auditory orienting (exogenous facilitation and inhibition of return) in healthy volunteers and reports activation patterns and behavioral effects. However the task does not assess an established executive function domain as defined by the review (working memory, response inhibition as cognitive control, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation) — inhibition of return is an attentional orienting phenomenon, not the executive/inhibitory control targeted by the meta-analysis. From the available content I can identify a within-group task contrast (valid vs. invalid cue conditions; I8). I cannot confirm whole-brain, voxelwise group-level maps or that the fMRI analyses meet the review’s whole-brain reporting requirement because the full text/methods/results are not provided. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered based on the abstract. Therefore the study is excluded because it does not meet I5 and I6 (and whole-brain reporting I7 cannot be confirmed from the incomplete text). If the complete full text shows the task was intended to probe executive-control processes (and provides voxelwise whole-brain within-group maps), it could be reconsidered.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using the emotional Stroop (an inhibition/attention executive function task). The paper reports within-group voxelwise contrasts (negative vs neutral word stimuli accompanied by galvanic skin responses) and whole-brain random-effects analyses with activation foci reported in text/figures/tables. Full article contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References, so full text is complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria relevant to task-based whole-brain executive-function activations are met.

This study reports task-based fMRI of an n-back working memory paradigm (an established executive function domain) with group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (random-effects SPM99 second-level results, corrected thresholds). It includes within-group task contrasts (e.g. 2-back > 1-back) and reports whole-brain effects (tables/figures) including interactions of load × visibility in LOC. Participants are healthy volunteers and results are suitable for pooling. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (2-back paradigm) in schizophrenia and healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (SPM99) and explicitly presents within-group contrasts (2-back > 0-back, 2-back degraded > 0-back degraded) for patients and controls; results are reported with coordinates and thresholding details. Thus it satisfies I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (working memory = executive domain), I7 (voxelwise whole-brain analyses), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (clinical participant groups acceptable), and I10 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables). No exclusion criteria apply: it is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not limited to between-group contrasts, and is empirical. Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text incomplete: only title and abstract are provided. The abstract confirms an event-related fMRI study of working memory (satisfies I5 and I6). However, the available content does not allow verification that the paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task-evoked statistical maps (I7) or explicitly documents at least one within-group voxelwise task contrast (I8). Because ALL inclusion criteria must be verifiable from the full text and these key criteria cannot be confirmed, the study is excluded pending full-text access. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are clearly met based on the abstract alone.

Excluded because the study does not provide a within-group task activation contrast required for inclusion (I8). The paper reports voxelwise, whole-brain PET comparisons of nicotine patch versus placebo during an aggression provocation task (drug effects during task), but does not report task>baseline or other within-group task activation contrasts. Also, the primary task (Bushman Aggression Test) is not clearly within the predefined executive-function domains (I6); the CPT (vigilance) is mentioned but no within-group task activation maps for the CPT are reported. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analyses), I9 (participant groups acceptable), I10 (whole-brain results reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (task within established executive domains) and I8 (within-group task contrast). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) were triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using the Paced Visual Serial Addition Task (PVSAT), which targets working memory/executive processes. The paper reports voxelwise whole-brain group-level analyses (SPM2) including within-group contrasts (calculation vs control) for controls, CIS, and CDMS groups, with thresholds and cluster correction described. Results are reported in the text, tables and figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive-function task activations.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (operation span), an executive function domain. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM99) with corrected thresholds and tables/coordinates, within-group task contrasts (Arithmetic+Memory vs single-task and task vs baseline), and reports results in figures/tables. Participants are healthy adults and a within-group contrast is provided. All inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion and references, so the full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of working memory (an executive function). Methods report task-based paradigms (phonological and visual working memory) with within-group, voxelwise group-level analyses using SPM99 (fixed-effects), reporting voxelwise significance (P<0.05 corrected) and figures/tables of whole-brain activations. Although acquisition used 16 slices (partial coverage), analyses were voxelwise and group-level contrasts (memory vs matched control) are reported. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10). No exclusion criteria are triggered (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full text appears to contain introduction, methods, results, and discussion (core content present).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive function (semantic event sequencing/planning). The paper reports within-group voxelwise task contrasts (PS > CON) for both HIV+ and control groups, using whole-brain correction (FDR) and random-effects group-level analyses in SPM2. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise activation maps are described and displayed; between-group contrasts and functional connectivity are also reported. The task falls within established executive domains (planning/sequencing). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; it is complete for screening. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

Based on the provided abstract and metadata, this is a task-based PET study reporting group-level activation patterns for simple calculation and number repetition in 12 healthy volunteers. Tasks engage working memory components (phonological store and articulatory loop) and attention, placing them within established executive function domains. The paper reports whole-brain activation patterns (voxelwise PET activations across the group) and within-group task contrasts (calculation vs repetition/ baseline). However, only title/abstract/metadata were provided here (no full methods/results/discussion), so fulltext_incomplete is set to true and there is some residual uncertainty about specifics of voxelwise reporting and coordinates. Inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 appear satisfied; no exclusion criteria are met.

This study reports task-based fMRI of working memory (an executive function domain) in a within-subject, placebo-controlled design. The full text describes voxelwise, whole-brain analyses (voxel-by-voxel multiple regression, group-level repeated-measures ANOVA), reports coordinates and region tables, and presents within-group task contrasts (face vs control, encoding vs recognition, memory delay vs control). Participants are healthy adults. Results and methods are fully reported (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore it satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI task study of working memory (Sternberg variant), addressing executive function (access/evaluation in WM). It reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level random-effects analyses (paired t-tests across N=8) with coordinates and time-series, and includes within-group task contrasts (negative vs positive responses). Participants are a within-group healthy sample. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10.

This is an fMRI task-based study of numerical Stroop/conflict processing, which assesses cognitive control/inhibition and conflict resolution, matching executive function domains. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses (SPM2) with t and F contrasts and tables/coordinates for task contrasts (conflict vs nonconflict; error vs correct), satisfying within-group task contrasts. Participants are healthy adults; results are reported as standard voxelwise activation tables and figures. The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, allowing assessment of methods and group-level voxelwise findings. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study reports task-based fMRI of an executive function task (letter fluency) in ALS patients and controls, with whole-brain voxelwise group-level analyses and within-group task contrasts (task vs baseline). Results are reported as thresholded group maps and cluster coordinates in tables/figures. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is a PET study using a working memory (executive function) task, reporting voxelwise, whole-brain SPM analyses and within-group task contrasts (rest vs task and within-group comparisons across scans). The report includes group-level activation maps, statistical thresholds, and detailed methods/results (full text present). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria for a task-based executive-function neuroimaging meta-analysis. It is an fMRI study using a cognitive control/inhibition paradigm (counting Stroop). Group-level, voxelwise whole-brain mixed-effects analyses are reported (cluster-thresholded Z maps with peak coordinates reported in tables/figures). Crucially, within-group task contrasts (I–N Stroop contrast) are presented and contrasted between Trp and placebo conditions; results include whole-brain activation patterns and coordinates. The participant sample (healthy adults) is acceptable under I9. The paper is an empirical task-evoked fMRI study (not ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore include in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study that evaluates cognitive control demands of complex mental multiplication, which explicitly involves working memory, strategy planning, and executive demands. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses using SPM (one-sample t-tests; voxelwise p<0.001; cluster extent thresholds) and presents within-group task contrasts (e.g., untrained vs trained, trained vs untrained, and task vs number-matching control). Participants are healthy adults. Results are reported as tables/figures and described in text. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I5–I10) and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based modified Stroop paradigm (selective attention/inhibition), which falls within executive function domains. The paper reports voxelwise, group-level whole-brain analyses (SPM99; second-level random effects), with within-group contrasts of task versus rest for both healthy controls and schizophrenia patients. Results are presented as SPM maps and coordinate tables. Full article content (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical study; within-group contrasts are reported). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This fMRI study directly assesses an executive function (attention switching/cognitive flexibility within working memory) using task-based paradigms (verbal, visuospatial, combined). It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (one-sample t-tests vs rest; voxelwise ANOVAs; parametric High>Medium>Low switching contrasts) with cluster-correction, satisfying voxelwise whole-brain evidence. Within-group task contrasts are reported, and results are described in text and ROI/voxelwise maps; participants are healthy adults. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-group contrasts, empirical human neuroimaging data). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 are met and no exclusion criteria are violated.

This is an fMRI task study with group-level voxelwise contrasts, but the tasks probe semantic/autobiographic temporal-order and spatial-location memory retrieval rather than established executive-function domains. Although the authors discuss working-memory involvement, the primary manipulation targets episodic/semantic memory processes, not explicit executive functions (working memory paradigms like n-back, inhibition, task switching, planning, vigilance, or initiation). Therefore it does not meet I5 (study assessing executive function/cognitive control) nor I6 (tasks within established executive domains). The paper does satisfy voxelwise whole-brain analyses (I7), reports within-group task contrasts (I8), includes an acceptable participant group (I9), and reports coordinate and map results in text/figures (I10). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study of verbal working memory (an executive function domain) that reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise contrasts (structured vs. unstructured) with FDR-corrected thresholds and tables/figures. A within-group task contrast is reported for healthy adult participants. The methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria relevant to the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract provided). From the abstract this is an empirical PET study of verbal working memory, so I5 (PET task-based study of executive function) and I6 (working memory task) are met, and the abstract indicates a control task suggesting a within-group task contrast (I8). However, I cannot verify that a group-level, voxelwise whole-brain statistical map was reported (I7) or that whole-brain results are available in coordinate/figure/table form as required (I10) because methods/results details are not provided. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Because key inclusion criteria (notably I7 and I10) cannot be confirmed from the incomplete full text, the study must be excluded pending access to the complete article.

Full text incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). From the abstract we can confirm: I5 (PET task-based study of executive function), I6 (working memory task), and I9 (clinical and control groups reported). However I7 (presence of whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps) and I8 (explicit within-group voxelwise task contrast reporting) cannot be verified from the abstract alone. No exclusion criteria are positively met based on available information. Because the full text is not available to confirm critical inclusion criteria I7 and I8, I must exclude this study pending full-text review.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (2-back), an executive function, reporting voxelwise within-group 2-back vs baseline contrasts and group-level activation maps (second-level SPM analyses). The full text includes methods, results, and discussion; coordinates and whole-brain activation patterns are provided and ROI time-series were extracted for SEM, but voxelwise activation results and within-group contrasts are explicitly reported. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for task, domain, voxelwise whole-brain analysis, within-group contrasts, and reporting format. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study of action planning that directly manipulates and tests planning processes (an executive domain listed in I6: planning). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses with cluster-level FWE correction and provides coordinates and statistical maps (I7, I10). Contrasts are within-subject/within-group (Final Goal vs Immediate Goal) and thus satisfy I8. Participants are a healthy volunteer group (I9). The study is empirical human neuroimaging (not ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical), so no exclusion criteria apply. Full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation using task-based Stroop paradigms that probe inhibitory/cognitive control processes (executive function). It reports within-group voxelwise contrasts (incongruent-minus-neutral and negative-minus-neutral) and group-level paired t-test maps derived from whole-brain voxelwise analyses (thresholded and cluster-corrected). Thus it provides task-evoked, within-group, voxelwise results suitable for pooling. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an event-related fMRI study of working memory (delayed-recognition), which falls squarely within executive function domains (working memory). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise maps (mapwise analyses, random-effects t-tests, cluster correction) and within-group task contrasts (task vs fixation; object vs spatial). Participants are a within-group healthy adult sample. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This empirical fMRI study investigates cued task switching (an executive-function cognitive flexibility paradigm) using a task-based design in healthy participants. The authors report group-level, voxelwise analyses (subject contrast maps followed by random-effects one-sample t-tests) to identify activations and define ROIs; they also report within-group task contrasts (e.g., switch > repeat, task conditions vs null events, and motor contrasts). Whole-brain voxelwise results were used to select ROIs, and the manuscript contains full methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5–I10 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical study). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using the counting Stroop (inhibition domain of executive function). The paper reports voxelwise, whole-brain random-effects analyses (incongruent > congruent contrast), presents within-group activation maps/tables/coordinates for both healthy and bipolar groups, and describes methods/results in full. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function whole-brain activation reporting. Sample size and medication status are noted as limitations but do not violate inclusion/exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical PET study using a task-based paradigm that explicitly manipulates working memory updating (an executive function). A within-group, group-level voxelwise contrast (variable target > fixed target) was computed using SPM95 and reported as statistical maps, tables of activations, and figures across the whole brain. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (not just abstract/metadata). Therefore it meets I5 (PET task-based study of executive function), I6 (working memory), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group analysis), I8 (within-group task contrast), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (results reported as coordinates/figures/text). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based PET study measuring brain activation during simultaneous interpreting, which involves verbal working memory and cognitive control processes. The study uses group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM96) and reports within-group contrasts (SI vs shadowing) comparing task against an active control, with results described in text and figures. Participants are a valid group (professional interpreters). All inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied, and no exclusion criteria apply. The provided full text includes background, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This is a task-based fMRI study of cognitive control/executive function using a task-switching (cognitive flexibility) paradigm. The full text reports group-level, voxelwise searchlight decoding analyses normalized to MNI space and subjected to second-level statistical tests across subjects (i.e., whole-brain voxelwise group maps). Within-group contrasts (decoding accuracy versus chance) are reported. Participants and methods are described in full (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an event-related fMRI study of working memory (executive function) with within-subject contrasts and healthy participants, but the imaging results are reported primarily as ROI-based analyses and beta-series connectivity; no group-level, voxelwise whole-brain statistical activation map (e.g., group voxelwise contrast or coordinate table) is presented. The paper defines functional ROIs from individual activation maps and reports group statistics on extracted ROI betas and correlations, which indicates absence of voxelwise group activation results required by I7. Therefore it fails I7 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only reporting).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based verbal working memory paradigm (working memory = executive function). It reports group-level, voxelwise activation contrasts (e.g., EAR > NO-MEMORY, EAR > EYE) with whole-brain analyses and cluster thresholds, and describes random-effects group statistics and β-series connectivity; coordinates and surface maps are reported. The contrasts are within-group task contrasts. Participant sample (healthy adults) is acceptable. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and should be included.

This study reports behavioral experimental testing of working memory in schizophrenia and schizoaffective patients but does not report any fMRI or PET data or voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (tasks are within the executive function domain—working memory). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (no fMRI/PET imaging study reported), I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise analyses or maps), I8 (no within-group voxelwise task activation contrast reported). Exclusion criteria met: E5 (the paper contains only group comparisons of behavioral performance and no within-group task activation contrasts/maps). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion) so fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore the study does not meet the meta-analysis requirements for imaging task activation maps and is excluded.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (target detection among faces), which falls within the executive function domain. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (voxel thresholds, Talairach coordinates, and reported activated regions), and presents within-group task contrasts (targets vs nonrepeated distracters; repeated distracters vs nonrepeated distracters). Participant sample (six healthy adults) is within-group and qualifies. Results are reported as voxel coordinates and described in text/figures. The provided full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so is sufficiently complete for screening. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical).
