Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and should be included in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based paradigm probing working memory (an established executive function domain). It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (random-effects second-level analyses) with thresholded statistical maps and tabulated coordinates, and includes within-group task contrasts (e.g., cue-related and switch vs. stay contrasts and main effects against implicit baseline). The full text contains methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study probing selection/cognitive control (free vs externally specified selection), which maps onto executive function processes. It reports voxelwise, group-level SPM analyses (random-effects second-level t-tests) with whole-brain results and tables/figures of activation peaks and SPM maps (including whole-brain family-wise error corrected results and coordinate tables). Multiple within-group task contrasts are reported (e.g., free selection vs external specification; FA−EA; FC−EC; action vs colour), satisfying the requirement for within-group task contrasts. The sample and methods are clearly described and the full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). All applicable inclusion criteria are satisfied (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based working memory paradigm (executive function domain) with voxelwise, whole-brain analyses reported using SPM2. The paper reports within-group task contrasts (task vs rest and separate encoding/maintenance/retrieval contrasts), describes voxelwise group-level statistical maps and thresholds, and provides regional activation results (figures/tables referenced). Partial-brain coverage (lower cerebellum/brainstem omitted) does not preclude inclusion because analyses were voxelwise. Participants include a clinical sample (schizophrenia), which is allowed. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study meets required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an event-related fMRI task study that directly examines cognitive control processes (ACC conflict detection, right DLPFC monitoring) during a two-alternative associative recognition task. It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM), including within-group task contrasts (Strong > Weak; Weak > Strong), with coordinates and figures. Participants are healthy adults and results are fully reported in methods, results, tables, and discussion. Although the primary paradigm is episodic associative recognition, the paper explicitly tests and interprets executive/cognitive control mechanisms (conflict monitoring, familiarity monitoring) — functions that fall within established executive domains (monitoring/inhibition/selective attention). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

Although this is an empirical fMRI study with whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses and within-group task contrasts (and reports results in figures/tables), the experimental paradigm is a spoken-word identification task in noise rather than an established executive-function/cognitive-control task. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I8 (within-group task contrasts/main effects reported), I9 (participant groups reported; within-group contrasts provided), I10 (whole-brain results presented in figures/tables). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 and I6 — the study does not assess executive function/cognitive control using a task designed in established executive domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation); although the authors discuss recruitment of attention/working-memory regions, the task is primarily perceptual/lexical (speech-in-noise) and not a canonical executive-function paradigm. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI task study of overt word-generation (language production) across sessions. It provides whole-brain, voxelwise within-group task contrasts (task vs baseline), includes mixed-effects/group-level maps, and reports results in the text. However, the tasks are language/word-generation paradigms, not established executive function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore it does not meet the review’s core eligibility for executive function tasks. Inclusion met: I7, I8, I9, I10. Inclusion not met: I5, I6. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that includes a sustained visual attention (vigilance) task alongside an episodic retrieval task. It meets I5 (fMRI task-based study of cognitive control/attention) and I6 (vigilance falls within the listed executive function domains). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses using SPM99 (I7), and presents within-group task contrasts (ER vs baseline, VA vs baseline, direct ER vs VA contrasts; I8). Participants are a within-group sample of healthy young adults (I9). Whole-brain results are reported in tables and figures and described in text (I10). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, and include within-group contrasts rather than only between-group effects. Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for a meta-analysis of executive function task activations (vigilance/sustained attention).

This is an event-related task-based fMRI study using pro- and anti-saccade tasks (anti-saccade involves inhibitory control, an established executive function). The paper reports voxelwise activation maps (localizer t-tests with cluster correction and Talairach coordinates) and extracts within-group contrasts/time courses (saccade vs fixation localizer; event-related analyses sorted by saccadic reaction time quartiles). Partial-brain acquisition (focused slices) was used but analyses were voxelwise and coordinates are reported. Thus the study meets I5 (task-based fMRI assessing executive/inhibitory control), I6 (inhibition domain via anti-saccade), I7 (voxelwise activation maps reported, with coordinates), I8 (within-group task contrasts/time-course analyses), I9 (healthy participant group qualifies), and I10 (whole-brain/voxelwise results presented as coordinates and figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a Continuous Performance Task (CPT), a vigilance/sustained-attention paradigm that falls within established executive function domains. The authors performed voxelwise, group-level GLM analyses (random-effects) and report CPT vs control within-group contrasts (t-maps) used to select frontal VOIs and to compare control and schizophrenia groups. Whole-brain (frontal mask) voxelwise analyses and group-level task-evoked statistical maps are described. The study is not ROI-only, is not limited to connectivity-only analyses, and includes within-group task contrasts for included groups (controls and patients). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all applicable inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a methods/empirical fMRI study using flashing checkerboard visual stimulation and simulations to compare modeling approaches. It does not assess executive function or cognitive control tasks (fails I5 and I6). The paper does include whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses and within-group task vs baseline contrasts (satisfies I7, I8), includes participant groups (I9) and reports results in text/figures (I10). No exclusion criteria are triggered. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study (AX-CPT variant) examining cognitive control/attentional set shifting and reward expectation. It reports within-group voxelwise whole-brain SPM analyses (FDR-corrected) and presents group-level task contrasts (reward expectancy, verbal/spatial bias, all-tasks-vs-rest) with coordinates and figures. The task falls within executive function domains (vigilance/monitoring, cognitive flexibility/attention control). Participants are healthy adults (within-group contrasts reported). Whole-brain results are reported in text, figures, and tables. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided, so full text is complete. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and violates no exclusion criteria (none of E3–E6).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (a core executive function). It reports voxelwise, whole-brain general linear model analyses (SPM2), group-level activation maps (delay-, encoding-, and retrieval-period effects) and stereotactic coordinates (Table 2; Figure 2). The within-group task contrasts (delay-period activity collapsed across conditions; main effect of task versus baseline and period-specific regressors) are explicitly reported for healthy participants. Participant groups (healthy young adults; also lesion patients for behavioral data) are acceptable. Results are presented as group voxelwise maps and coordinates, meeting the meta-analysis reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not a non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical PET study using a task-based 2-back verbal working memory paradigm (executive function). It reports group-level voxelwise SPM99 whole-brain analyses with coordinates and cluster statistics (BBR correlations with rCBF), and within-group task analyses (2-back vs reference and performance correlations). Results are reported as Talairach/MNI coordinates. All inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of mental rotation/visuo-spatial working memory (an executive function domain: working memory). It reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses using SPM2, including within-group task contrasts (mental rotation vs passive viewing; one-sample and paired t-tests). Results are presented as coordinates, tables and figures. Participants are healthy adults (women tested in two cycle phases, men once). The paper therefore satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, contains within-group activation contrasts).

This is an fMRI task study with full methods, within-group voxelwise contrasts and whole-brain random-effects analysis (meets I7, I8, I9, I10). However, the task is a smooth-pursuit oculomotor paradigm investigating visuomotor/predictive and attentional mechanisms rather than an executive function or cognitive-control task as defined by the review (does NOT meet I5 and I6). No exclusion criteria apply (no E3–E6). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study is excluded because it fails the required inclusion criteria I5 and I6 (not an executive-function task). Inclusion IDs met: I7, I8, I9, I10. Inclusion IDs not met: I5, I6. Exclusion IDs met: none ([]).

The study is excluded because the fMRI analysis was ROI-based (AROI parcellation) with average regional timecourses and AROI-level statistics, and no group-level voxelwise whole-brain task activation maps are reported. This meets exclusion criterion E3. Included criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI assessing executive function/inhibition), I6 (task falls within inhibition domain), I8 (within-group task contrasts: INT vs COV), I9 (adult participant group). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps reported), I10 (no whole-brain voxelwise results/coordinate tables provided). Because I7 is required by the review and E3 is triggered, the paper must be excluded.

This study reports task-based fMRI during an emotional Stroop task that requires inhibition/cognitive control (suppressing word meaning to name ink color), which falls within the executive function domain of inhibition. The paper includes group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (FEAT/FLAME, voxelwise contrasts with cluster-size correction via AlphaSim) and reports within-group contrasts (negative vs. neutral; positive vs. neutral; task vs. fixation) with coordinates and cluster descriptions. Participant groups are nonpatient undergraduates (acceptable per criteria). Results are presented as voxelwise maps and clusters/coordinates, meeting the requirement that whole-brain evidence may be reported in tables/figures/text. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore the study meets the review inclusion criteria and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study of antisaccade performance (response inhibition/volitional control), which falls within executive-function domains (inhibition). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses using SPM2 (standard antisaccade vs fixation and delayed-task contrasts), with coordinates, tables, and figures provided. At least one within-group task contrast is reported (standard antisaccade > fixation; SaccadeTask and DelayCondition ANOVAs), satisfying the requirement for task-evoked maps. Participants are healthy adults (within-group contrasts reported). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and references; core content is present. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; not connectivity-only; not only between-group contrasts; not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and should be included.

This is an fMRI, task-based study using a continuous performance task (CPT) probing vigilance/attentional modulation of motor function (an executive domain). The paper reports voxelwise whole-brain SPM2 analyses (task vs baseline and degraded vs non-degraded contrasts) with coordinate tables and psycho-physiological interaction analyses. At least one within-group task contrast is reported for participant groups. Partial slice coverage was used but analyses were voxelwise and whole-brain/ROI-masked as described, which satisfies the meta-analysis requirements. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and includes within-group activations). Full text is present (introduction, methods, results, discussion, refs).

This fMRI study directly investigates cognitive control/conflict monitoring (ACC, DLPFC) during a task-based moral judgment paradigm that requires inhibiting prepotent emotional responses (i.e., cognitive control/inhibition). It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (and ROI-restricted analyses), and within-group contrasts (high-RT vs low-RT personal trials; utilitarian vs nonutilitarian trials) with voxelwise thresholds and cluster corrections. Participants are a within-group sample of healthy adults. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, stimuli, fMRI acquisition, preprocessing, analysis), Results, and Discussion, so core article content is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an event-related fMRI study of visuospatial working memory (an executive function domain) reporting group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses and within-group contrasts (short vs long delay; main effect maps) for children, adolescents, and adults. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. The study therefore meets all inclusion criteria and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

The study reports task-based fMRI contrasting working memory and spatial attention within the same subjects. Working memory is an established executive function domain, and the abstract describes group-level voxelwise analyses (conjunction and double-subtraction) yielding whole-brain activations attributable to each task, indicating within-group task contrasts and whole-brain results reported in text/figures. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are apparent from the abstract. However, only the abstract/metadata were provided here (no full methods/results/discussion), so fulltext_incomplete is set to true; this reduces certainty. Inclusion criteria applied: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10. Exclusion criteria applied: none.

This is a task-based fMRI study examining a cognitive control strategy (“reality checking”) during anticipation of emotional stimuli. It meets I5: fMRI study assessing cognitive control. It meets I6: the task requires executive control/inhibition of anticipatory emotional responses (falls within executive function/cognitive control domain). It meets I7: whole-brain voxelwise group-level random-effects analyses are reported (voxelwise contrasts, cluster thresholds). It meets I8: within-group task contrasts are reported (negative vs neutral; unknown vs neutral). It meets I9: participant group (healthy adults) qualifies. It meets I10: whole-brain results are reported in tables and figures described in text. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is an empirical task-based fMRI investigation of cognitive control (flanker/ANT) in autism and neurotypical participants. It explicitly assesses executive/inhibitory control (I5,I6) using a task that manipulates congruency and arousal. Analyses report whole-brain, voxelwise procedures (group-averaged t-maps, FDR thresholds, random-effects contrasts) meeting whole-brain evidence requirements (I7). The paper includes within-group task contrasts (incongruent vs congruent and high- vs low-arousal conditions) and reports within-group activation maps and timecourses (I8). Clinical and control groups are included (I9). Whole-brain results are described in text/tables/figures (I10). The full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not limited to ROI-only analyses, not solely connectivity/resting-state, and within-group activation contrasts are reported. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

Although the study uses task-based fMRI of an executive function (working memory for order) and reports within-group task contrasts in healthy adults (I5, I6, I8, I9 satisfied), all reported analyses were conducted within predefined ROIs (four 12mm spheres) rather than as voxelwise, whole-brain group-level maps. The paper does not present voxelwise whole-brain activation results or coordinates/tables for a whole-brain contrast, so it fails inclusion criterion I7 and therefore meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses with no voxelwise results). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study that includes a within-group, task-evoked contrast for an executive function task (n-back working memory). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain maps (thresholded group t-maps, ROI tables and figures), and contrasts (1-2-3 back > ‘look for X’ baseline and sustained attention > fixation). Participants are healthy adults (acceptable). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive function in which participants performed two executive tasks (random generation and an alphabet SO/SI task). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise SPM analyses (with coordinates and thresholding), and presents within-group task contrasts (Random vs Baseline; SI vs SO) for participant groups. Results are reported as voxelwise activations with coordinates in the text/tables and include both clinical (ASD) and control groups. Full article sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for task-based whole-brain activation meta-analysis (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract provided). The study is a task-based PET study of sustained attention (degraded stimulus CPT) so it meets I5 (PET task-based), I6 (task domain: vigilance/sustained attention), and I9 (reports within-group results for participant groups). However, the available content does not provide evidence of whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps (I7) nor a clear within-group task activation contrast (I8); reporting appears to focus on regional correlations of glucose metabolism with performance and may reflect ROI-based analyses, but this cannot be confirmed from the abstract alone. I10 (acceptable whole-brain result reporting) also cannot be verified. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) can be confirmed from the provided text. Full text incomplete, so cannot ascertain necessary criteria; therefore excluded pending full-text availability.

This is a task-based PET study of sustained attention/vigilance and selective target detection (executive domains). The full text reports group-level, voxelwise SPM analyses with thresholded statistical maps and MNI/atlas coordinates for whole-brain results (e.g., Z values and x,y,z locations). Within-group contrasts are reported (S vs NS, time-on-task covariate, interaction analyses), and behavioural/voxelwise results are described for the healthy participant group. The paper includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and violates none.

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). Based on available information: I5 (fMRI study) is satisfied; I6 (tasks involve phonological rehearsal/working-memory processes) is likely satisfied; I9 (participant group reported) is satisfied. However I7 (presence of a group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task activation map) cannot be confirmed from the abstract, I8 (a within-group task contrast reported) cannot be confirmed, and I10 (clear whole-brain results reporting such as coordinates/figures) cannot be confirmed. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Because key inclusion criteria cannot be verified from the incomplete full text, the study is excluded pending access to the full article.

This is a PET task-based study of visual working memory (executive function) reporting within-group contrasts for controls and JME patients. However, the analyses are region-of-interest (ROI) based (87-region template, rMRGlc, discriminant and factor analyses) rather than voxelwise whole-brain group-level statistical maps or coordinate tables. No voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps or coordinates are reported. Therefore the study violates exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses) and does not meet inclusion criterion I7 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain results). It does meet I5 (PET task-based study), I6 (working memory task), I8 (within-group task contrasts), and I9 (clinical participant groups). I10 (acceptable reporting formats for whole-brain results) is not satisfied because no whole-brain voxelwise results or coordinate tables/figures are provided. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI task-based study of task switching (cognitive flexibility), meeting I5 and I6. The abstract reports whole-brain activations and group contrasts (main effects of predictability and task switching vs performing each task separately), consistent with voxelwise group-level task-evoked maps (I7) and within-group task contrasts (I8). Participant group is acceptable (I9) and results are reported in the text (I10). No exclusion criteria are met: the study is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical. However, only title/abstract/metadata are provided here; the full article text (methods, full results, discussion, figures/tables) is not included, so fulltext_incomplete=true and confidence is moderate.

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). From the abstract the study used fMRI during gambling, working memory (two-back), and rest and correlated fMRI time series with skin conductance responses (SCR). This satisfies I5 (task-based fMRI) and I6 (includes a working memory executive task). However, the abstract does not report any group-level, voxelwise task-evoked statistical map or a within-group task contrast (e.g., task > baseline or 2-back > baseline), so it does not meet I7 or I8. No explicit exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are clearly met based on the available text, but the absence of evidence for within-group voxelwise task contrasts prevents inclusion. Because the provided full text is incomplete, firm determination is limited.

This is an event-related fMRI study of saccadic inhibition (antisaccade and fixation vs prosaccade), an established executive function domain (inhibition). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level statistical maps (t maps) and voxelwise analyses with Bonferroni-corrected thresholds, and provides within-group task contrasts (inhibition vs prosaccade and main effects) for both controls and patients, including activation maps and coordinates. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and empirical). Therefore it meets I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 and should be included.

Full text unavailable (API error in provided content). Cannot verify any required methodological details. Exclusion IDs met: none (insufficient information to apply E3–E6). Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met (unable to confirm from incomplete full text): I5 (fMRI/PET task-based executive function), I6 (task within executive domains), I7 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain analysis), I8 (within-group task contrast), I9 (participant groups acceptable), I10 (whole-brain results reported clearly). Because the full text is incomplete, the study cannot be confirmed to meet all inclusion criteria; therefore excluded pending retrieval of the complete article.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that parametrically manipulates working-memory demands during a grammaticality-judgment task. It directly assesses working memory (an established executive function domain) and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (group maps, cluster thresholds, MNI coordinates). Within-group task contrasts and linear-effect contrasts (distance effects within Movement and Binding conditions; grammatical trials versus baseline) are reported. Participants are healthy adults. Results and analyses (methods, results, discussion) are fully present in the provided full text. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete.

This paper is excluded because it reports only connectivity/coherence analyses (functional connectivity) without reporting any group-level, voxelwise task-evoked activation contrast (Exclusion E4). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI study of working memory/executive function), I6 (working memory task falls within executive domains), I9 (within-group task was performed on a participant group). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical map is reported), I8 (no within-group task activation contrast against baseline or control is presented in the current report). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The abstract and metadata indicate an empirical task-based fMRI study of spatial working memory (an executive function domain). The text describes voxelwise analyses ("response characteristics of the individual voxels") and condition-related modulations of activation, implying within-group task contrasts and group-level task-evoked maps. Therefore the study appears to meet inclusion criteria for fMRI task activation (I5), working memory domain (I6), voxelwise whole-brain analysis (I7), within-group contrasts (I8), and permissive participant groups (I9). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met based on the available information. However, the provided content is incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata present) so I set fulltext_incomplete=true — full text should be retrieved to confirm the presence of voxelwise group-level statistical maps, exact contrasts, and reporting format (e.g., coordinates/figures).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive function (attention switching within verbal working memory). It reports group-level voxelwise analyses (one-sample t-tests and a voxelwise ANOVA across switching frequency) with whole-brain coverage and Talairach-space localization; task activation maps and cluster tables are provided. Within-group contrasts are reported (task vs rest and parametric modulation by switching frequency). Participants are a healthy adult sample. Reporting includes tables/figures of whole-brain results. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are violated. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (Sternberg paradigm) in schizophrenia reporting voxelwise, group-level activation maps (NT vs CT and task vs rest) with whole-brain correction and explicit ROI-derived voxelwise b-values. It contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (full text present). The study therefore meets I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (working memory = executive domain), I7 (voxelwise whole-brain analyses and group maps), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported), I9 (clinical participant group acceptable), and I10 (whole-brain results described in text/figures). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not connectivity-only; within-group contrasts are reported; empirical human neuroimaging data present).

This is a task-based fMRI study of a numerical Stroop (number-size congruity) task that probes interference/inhibition and attentional control (executive function). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (e.g., incongruent > congruent, distance effects) with tables of coordinates and figures, and within-group contrasts versus baseline and between conditions. Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures descriptions) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

The paper reports task-based fMRI (N-Back working memory) in healthy humans with whole-brain, group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses (2-Back > 0-Back). Within-group task contrasts and main effects of task are reported, and genotype-based group comparisons are secondary. Voxelwise results and regional activations (including striatum and prefrontal cortex) are described in the text and supplementary tables/figures. Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria for executive-function task fMRI with whole-brain, within-group voxelwise maps and meets no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a modified emotional Stroop paradigm that probes cognitive control/inhibition over emotional interference (an executive function). The paper reports within-group voxelwise contrasts (emotional incongruence vs congruence) with voxelwise one-sample t-tests and cluster thresholds, and provides regional results (Table 1, figures) for both healthy controls and patients with schizophrenia. Thus it supplies whole-brain, group-level task-evoked statistical maps (voxelwise analyses) and within-group contrasts for participant groups, meeting all inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an event-related fMRI empirical study using a task-based paradigm that probes cognitive control processes (go/no-go inhibition, response-selection, conflict/facilitation). It reports group-level, voxelwise random-effects SPM analyses (whole-brain contrasts with coordinates and thresholding) and multiple within-group contrasts (e.g., incompatible vs. neutral, effect tones vs. neutral). Participants are healthy adults; results are reported as coordinates, figures, and tables. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided. Thus all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an event-related fMRI study of spatial working memory (an executive function domain). The study reports voxelwise whole-brain activation analyses with statistical thresholds and peak coordinates (tables/figures and t statistics), and performs within-group contrasts (memory maintenance vs equivalent nonmemory control; selection vs control). Participants are human and results are reported as coordinates and time courses. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, enabling assessment of analyses. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that reports whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses of task contrasts relevant to cognitive control/conflict processing. The experiment required synesthetes to perform a speeded response (button press) indicating synesthetic experience and includes within-group contrasts (e.g., C− S+ > C− S−; interaction contrasts) that reveal activation in DLPFC associated with perceptual conflict and supervisory cognitive control. Whole-brain fixed- and random-effects SPM analyses are reported with stereotactic coordinates in tables and figures. Participants are a defined group (grapheme-color synesthetes), which is acceptable. The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion (not truncated). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and is suitable for inclusion in a meta-analysis of executive function/task activations that pools across participant groups.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (two-back), which is an executive function domain. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM99) with thresholding and conjunction/cognitive-subtraction contrasts (WM minus reference) for within-group task effects. Behavioral and imaging methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. Participants are healthy adults. Results are reported in text, tables and figures. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, not a non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

Full text incomplete: only title/abstract/metadata provided. Abstract confirms a task-based fMRI study of working memory in younger and older adults, satisfying I5 (fMRI task-based) and I6 (working memory, an executive function) and I9 (participant groups acceptable). However, the provided content does not allow verification of I7 (presence of whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps) or I8 (explicit within-group task contrast reporting). I10 (reporting format for whole-brain results) cannot be confirmed. No exclusion criteria (E3-E6) are clearly met from the available content. Because essential inclusion criteria (I7 and I8) cannot be confirmed from the incomplete full text, exclude pending access to the complete article.

Full text content provided is limited to title, abstract, and metadata only (fulltext_incomplete=true). From the abstract the study is an empirical PET task study of working memory in schizophrenia, meeting I5 (PET task-based), I6 (working memory task), I8 (within-group task vs fixation contrast), and I9 (clinical and control groups). However, the full text is not available to confirm critical inclusion criterion I7 (that at least one group-level voxelwise whole-brain statistical map/analysis was reported) or I10 (format of whole-brain results). Because I7 cannot be verified from the abstract alone and the review requires explicit whole-brain voxelwise results, I cannot confirm all required inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria (E3-E6) are clearly met from the abstract. Therefore I must exclude due to incomplete full text and inability to confirm whole-brain voxelwise analyses.

This study reports task-based fMRI during an N-back working memory task (an established executive function domain). The paper describes voxelwise SPM analyses of BOLD activation (2B vs 0B contrast), generation of subject contrast maps and group-level analyses, and reports peak coordinates and statistics for genotype effects on task-related activation in prefrontal cortex. A within-group task contrast (2-back vs 0-back) is explicitly used; results are reported as voxelwise activation loci (with correction within an ROI but obtained from voxelwise SPM analyses) and coordinates are provided in the text and figure. Participants include healthy controls (and clinical samples elsewhere), and the within-group contrast in controls qualifies. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. The full-text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a Stroop task (inhibition/interference), which falls within executive function domains. The study reports voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM) with random-effects group-level contrasts and provides coordinates and cluster results. Within-group task contrasts are reported for patients (task vs control/interference vs control) and for controls, and pre/post within-patient contrasts are also presented. Participant sample (clinical OCD and healthy controls) is acceptable per criteria. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures) is provided, allowing extraction of whole-brain task activation coordinates. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of cognitive control/executive function (letter vs visuospatial decision tasks) in healthy participants. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level contrasts with coordinates and corrected statistics (task vs baseline and task vs task), satisfying within-group task contrasts. Tasks probe executive processes (response selection, inhibition, conflict monitoring), and results are reported as coordinates/figures. No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and it is empirical neuroimaging research. Full text appears to include introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (syllable working memory) in healthy Japanese adults. It assesses an executive function domain (working memory) using block-designed task contrasts and reports within-group voxelwise analyses (task vs rest and l/r vs b/n or d/n) using SPM99, with activation maps and coordinate tables provided. Thus it provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked results. All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion, figures/tables, references).

This fMRI study reports within-group, voxelwise task contrasts (game > dot, game > scene, game > random) assessing working memory and recognition tasks in chess players — the game > dot contrast isolates working-memory/executive processes. Whole-brain images were acquired and SPM99 voxelwise group-level maps (corrected p<.05) and activation foci are reported. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis requirements for task-based fMRI of executive function with whole-brain, within-group voxelwise contrasts. Although the group analysis used a fixed-effects model and the sample is small (n=5), the inclusion criteria do not exclude fixed-effects or small samples. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using verbal and non-verbal working memory tasks (executive function domain: working memory). The paper reports within-group, voxelwise working-memory versus baseline contrasts, group-level whole-brain t maps, voxelwise regression with PCS scores, and VOI analyses. Participants include concussed athletes and control athletes (clinical and healthy groups). Whole-brain, group-level statistical maps are described and displayed; analyses are voxelwise rather than ROI-only. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10), and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM) and coordinates, including within-group contrasts (main effect of condition, main effect of velocity, regression analyses). Although the primary paradigm probes smooth pursuit eye movements, the contrast of target blanking versus continuous presentation was explicitly designed to engage extraretinal mechanisms such as prediction, monitoring and short-/mid-term spatial working memory (DLPFC, angular gyrus)—functions within established executive domains (working memory/monitoring). Participants were healthy adults and results are reported as group-level voxelwise maps with tables of coordinates. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10 and should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI task-based study of verbal working memory (an executive function domain). It reports within-group, voxelwise, group-level whole-brain analyses (e.g., maintenance vs control; words vs pseudowords; 5 vs 2 load), including random-effects one-sample t tests and whole-brain functional connectivity, and provides sufficient methods, results, and discussion in the full text. Participants are a within-group healthy sample. Reporting includes voxelwise maps and contrasts described in text and supplemental materials. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive function (working memory span/dual-task coordination) with healthy adult participants. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise SPM analyses (random-effects group analyses and t-tests), within-group task contrasts (e.g., Read+Remember vs Read; Read+Remember vs Remember), and reports whole-brain activations with coordinates and tables. Although slice coverage is limited in Experiment 1, the analyses are voxelwise and whole-brain contrasts are presented; results are reported in text, figures, and coordinate tables. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using a modified Wisconsin Card Sorting Test (set-shifting) that targets cognitive flexibility — an executive function. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (SPM99 random-effects GLM) with multiple within-group task contrasts (e.g., A minus D, A minus B, B minus C) and provides Talairach/MNI coordinates and statistical maps. Participants are a within-group healthy adult sample. Reporting includes tables, figures, methods, results, and discussion, satisfying whole-text completeness. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for pooling executive-function task activations.

This fMRI study includes a classic executive-function task (Stroop; inhibition domain) and a task-based moral-dilemma paradigm. Group-level, voxelwise analyses are reported (ICA-derived spatial maps, voxelwise paired-samples t tests, and tables of coordinates/cluster statistics are provided), and within-group task contrasts (task vs rest/fixation and task-condition contrasts) are described. Whole-brain voxelwise results and coordinates are reported in tables and supplemental materials. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function fMRI (within-group contrasts, whole-brain voxelwise maps, coordinates). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of executive function/cognitive control (time-estimation feedback and Stroop tasks). It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (contrasts such as incongruent>congruent and errors>correct in the Stroop task; feedback contrasts in the time-estimation task) with figures/tables, and at least one within-group task contrast. Participant group is healthy adults (within-group contrasts reported). Although slice coverage was limited to 28 slices, analyses were voxelwise (partial-brain acquisition still qualifies). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function domain) with distraction, using an event-related design. It reports within-group, voxelwise random-effects analyses for adults and children (main-effect 1-sample t-tests on contrast images), whole-brain corrected results, and provides coordinate tables and figures. The task contrast includes WM vs control and distraction vs delay (within-group contrasts). Participants include developmental and adult samples. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; thus fulltext_incomplete is false. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10. Exclusion criteria applied: [].

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of spatial working memory (an established executive function domain) that reports within-group, voxelwise, group-level (random-effects) task contrasts (e.g. Space>NonSpace; AlloSpace–EgoSpace) using whole-brain SPM2 analyses with FDR correction and MNI coordinates/figures. Participants are a within-group healthy sample. Whole- brain results are reported in text, tables and figures. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, not non-empirical). Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present. Therefore it meets I5–I10 and none of E3–E6.

This is an fMRI task-based study of working memory (Sternberg task) in healthy adults that reports whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level activation contrasts. The paper presents within-group contrasts (e.g., average encoding vs implicit baseline; load-dependent linear contrasts) tested with random-effects one-sample t-tests and reports whole-brain corrected results (tables and surface renderings). Methods, results, and discussion are present in full text. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for task-based executive function (working memory) fMRI, whole-brain voxelwise analysis, and within-group contrasts. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using a GO–NOGO paradigm that assesses action planning and response selection/inhibition — an established executive function domain (inhibition). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain random-effects GLM contrasts (e.g., NOGO vs GO) with coordinate tables and contrast images, satisfying voxelwise reporting even though Experiment 2 used reduced slice coverage. Within-group task contrasts are explicitly reported. Participants are neurologically healthy adults. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10) and none of the exclusion criteria.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). The study used whole-brain fMRI and reports within-group, voxelwise parametric task contrasts, but the task (attending to and predicting target motion) does not clearly fall within the meta-analysis' defined executive function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criteria I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met based on available information. Confidence moderate due to incomplete full text; a full article could clarify whether the task was framed as an executive/planning task.

This is an event-related fMRI study that directly assesses planning and initiation of motor sequences—domains classified under executive function (planning, initiation). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (voxel-wise ANOVAs, HRF estimates, Talairach coordinates) with results presented in tables and figures. Within-group task contrasts are reported (IG vs EG, premovement vs movement, complexity effects; main effects vs baseline), and healthy volunteers are the participant group. Whole-brain voxelwise results are reported as coordinates/ROIs. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical). The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References, so the full text appears complete. Therefore, the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical PET study using a task-based PASAT that targets working memory/attention (executive function). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise SPM analyses (whole-brain), corrected p-values, and within-group contrasts (PASAT vs rest; parsed contrasts like repeat prior vs repeat immediate). Results are reported as SPM maps and tabulated coordinates. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so it is complete for screening. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and violates no exclusion criteria. Study is appropriate for inclusion in a meta-analysis of executive-function task activations.

The study reports task-based fMRI with simultaneous EEG during a mental arithmetic task designed to induce working memory load (an executive function). It includes within-group, voxelwise group-level SPM analyses contrasting mental arithmetic vs reference, and reports whole-brain voxelwise results with coordinates and multiple comparison correction (FWE/FDR). Although acquisition used 20 slices, the analysis was voxelwise at the group level, which meets the allowance for partial-brain acquisition. Participant sample (healthy adults) is acceptable. The full text provided contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Conclusions. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is an fMRI task-based investigation and reports group-level, voxelwise within-group contrasts (test vs control) with whole-brain results (p<0.001 FWE), satisfying I7, I8, I9, and I10. However, the experimental task is the Word Memory Test (delayed recognition), an episodic verbal memory/symptom validity task rather than a canonical executive function or cognitive-control task (e.g., working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore it does not meet I5 (study assessing executive function or cognitive control) nor I6 (task falls within established executive function domains). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI task-based study of mental arithmetic that explicitly manipulates task complexity to tax working memory. It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (complex vs. simple) using SPM2 with FDR correction and presents conjunction and contrast results in tables and figures. The within-group contrasts (complex > simple for each operator) are reported and used in group-level analyses. Tasks target working memory/executive demands (explicitly discussed) and thus fall within the executive function domain. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based PET study of spatial working memory (executive function). It reports group-level, voxelwise SPM analyses (ANCOVA) and both a priori search volumes and an exploratory whole-brain search with corrected thresholds; results are presented as stereotaxic coordinates and subtraction contrasts. Within-group task contrasts are reported (spatial span vs visuomotor control; spatial manipulation vs control; spatial manipulation vs span). Participants are a within-group sample of healthy adults (n=5). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion sections. Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10, and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a 2-back working memory paradigm (executive function domain). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise analyses (surface- and volume-based t tests, Fourier analysis) and presents whole-brain/whole-head coverage for group analyses (n=12 for whole-head), with task-versus-passive and identity-vs-location within-group contrasts and group maps/figures/tables. Results include voxelwise statistical maps and ROI and group-average analyses, satisfying requirements for within-group task contrasts and whole-brain voxelwise maps. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply: analyses are not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, and include within-group contrasts and original empirical data. Full text is complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and is included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based spatial working memory paradigm (executive function) with both patients and healthy controls. The manuscript reports group-level voxelwise signal-change maps and composite t-maps comparing task vs baseline (within-group contrasts), satisfying the whole-brain/voxelwise requirement. The full text includes introduction, methods (imaging acquisition, preprocessing, group t-maps), results, and discussion, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical).

Full text as provided appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata). The abstract indicates an fMRI Stroop task (I5) and that the Stroop task falls within executive function (inhibition) (I6), so those criteria are met. However, the manuscript content needed to confirm other required items is missing: there is no accessible methods/results to verify whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked maps (I7), whether at least one within-group task contrast is reported for any group (I8), or whether whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures (I10). Because the full article text (methods, results) is not present, I cannot confirm these inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) can be confidently applied from the abstract alone. Therefore I must exclude on the basis of incomplete/full-text unavailability and inability to confirm required inclusion criteria (I7, I8, I9, I10). If the full article text/methods are provided, screening could be revisited.

This is an empirical PET study that uses task-based paradigms targeting working memory (an established executive function domain). The study reports group-level, voxelwise SPM analyses with whole-brain results and Talairach/MNI coordinates, and presents within-group task contrasts (e.g., WM vs SC, WM vs BL, sign vs speech) suitable for voxelwise activation mapping. Participants are a defined group (early bilingual sign–speech interpreters), and results are reported in tables/figures with coordinates. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion and conclusions, so full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of attentional control (Stroop-like interference), which falls within executive function domains (inhibition/selection). The paper reports within-group, voxelwise group random-effects analyses (interference vs control) and presents whole-brain results in text, figures, and tables. Although slice coverage was limited (15 slices), analyses were voxelwise rather than ROI-restricted, satisfying partial-brain allowance. Participants are a within-group healthy adult sample. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10). No exclusion criteria are triggered (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical study). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI task study with within-group contrasts of selection (select 10/30 > 70/90) in adolescents and adults and targets cognitive-control regions. However, the main analyses were restricted to a priori anatomical ROIs with small-volume correction (3 mm spheres) and voxelwise tests only within those ROIs. The paper does not report a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map; results are ROI/SVC-based. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I7 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI/SVC-only reporting). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (task probes cognitive control/conflict monitoring), I8 (within-group contrasts reported), I9 (participant groups acceptable). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group map).

This fMRI study used task-based contrasts (Magic vs Causal Control; Surprise vs Causal Control) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses, but the experimental task (passive viewing/perception of magic tricks and surprise events) does not fall within the prespecified established executive function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Although the authors interpret activations in ACC and DLPFC in terms of conflict detection and cognitive-control processes, the paradigm is primarily perceptual/causality-violation rather than an established executive-function task. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI, cognitive-control-related investigation), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported), I9 (appropriate participant group reported), I10 (whole-brain results presented in text/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (task does not map to listed executive function domains). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study that used a task-based go–nogo paradigm (inhibition domain of executive function). It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (FSL FLAME mixed-effects, cluster-thresholded Z images) and within-group contrasts (go vs nogo, compatibility interactions). Participant sample (healthy adults) is acceptable. Results (voxelwise activations) are described in text and tables/figures. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (image acquisition, preprocessing, first- and second-level analyses), Results, and Discussion. Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function activation mapping and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of attentional control (Stroop), which falls within executive function/inhibition. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise statistical analyses (voxel-wise repeated-measures ANOVA and blocked voxelwise maps converted to Z-scores) and provides whole-brain activation results (tables of Talairach coordinates and figures). Within-group task contrasts are reported (incongruent vs. neutral; incongruent-eligible vs. incongruent-ineligible), and participants are healthy adults. Although acquisition used limited slices (partial-brain coverage), the study performed voxelwise group analyses and reported whole-brain-style results, which meets the review’s allowance for partial-brain acquisitions so long as voxelwise analyses are presented. Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study of sustained attention (vigilance), which falls within executive function domains. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise SPM analyses and within-group task contrasts (novel and practice blocks vs. baseline) for both cocaine and control groups. Methods, results, and group- and within-group activation maps/analyses are reported, satisfying the meta-analysis inclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that explicitly manipulates working memory load (an established executive function) and reports group-level, voxelwise random-effects GLM analyses. The paper used whole-brain EPI coverage, conducted within-group contrasts (e.g. high vs low memory/attention load; same-side vs opposite-side visuo-tactile effects), and reports results in text, figures, and tables. Participants are healthy adults. No exclusion criteria apply: the study is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical. The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete for screening purposes.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study examining working memory (n-back), an established executive function domain. The paper reports group-level voxelwise contrasts (2-back vs 0-back) and second-level ANOVA trend analyses across sessions, fulfilling the requirement for within-group task activation maps. Although the acquisition used 15 slices (partial coverage), the analyses were voxelwise at the group level, which satisfies the meta-analysis' allowance for partial-brain voxelwise analyses. Results are described in the text and figures. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, and is empirical).

This is an fMRI task-based study using n-back working memory paradigms (verbal and spatial), which are established executive function tasks. It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain mixed-effects analyses (2-back > 0-back; verbal > spatial), with cluster-corrected statistical maps and tables of peak coordinates. Within-group task contrasts are presented for the healthy control group (behavioral and imaging results), and results are reported in figures/tables in the full text. The sample, methods, and results (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are fully provided. No exclusion criteria are met.

Full text provided appears to be only title/abstract and lacks methods, results, and detailed analyses (fulltext_incomplete=true). Based on the abstract, the paper is an fMRI study of visual working memory (meets I5 and I6). However, I cannot confirm that the paper reports a group-level voxelwise whole-brain task activation map (I7), nor can I verify that it reports a within-group task contrast (I8) or that qualifying whole-brain results are reported clearly (I10). Because the full text is incomplete and key inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed, I must exclude the study pending a complete full text. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met from the available content.

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study of reversal learning, which assesses cognitive flexibility/affective switching — an executive function domain. The study reports within-group, group-level random-effects voxelwise contrasts (e.g., CR > BL, PENS+PRE > BL, FRE > BL, FRE > PENS+PRE) analyzed with SPM2 and reports whole-brain results with MNI coordinates in tables/figures. Participants are healthy volunteers and within-group contrasts are provided. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an event-related fMRI study using a task of executive function (Simon task; cognitive interference/inhibition) in older adults. The paper reports within-group, voxelwise group-level contrasts (incongruent > congruent) with voxel- and cluster-level thresholds and tables/clusters of coordinates (whole-brain analysis). Therefore it satisfies I5 (fMRI task-based executive function), I6 (inhibition domain), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group analyses), I8 (within-group task contrast), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; fulltext is complete.

This is an event-related fMRI study of visuo-spatial working memory (an executive function: working memory). The paper reports voxelwise, group-level SPM analyses (fixed- and random-effects), within-group task contrasts (various task vs. grid/no-grid conditions and baseline), and presents group statistical maps/tables/figures. Although coverage was partial (parieto-frontal and occipito-temporo-frontal scans), analyses were voxelwise at the group level, satisfying partial-brain requirements. The full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (working memory), I7 (voxelwise group maps; partial coverage acceptable), I8 (within-group contrasts), I9 (participant group reported), and I10 (results reported in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (2-back), an established executive function domain. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain second-level analyses (one-sample and two-sample SPM99 t-tests) with voxelwise thresholds and cluster corrections and provides coordinate tables. Within-group contrasts are reported (load effects: [2-back>0-back] for verbal and spatial sessions) for both patient and control groups. Participants include clinical (schizophrenia) and control samples. Thus it satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10 and violates no exclusion criteria (E3–E6). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using the 2-back working memory task (an executive function). The paper reports group-level voxelwise SPM analyses (whole-brain maps are shown and used to define ROIs), and reports within-group task contrasts (main effect of 2-back vs baseline combined across subjects and subject-specific contrasts entered into second-level models). Participants include clinical (de novo, unmedicated Parkinson's) and control groups but a within-group/combined-group task activation map is provided. All inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This fMRI study tests working memory/binding tasks (meets I5, I6), reports within-group task contrasts (I8), includes an eligible participant group (I9), and reports results in text/figures/coordinates (I10). However, the authors explicitly state they ‘used the clusters of activation found in that study as a mask, applying those regions of interest…’ and computed ROI-based percentage signal change for planned comparisons rather than reporting group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-activation maps. Thus it does not provide voxelwise whole-brain activation results and qualifies as an ROI-only analysis, meeting exclusion E3. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I8, I9, I10. Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level task maps). Exclusion criteria applied: E3. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study that includes a task-based verbal working memory (VWM) paradigm (an executive function domain). Group-level, voxelwise task activation maps are reported (global whole-brain analysis and regional single-slice ROI analyses with thresholded correlation maps and across-subject paired tests), and within-group contrasts (task vs baseline/control) are used to generate activation maps. The paper contains full methods, results, and discussion, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met.

The manuscript reports task-based fMRI analyses of a working-memory (feature binding) task and voxelwise whole-brain statistics, but the results presented are focused on between-group comparisons (APOEε4+ vs APOEε4−). The full text does not report any within-group task activation contrasts (e.g., task>baseline) for either participant group, only the between-group t-tests. Therefore the study fails inclusion criterion I8 and meets exclusion E5 (reports only between-group contrasts with no within-group task activation contrast). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI task study), I6 (working memory — an executive function), I7 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses), I9 (participant group acceptable), I10 (results described in text/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I8 (no within-group task contrast reported). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based continuous performance (vigilance) paradigm, which falls within executive function domains. The paper reports voxelwise, whole-brain group-level analyses (within-group vigilance>fixation contrasts for both schizophrenia and healthy control groups) with cluster-correction and presents maps/tables of activations. Participants include clinical and control groups. All required inclusion criteria for task-based whole-brain within-group activation are met, and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion.

This is an fMRI, task-based, within-group voxelwise study reporting whole-brain contrasts and coordinates (meets I7, I8, I9, I10). However, the task is a long-term memory (face–name recognition) paradigm examining episodic vs semantic memory and retrieval processes, not an established executive function domain (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore it does not satisfy I5 (study assessing executive function/cognitive control task) and I6 (task within established executive function domains). Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study of voluntary self-regulation of slow cortical potentials (SCPs), which the authors interpret as involving cognitive control processes including active inhibition and preparatory attention. It therefore assesses executive/cognitive control (I5) and maps onto established executive domains (inhibition/initiative/attention) as discussed in the text (I6). The study reports whole-brain, voxelwise SPM analyses with both fixed- and random-effects group-level contrasts (I7), and includes within-group task contrasts (negativity vs baseline/passive viewing, positivity vs baseline, and negativity vs positivity) (I8). Participant groups include both healthy subjects and epilepsy patients with within-group contrasts reported (I9). Results are presented as tables/figures with coordinates and detailed descriptions (I10). The provided full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study of spatial working memory (an executive function domain). The paper reports group-level voxelwise analyses (Z-maps, FDR correction), one-sample t-tests and mixed-effect ANOVA for within-group contrasts (maintenance vs recognition; modality comparisons), and whole-brain results reported in text/maps. Participant group is healthy adults; within-group contrasts are provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study explicitly investigating cognitive control/conflict monitoring during recognition (rejecting novel objects in familiar contexts). It reports whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses (SPM2) with voxelwise NO>NN contrasts and reports peak coordinates and cluster results. The NO versus NN contrast is a within-group task contrast (examined within young and elderly and used to relate activation to performance), and group-level random-effects analyses are reported. Participants include healthy young and elderly adults. Reporting includes tables/coordinates and full methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical PET study with task-based manipulations that explicitly examine attentional/control (executive) processes in interaction with learning/memory. It reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain SPM analyses (thresholding, Talairach coordinates) and multiple within-group contrasts (NR-RS, TR-RS, NR-TR, interaction contrasts). The tasks engage executive components such as working memory/visuo-spatial sketchpad, initiation, monitoring, response selection, and top-down attentional control (PFC, ACC, PPC activations discussed), mapping onto the review’s executive domains (notably working memory and initiation/planning/monitoring). Participants are a within-group healthy adult sample. Results are reported as voxelwise maps and coordinate tables. No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and within-group contrasts are present. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study reporting group-level voxelwise activation maps for task contrasts (block localizers and event-related gap and memory-delay contrasts). The memory-delay paradigm involves holding spatial information over a delay (working memory) and the gap paradigm probes preparatory/ initiation processes; both fall within executive-function domains (working memory, initiation/planning). Whole-brain voxelwise analyses and corrected statistical maps are reported; partial-slice coverage is allowed per criteria and voxelwise analyses were used. Within-group task contrasts (saccade/pointing vs fixation; memory-delay/gap durations) are presented. Participant group is healthy adults and results are reported as voxelwise maps and timecourses. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided and appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of spatial working memory (an executive function) in heavy cannabis users and controls. Methods describe whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM99 (realignment, normalization, smoothing) with voxelwise one-sample and two-sample t-tests and subtraction contrasts. The paper reports within-group contrasts (short-delay task minus perception) for both controls and cannabis users, and between-group contrasts; results are described in tables/figures. Partial-brain coverage (frontal cortex and parts of temporal/parietal lobes, excluding cerebellum) is explicitly stated but voxelwise analyses were performed, which satisfies the allowance for partial-brain acquisition. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, within-group contrasts present, and empirical human imaging data). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references, so fulltext appears complete.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). From the abstract, the study is an event-related fMRI investigation of working memory/elaborative rehearsal (meets I5 and I6). However, the provided content does not allow confirmation that group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps were reported (I7 cannot be verified). It is also not possible to definitively confirm that a within-group task contrast (group-level voxelwise contrast) is reported in the available text (I8 cannot be verified), even though the abstract describes task-related activations. Because key inclusion criteria (I7 and I8) cannot be confirmed from the incomplete full text, I must exclude the study pending access to the complete article.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a 2-back working memory task (an executive function domain). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise GLM analyses and presents group t-maps and voxelwise comparisons; within-group task contrasts (2-back vs baseline) are reported for both patients and controls.
