Participants include clinical and control groups. Results are reported in figures and text. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5–I10. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. The provided full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

Full text incomplete; only abstract/metadata available. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met (based on abstract): I5 (PET, task-based paradigm assessing brain activation), I8 (within-group contrasts reported: rest vs movement and sequence length effects), I9 (participant group reported; within-group contrasts present). Inclusion IDs not met / cannot confirm due to missing full text: I6 (uncertain whether the finger-sequence task was intended as an executive-function task within established domains — authors suggest involvement of spatial working memory but task may be primarily motor), I7 (cannot confirm that at least one group-level, voxelwise whole-brain statistical map/analysis is reported), I10 (unable to verify the format of whole-brain results e.g., coordinates/voxelwise maps). Because core methods/results are not available, I cannot verify all required inclusion criteria; therefore exclude pending full-text review.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (an established executive function domain). The paper reports within-group, voxelwise group-level contrasts (NT vs CT) with whole-brain statistical maps (Z-statistics), cluster results, and a table of coordinates for activated regions. The methods describe preprocessing, normalization to MNI space, and group analyses; figures and Table 1 provide whole-brain activation details. Participants are healthy adults (acceptable). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for executive-function task activations and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and reports within-group contrasts). Full text is complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The article reports an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (N-back), an executive function. It includes whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (2-Back > 0-Back) using random-effects SPM99 and reports peak coordinates and statistics for task activations. A within-group task contrast is explicitly reported and used for genotype-based regression analyses. Results are presented across the working memory cortical network with coordinates and effect sizes. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; supplemental material is noted but not required. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based visuo-spatial working memory paradigm (executive function domain). The paper reports voxelwise, group-level GLM analyses (SPM2) contrasting delay-phase versus control and uses the simulated BOLD as a covariate to identify brain regions; results are reported as cluster-corrected whole-brain activations with stereotaxic coordinates. Thus it provides within-group task contrasts and whole-brain voxelwise results suitable for pooling. Full text includes background, methods (fMRI acquisition and voxelwise analysis), results and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical).

This is a task-based, within-group fMRI study examining working memory and prospective memory (executive function domains). It reports whole-brain, voxelwise, random-effects group analyses and multiple within-group contrasts (e.g., PM-1Back vs NB-1Back; NB-3Back vs NB-1Back). Results are presented in-text with ROIs, figures, and tables. The full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5–I10 and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

Exclusion E3 met: the study reports primarily ROI-based analyses (FFA, PPA, dorsolateral PFC) with beta values averaged within ROIs and ANOVAs on those ROI estimates; no whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps are presented in the full text. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI study of executive function — working memory), I6 (task falls within executive function domain: working memory), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported for task phases/load/instruction), I9 (healthy adult participant group with within-group analyses). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (no evidence of a group-level voxelwise whole-brain activation map; acquisition was limited to 18 slices and analyses focused on ROIs). Therefore the study must be excluded per E3. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an event-related fMRI empirical study using a task (negative priming) that indexes inhibitory control, an established executive-function domain (inhibition). The paper reports within-group, voxelwise second-level random-effects contrasts (NeuI>C, NegI>C, NegI>NeuI) analyzed with SPM2 and provides whole-brain activation results with MNI coordinates (Table 2, figures). The methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text. Therefore it satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Although the sample is small (n=8), that does not violate inclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical PET study using task-based paradigms (translation and language switching) that probe cognitive control (inhibition and cognitive flexibility). The study reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses using SPM and reports coordinates/tables for within-group contrasts (translation vs reading; switching vs no switching). Participants are a within-group sample of healthy bilingual adults. Results are presented as voxelwise activation maps and tables. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an empirical PET study using a task-based executive function paradigm (self-ordered object working memory). It reports a within-group, voxelwise subtraction contrast (self-ordered task > control) with group-level statistical maps and peak coordinates (whole-brain voxelwise analyses, noting some superior coverage limits). The task falls squarely within the working memory domain (executive function). Participants are a healthy adult sample and results are reported as coordinates and described in text. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusions.

This is an event-related fMRI study that uses a parametric verbal working memory task (an established executive function domain) with both within-group contrasts (each load vs control) and random-effects group analyses. Analyses were performed voxelwise across the whole brain using SPM2, and results are reported with stereotaxic coordinates and tables. The paper thus provides task-evoked, group-level voxelwise statistical maps and within-group task contrasts for participant groups (pre-HD and controls), meeting all inclusion criteria and violating no exclusion criteria. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing complete assessment.

This PET study reports voxelwise, group-level task contrasts that probe conditional movement selection based on arbitrary visual cues — a form of cognitive control/selection (executive function). It includes within-group contrasts (conditional vs. power+precision and movement vs. rest), whole-brain voxelwise analysis with reported peak coordinates, and meets reporting requirements. Participants are healthy adults and the imaging modality (PET) is acceptable. The task maps onto executive processes (stimulus-response selection/cognitive flexibility/selection) relevant to the meta-analysis objective. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/coordinates) is provided, enabling extraction of activation coordinates and contrasts.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a 2-back working memory task (an established executive function domain) with both patient and healthy control groups. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise, whole-brain activation maps (BOLD), stereotaxic normalization, and statistical group analyses, including within-group task contrasts (task vs baseline) for patients and controls. Results and tables/figures describing whole-brain activation are provided, and the full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I10 and should be included.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (voice identity and location), which falls squarely within executive function (working memory). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (Z-maps registered to Talairach and corrected for multiple comparisons), and within-group task contrasts (location vs control; voice vs control; direct comparisons between tasks) at the group level. Partial-brain acquisition is noted (21 axial slices), but the analyses are voxelwise and thus meet the allowance for partial coverage. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using task-based paradigms including a 2-back working memory task (an executive function domain). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise analyses (mixed-effects, Z statistic maps, cluster-corrected) and presents whole-brain results in figures and tables. Within-group task contrasts (task vs rest/implicit baseline) are reported, and the participant sample (healthy adults) is acceptable. The full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (kinesthetic delayed-recognition), which falls within the executive function domain (working memory). The paper reports within-group voxelwise contrasts (Set 3 > baseline and parametric load analyses) using whole-brain SPM random-effects analyses and provides tables/coordinates and statistical maps. Participants are a healthy right-handed sample (within-group contrasts reported). Full article includes methods, results, and discussion (complete full text). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly examines spatial working memory (a core executive function domain) using task-based contrasts. It reports within-group voxelwise contrasts (memory-guided saccades vs visually guided saccades; visually guided saccades vs fixation) and presents group-averaged activation maps and Talairach coordinates. Functional data were acquired for whole-brain coverage in at least some runs and analyses use standard subtraction/voxelwise approaches. Participants are healthy adults. Results are reported as coordinates and described in the text. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only analyses, connectivity/resting-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical paper) apply. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study investigating working memory (complex DMS + Sternberg) and its interaction with long-term memory. It reports voxelwise, group-level random-effects SPM2 analyses with within-group task contrasts (e.g., DMS+LTM+ > DMS+LTM−), provides whole-brain results (tables/figures and coordinates) and functional connectivity analyses. Participants are healthy adults. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI of executive function (working memory), voxelwise group analyses (partial slice coverage but voxelwise), within-group contrasts, and reporting of whole-brain results in text/tables. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-group contrasts, empirical human neuroimaging data). Full text appears complete.

This is an event-related fMRI study manipulating verbal working memory (HOLD vs RELEASE), which directly assesses an executive function domain (working memory). Group-level, voxelwise analyses were performed using SPM (thresholds and voxel coordinates reported, activations tabulated and plotted), satisfying whole-brain/voxelwise reporting; partial slice coverage (6 contiguous slices) is present but allowed by criteria since analyses are voxelwise. At least one within-group task contrast is reported (task effects and HOLD vs RELEASE comparisons; EHR peak latency ANOVA and activation maps are group-level contrasts). Participants are healthy adults (within-group contrasts reported). Results are reported in tables/figures and described in text. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and should be included in the meta-analysis.

Full text provided is incomplete (only title/abstract). Inclusion met: I5 (PET task study), I6 (verbal fluency = initiation/executive domain), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported in abstract), I9 (healthy participant group). Inclusion NOT verifiable / not met: I7 (no clear evidence of group-level voxelwise whole-brain statistical maps reported in the provided text), I10 (no coordinates/voxelwise results or clear whole-brain reporting shown). No exclusion criteria (E3-E6) explicitly met in the available content. Because core methods/results are missing, cannot confirm required whole-brain voxelwise analyses; exclude pending full text.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory updating (an executive function). It reports group-level, voxelwise (random-effects) whole-brain analyses (parametric regressors and contrasts versus the 0-arrow baseline), thresholded maps and tables of peak coordinates, and ROI follow-up — satisfying whole-brain voxelwise reporting and coordinate tables. At least one within-group task contrast is reported (e.g., 3/6/9/12 vs 0-arrow, and parametric load regressors). Participants are a within-group sample of healthy adults. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. It does not rely solely on ROI or connectivity-only analyses and does not present only between-group contrasts. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI task-based empirical study that includes an executive-control task (reverse alphabetizing) designed to engage working-memory manipulation and monitoring, meeting I5 and I6. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level multivariate ST-PLS results with voxelwise maps, figures, and tables of local maxima (peak coordinates and cluster extents), satisfying I7 and I10. The analysis includes within-group task contrasts (e.g., EM retrieval vs Alpha; recency vs recognition) and within-group PLS analyses as described, meeting I8. Participant groups (young and older adults) are reported, satisfying I9. The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, discussion, and tables/figures, so full text is complete. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study should be included for a meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an event-related fMRI study of a delayed match-to-sample working memory task (executive function domain). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise random-effects analyses (SPM2 one-sample t-tests and ANOVAs), whole-brain thresholding and tables/figures, and within-group task contrasts (e.g., DMS delay > CON delay; object vs. location; familiar vs. trial-unique). Participants are healthy adults. Results are reported as voxelwise maps and coordinate tables. All inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI task-based study that includes a working-memory (episodic/working memory) paradigm, which falls within executive function domains. The paper reports within-group voxelwise contrasts (e.g., EWM > SM) for both healthy controls and AD subjects, with group-level SPM analyses and reported activation coordinates (tables/coordinates), corrected for multiple comparisons. Acquisition used slice-based EPI and voxelwise whole-brain normalization/analysis (partial-brain acquisition would still qualify). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study is an empirical fMRI paper with whole-brain voxelwise group analyses and within-group contrasts (approximate vs control, exact vs control, magnitude comparison vs baseline) and reports coordinates—thus it meets I7, I8, I9, and I10. However, the tasks are numerical processing (symbolic exact/approximate calculation and non-symbolic magnitude comparison) aimed at number representation and arithmetic development, not tasks that fall within established executive-function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore it does not satisfy I5 (study assessing executive function/cognitive control) nor I6 (tasks within executive function domains), so it must be excluded. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using a spatial Stroop conflict paradigm that probes executive control/inhibition. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (e.g., informative position vs. neutral cue contrasts, P–N; W–N; P–W) and voxelwise regression analyses relating preparatory activity to behavioral cueing effects. These are within-group task contrasts analyzed with random-effects group statistics. Participants are healthy adults. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and therefore appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met. Given these points, the study satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and should be included.

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). The study is an empirical task-based fMRI investigation of visual comparisons involving working memory (meets I5, I6) and reports within-subject contrasts (unilateral vs bilateral) consistent with I8; participants are healthy volunteers (I9). However, the provided content does not allow verification that at least one group-level voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked statistical map was produced or reported (I7 not verifiable). Because I7 (whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analysis) cannot be confirmed from the available text, the study cannot be determined to meet all inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are clearly met based on the available information.

Full text presents an fMRI task with whole-brain, within-group voxelwise contrasts (wins vs losses; high vs low provocation) and reports coordinates (satisfies I5, I7, I8, I9, I10). However the task is a Taylor Aggression Paradigm designed to elicit reactive aggression and social-emotional processes rather than an established executive function domain (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Although authors discuss cognitive control/conflict monitoring, the paradigm does not fall within the predefined executive-function task categories required by I6. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to meet I6 (task domain).

The study reports both EEG and fMRI experiments and includes a group-level, voxelwise within-group contrast (insight preparation vs. noninsight preparation) with whole-brain voxelwise analyses and cluster thresholds. However, the task is a compound remote-associates (insight/creativity) problem paradigm rather than a canonical executive-function task within the prespecified domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Although the authors interpret ACC activity as reflecting cognitive control, the task itself does not clearly fall within the listed executive-function domains (I6 not met). Therefore the study does not satisfy all required inclusion criteria and must be excluded.

This is a task-based, empirical fMRI study that directly examines selection/initiation and preparatory processes for action and includes working-memory demands for self-selection, fitting executive function domains (initiation, selection, working memory). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain random-effects analyses (thresholded statistical maps and conjunctions), within-group contrasts (observation vs self-selection and task vs baseline), and provides voxelwise results in tables/figures. Although slice coverage was limited (17 axial slices), analyses were voxelwise and therefore satisfy the partial-coverage allowance. The full text (abstract, introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). From the abstract, the study uses fMRI and includes a working memory task (meets I5 and I6). However, the available content does not permit verification of required whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked maps (I7), nor confirmation of a within-group task contrast (I8). I9 and I10 cannot be confirmed from the abstract alone. No exclusion criteria from the list (E3–E6) are clearly met based on the available information. Because the full text is incomplete, I cannot determine whether the study truly reports voxelwise within-group activation maps required for inclusion; therefore it is excluded pending provision of the complete article.

The study reports task-based fMRI using an event-related Sternberg working memory (WM) task (executive function domain). It provides within-group, voxelwise activation analyses (single-subject and random-effects group-level SPM5 analyses) comparing task vs baseline, and reports whole-brain voxelwise activation and connectivity maps. Participants are healthy adults (within-group contrasts reported). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for meta-analysis of executive-function activations.

This is an event-related fMRI study reporting whole-brain, group-level voxelwise activation contrasts (random-effects SPM analyses) comparing task conditions. The paradigm manipulates intentional/top-down control (instructions to ‘remember’ vs ‘look’), which falls under the executive domain of initiation/top-down cognitive control, and yields within-group task contrasts (e.g., high-intention encoding vs low-intention encoding; high-intention recognition vs low-intention re-viewing). Whole-brain results are reported (FDR-corrected maps and coordinates), and participant groups are healthy adults. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of task switching (cognitive flexibility), reporting group-level voxelwise activation maps (whole-brain acquisition and SPM96 analyses) and within-group contrasts (switching vs baseline; main effects of timing and task-order). Participants are healthy adults. Results are reported as voxelwise maps and tables/figures of peaks. Thus all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met (fMRI task-based executive function; task within executive domains; whole-brain voxelwise group analyses; within-group task contrasts; participant group qualifies; voxelwise results reported). No exclusion criteria (only ROI/connectivity/between-group-only/non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (includes intro, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports original fMRI data using a working memory (visuospatial) task — an established executive function domain — and presents group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task activation analyses (SPM random-effects), with within-group contrasts (experimental vs control). The full text includes methods, results, and discussion, and whole-brain results are reported. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an event-related fMRI study of a delayed-match-to-sample working-memory task (executive function domain). The paper reports voxelwise within-subject and group-level analyses using SPM99, produces whole-brain parametric maps, bootstrap and permutation tests, and reports Talairach coordinates and brain figures. Thus it provides whole-brain, group-level, within-group task contrasts and whole-brain results in tables/figures. The full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/rest-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met.

(a) Exclusion criteria met: none (no E3–E6 violations). (b) Inclusion criteria met: I7 (voxelwise, group-level fMRI analyses reported), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported), I9 (within-group sample reported), I10 (whole-brain results reported with coordinates/tables). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I5 and I6 — the study investigates visuospatial attention and implicit visuomotor responses to graspable objects rather than an established executive function/cognitive control domain (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Although the task uses cueing and a go/no-go design, the primary contrasts and authors' focus are on attentional orienting and visuomotor processing rather than executive control processes targeted by the meta-analysis. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present), so exclusion is due to not meeting I5/I6 rather than missing information.

Full text is incomplete (API error 'rate limit exceeded'); core article content (methods/results) not available to verify voxelwise whole-brain results or within-group contrasts. Based on available metadata: fMRI study (I5) using an oddball visual attention/vigilance task (I6) in a schizophrenia sample (I9) — these inclusion criteria appear satisfied. However I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group-level statistical maps) and I8 (at least one within-group task contrast reported) cannot be confirmed from the incomplete full text. No exclusion criteria are clearly met from available information. Because critical inclusion criteria cannot be verified without the full text, I exclude the study pending complete article access.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that used a validated spatial working memory (Visual Delayed Matching to Sample) paradigm (executive function domain: working memory). The paper reports voxelwise, group-level SPM2 analyses (whole-brain voxelwise contrasts) isolating the working-memory component (4s minus 1s delay) and reports coordinates/tables and figures of activation. At least one within-group task contrast (delay 4 > delay 1 / task vs matching) is reported. Participant group (healthy postmenopausal women) is acceptable. Results are presented in tables and figures. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so is complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (2-back vs 0-back) in healthy adults. The paper reports within-group task contrasts (each condition vs silent baseline and direct 2-back > 0-back contrast) and a group-level voxelwise analysis using spatial ICA and GLM with Talairach-transformed data and reported coordinates/statistics. Although acquisition covered only two contiguous slices (partial-brain), I7 allows partial-brain voxelwise analyses. All required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met, and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using memory-guided saccade and a spatial working-memory task (working memory is an established executive function). Analyses used voxelwise methods (Fourier and regression) to produce statistical activation maps, group-level summaries (mean Talairach coordinates, volumes, group polar plots), and within-group contrasts versus baseline/fixation. Partial-brain coverage (frontal, parietal, dorsal occipital) is acceptable per protocol. Results include whole-brain voxelwise maps, coordinates, and figures. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion, figures, references).

This is an event-related fMRI study of verbal working memory (an executive function). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise second-level analyses (ANOVA and paired t-tests) with whole-brain preprocessing and reports coordinate-based results for task contrasts. Within-group contrasts are present (e.g., Load1>Control, L2>L1, L3>L2, and target vs non-target paired t-tests). Partial-brain acquisition (24 slices) is used but the analyses are voxelwise rather than ROI-only; small-volume correction was applied additionally. Participants are healthy adults. Thus the study satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 and does not violate exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical study). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an event-related fMRI study of a spatial working memory (executive function) task with healthy adult participants. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain composite activation maps and Talairach coordinates, and presents within-group contrasts (memory vs control; positive vs negative probes). Methods, results, and discussion are present in full text. These satisfy inclusion criteria for task domain (working memory), imaging modality (fMRI), whole-brain voxelwise analyses (partial coverage acceptable), within-group contrasts, and acceptable reporting of coordinates/figures. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of verbal working memory (an executive function domain). It reports within-group task contrasts (letter recognition vs. letter-case judgment) and uses group-level, voxelwise random-effects analysis (SPM99) with whole-brain normalization and corrected statistics. Results are presented as whole-brain activation maps and coordinate tables/figures. Thus the paper meets all inclusion criteria for task domain, modality, voxelwise whole-brain analysis, within-group contrasts, and reporting of results. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures and references) is present and sufficient for screening.

Full text incomplete: provided content contains only a redirect line and article metadata (title, authors, journal, DOI) without methods, results or analyses. Cannot confirm key inclusion criteria: no evidence that the study used fMRI/PET (I5 not met), cannot verify task domain or task-based paradigm beyond the title (I6 not met), no information about whole-brain voxelwise analyses (I7 not met), and no evidence of a within-group task contrast (I8 not met). Also cannot confirm reporting format (I10 not met). No exclusion criteria from the list are clearly met based on available content. Therefore excluded due to inability to assess required inclusion criteria from incomplete full text.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of spatial working memory (an executive function domain). It reports group-level, voxelwise surface-based statistical maps and within-group contrasts (cue, delay, response; MGS vs SIR; task vs baseline), with results described in text and figures. Although acquisition emphasized frontal/parietal coverage (custom coils, 24 slices), the paper reports voxelwise surface-based group analyses rather than ROI-only approaches, and the protocol/analyses satisfy the meta-analysis’ allowance for partial-brain acquisitions. Participants are a within-group sample (healthy adults). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based (auditory 2-back) working memory paradigm (executive function). It reports within-group, voxelwise whole-brain analyses using SPM2 with random-effects group-level contrasts and thresholded statistical parametric maps; the paper describes main task responses and interaction contrasts and provides coordinates and figures. Participants are healthy adults (acceptable). Results are reported in text, figures, and tables. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so full text is complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10) and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory for haptically explored object orientations (working memory = executive function). The paper reports within-group, voxelwise group-level contrasts (exploration, delay, matching vs ITI; delay-length contrasts) and fixed-effects group analyses with whole-brain voxelwise statistics and cluster tables/figures. Acquisition covered the whole brain (except lower cerebellum) and voxelwise GLM contrasts are reported and thresholded (FDR), satisfying whole-brain evidence and acceptable reporting. Participants are healthy right-handed adults (within-group contrasts reported). Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables, figures, references).

The article reports an event-related fMRI task-based study of working memory/attention (retro-cueing), which falls within executive function (working memory). It provides group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (GLM, mixed-effects group analysis, cluster-based thresholding) and reports coordinates and statistical contrasts in tables/figures. At least one within-group task contrast is reported (e.g., interaction [(Q4 − Q2) − (N4 − N2)] and simple contrasts), qualifying as voxelwise task-evoked maps. Participants are a within-group healthy adult sample. Results are described in full (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and is suitable for inclusion.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of response inhibition (executive function: inhibition). It reports a within-group voxelwise contrast (Incorrect Matching minus Correct Matching) at the group level, with whole-brain acquisition (20 axial slices covering the whole brain) and voxelwise t-test maps, thresholding, spatial normalization, and Talairach coordinates for activation clusters. The paper includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (full text appears complete). It is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and provides within-group task activation maps. Therefore it satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10, and no exclusion criteria apply. Note: small sample size (n=5) is a limitation but does not violate inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using an oddball target-detection paradigm that explicitly assesses cognitive control/vigilance. The authors report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise mixed-effects analyses (FSL FLAME) with thresholding and provide figures and MNI coordinates for within-group contrasts (shape targets > novels; face targets > novels; direct face>shape contrast). Participants are a within-group healthy adult sample. Thus the paper meets all inclusion criteria for task domain (executive control/vigilance), whole-brain voxelwise group analyses, and within-group task contrasts. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study of working memory (a core executive function domain). It reports group-level, voxelwise random-effects SPM analyses (whole-brain), presents within-group task contrasts (WM delay/encoding/retrieval vs baseline and condition contrasts novel vs familiar), and reports coordinates and time courses. Participants are healthy volunteer groups with within-group contrasts reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI task-based study examining dynamic manipulation of auditory imagery that explicitly taxes working memory/central executive processes, meeting the executive-function domain. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain contrasts (word reversal vs baseline, rhyme judgment vs baseline, and word reversal minus rhyme judgment) with activation coordinates, tables and figures. Participants are a within-group sample of 12 healthy adults and within-group contrasts are reported. Although ROI/small-volume corrections are additionally reported, whole-brain voxelwise results are provided, so exclusion criteria for ROI-only or connectivity-only studies do not apply. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 and does not violate E3–E6.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study assessing executive function (working memory manipulation) using a memory-guided saccade paradigm with a colour-coded manipulation phase. The paper reports within-group, voxelwise, whole-brain random-effects group analyses (SnPM2) and presents contrasts (colour-coded memory-guided vs fixation; retention period contrasts) with tables/figures. Participants are human adults. All inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are satisfied (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that tests neural recruitment for quantifier comprehension and explicitly examines involvement of executive resources (working memory) in higher-order quantifiers. It used whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (SPM99, random-effects t-tests) with full-brain coverage and reports peak coordinates and figures/tables. Within-group task contrasts are reported (proposition+response minus proposition alone; higher-order vs first-order), and behavioral performance is provided. Participants are healthy adults. Results include whole-brain activation maps and coordinate tables. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for a meta-analysis of executive function task activations and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study of task switching (executive function: cognitive flexibility). The full text reports methods, voxelwise whole-brain GLM group-level contrasts (one-sample t-tests/random effects), within-group task contrasts (switch vs repeat; main effects and interactions), and tables/figures describing results. Partial-slice coverage is acceptable (they report slice parameters and whole-brain coverage), and results are reported in tables/figures in the text. The article therefore meets all inclusion criteria for task-based fMRI executive-function activation mapping and violates none of the exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study (simultaneous EEG–fMRI) using a mental arithmetic task that engages working memory/attention (executive domain). The paper reports voxelwise, whole-brain SPM99 analyses with group-level one-sample t tests on task-related regressors (state-related boxcar arithmetic vs rest) and PSI-related regressors, and presents coordinates/tables/figures (Table 1, Figs. 5–7). A within-group task contrast (arithmetic vs rest) is explicitly analyzed and reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for fMRI task activation in executive function domains, with whole-brain voxelwise, group-level results clearly described in text/tables/figures. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study (3T) reporting whole-brain, voxelwise group-level contrasts (complex g-task > simple g-task) using one-sample and two-sample random effects analyses and regression, with coordinates and thresholding reported. The paradigm elicits fronto-parietal activations tied to cognitive control processes (working memory/attention, reasoning/problem solving) and the authors explicitly link findings to working memory and cognitive control networks. It therefore meets criteria for fMRI task-based executive/cognitive-control investigation, contains within-group task contrasts, reports whole-brain voxelwise results, and is applicable across participant groups (adolescent sample). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10. No exclusion criteria apply. Overall confidence is high that the study fits the meta-analysis objective of pooling executive-function task activations.

Although this is a PET study with executive-like tasks (Divided Attention, Flexibility) and reports whole-brain voxelwise SPM results and stereotactic coordinates, the imaging was not task-evoked. 18-FDG uptake was measured while subjects relaxed with eyes closed (to capture tonic pharmacological effects) and neuropsychological testing was performed outside the 18-FDG uptake period. The reported voxelwise contrasts are pharmacological condition contrasts (ethanol influx/elimination vs placebo) and correlations between test performance and metabolism, not within-group task-versus-baseline activation maps. Therefore the study does NOT meet key inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI/PET assessing executive function during imaging), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map), and I8 (within-group task contrast). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (tasks fall within executive domains), I9 (acceptable participant group), I10 (coordinates reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Excluded on the basis of missing I5, I7, and I8.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a Stroop task (inhibition/cognitive control), meeting the executive-function domain requirement. The paper reports voxelwise group-level GLM analyses and whole-brain statistical maps (group average z-maps) with coordinates/tables and figures. Within-group task contrasts are presented (e.g., incongruent vs. neutral Stroop; Stroop vs. null), and results are reported for a healthy adult sample. All relevant core article sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) are present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply.

This study reports task-based fMRI (simultaneously with ERPs) using an auditory go/nogo paradigm assessing inhibitory control (an executive function). The paper presents voxelwise, group-level GLM analyses (nogo minus control) for within-group contrasts in both alcohol-dependent patients and healthy controls, with whole-brain thresholding and cluster reporting. Although imaging coverage appears limited (10 functional slices), the analysis is voxelwise and partial-brain acquisition is allowed by the review criteria. Results are described in the main text (frontal, temporal, parietal activations) meeting reporting requirements. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of visuospatial working memory (a canonical executive function subdomain: working memory). It reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (including permutation-based cluster inference), presents within-group task contrasts (encoding and recognition vs baseline/fixation), and provides tables of coordinates for activated regions. Participants (pre-menopausal women and matched controls) are acceptable per inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so content appears complete. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10.

This study reports task-based fMRI of spatial working memory (an executive function domain), includes whole-brain voxelwise group- and within-group (WM>AV and WM>PV) contrasts, and provides voxelwise results described across the text (with cluster thresholds and coordinates). Participants include clinical (schizophrenia/schizoaffective) and healthy volunteer groups. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met and no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an fMRI study of auditory temporal discrimination/timing, not an executive function or cognitive control task as defined by the review (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Although the paper reports whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise within-group contrasts (easy–baseline, difficult–baseline, difficult–easy), meeting several inclusion criteria, it does not assess an executive function domain (I5 and I6 are not satisfied). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study examining predicting/working-memory processes (executive function domain). It reports within-group voxelwise group analyses (random-effects SPM results) contrasting Predict vs Detect (and Predict vs Detect 3-back), with whole-brain results presented (figures and coordinate table). Participants are healthy adults. All required information (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables) is present in the full text. No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, and include within-group contrasts. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is a task-based fMRI study that directly investigates inhibitory control over task-irrelevant distractors (an inhibition/executive control domain), reports within-group contrasts across coherence levels, and presents voxelwise regional activations (MT+, LPFC) and whole-brain observations (pOTS, angular gyrus) consistent with group-level task-evoked maps. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so appears complete for screening. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI task activations related to executive function.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a verbal working-memory (0-back/2-back) paradigm assessing executive function. It reports voxelwise, whole-brain group-level analyses (one-sample and two-sample SPM2 results) with tables of MNI coordinates, including a within-group contrast (2-back vs 0-back) and main effects of olfactory stimulation. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of spatial working memory (delayed recognition of locations), which falls within executive function domains (working memory). The paper reports within-group task contrasts (delay-period activity vs baseline) and presents group-level voxelwise analyses (spatial normalization-based group analysis with group maps and voxelwise thresholding), satisfying the whole-brain, voxelwise requirement. Participant sample and methods are described. Whole-brain results are reported in text, tables, and figures. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full text is provided (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 and violates none.

This is an event-related fMRI study reporting group-level, voxelwise task activation maps (SPM99) for rule-based vs similarity-based categorization. The tasks explicitly engage executive processes (working memory, selective attention, response monitoring) and compare conditions within groups (Rule vs Similarity; task effects vs baseline). Whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (thresholds, Talairach coordinates, activation tables/figures). Participants are a healthy volunteer group (within-group contrasts reported). Results are presented as coordinate tables and figures, satisfying reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

Full text provided appears to be only title/abstract/metadata; methods/results/discussion not available. The abstract indicates a BOLD fMRI study of working memory in healthy controls with group analysis and behavioral correlations (so I5, I6, I8, I9 appear satisfied). However, the manuscript text is incomplete and does not allow verification that at least one group-level voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked statistical map is reported (I7) or that whole-brain results are reported in acceptable formats (I10). Because I7 and I10 cannot be confirmed from the provided content, the study cannot be included. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met based on the abstract alone.

Although this study reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise fMRI contrasts (Ambiguous vs Unambiguous) and within-group analyses, its primary focus is language comprehension and lexical ambiguity rather than an explicit executive function task. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group analyses), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (participant group acceptable), I10 (whole-brain results clearly reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (study does not assess executive function/cognitive control as a primary task-based paradigm), I6 (tasks do not fall within established executive function domains such as working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, or initiation; although working memory capacity was measured and inhibition/suppression is discussed, the paradigm itself is a sentence-reading language task). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study should be excluded from an executive-function meta-analysis.

This fMRI study investigates spatial working memory (an executive function) using task-based fMRI and reports voxelwise analyses at the single-subject level (n=5). However, it does not report a group-level, voxelwise task-evoked statistical map or group-level within-group contrast: analyses are performed and presented for individual subjects rather than a group-level statistical map. Therefore it fails the requirement for a group-level voxelwise analysis (I7) and thus does not meet all inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI on executive function), I6 (working memory task), I9 (participant group acceptable), I10 (results reported in text/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no group-level, voxelwise statistical map), I8 (no group-level within-group task contrast reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) were triggered. Full text appears complete.

Abstract reports an empirical PET study using the Wisconsin Card Sorting Test (an executive function task) with group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM95) and resulting statistical/power maps identifying task-related regions. These details satisfy inclusion criteria I5 (PET, task-based executive function), I6 (WCST = cognitive flexibility), I7 (group-level voxelwise/statistical maps across the brain), I8 (within-group task contrast/main effect of task implied by mapping activations), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (whole-brain results described). No exclusion criteria (E3-E6) appear to apply: the paper is not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical human imaging data rather than methods-only. However, only the abstract/metadata are provided here and the full article text is not available in the supplied content, so fulltext_incomplete=true and confidence is reduced accordingly.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that used an auditory n-back working memory task (an executive function domain). Group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported (mixed-model repeated-measures ANOVA with FDR correction and cluster threshold), with within-group task contrasts (activation vs control) and coordinates/tables for significant regions. Participant groups (smokers and nonsmokers; genotype subgroups) are reported and within-group contrasts are available. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Full text (only abstract/metadata provided) indicates an fMRI working-memory task (meets I5, I6) and reports a within-group contrast between activation and control (meets I8). Participants are a within-group healthy sample (meets I9). However, the methods state data were analyzed on the basis of manually defined anatomical regions-of-interest rather than reporting group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps. Therefore the study reports only ROI-based analyses with no voxelwise whole-brain results, violating inclusion criterion I7 and meeting exclusion criterion E3. Additionally, the provided content appears incomplete (only title/abstract and metadata), so fulltext_incomplete is set true.

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). The study is a PET face-recognition study using subjects' own faces, not an executive function or cognitive-control task per the review definitions. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (whole-brain voxelwise activations implied by reported regional activations), I8 (within-group task contrasts: tasks P and A vs C), I9 (within-group contrasts in healthy volunteers), I10 (whole-brain results described in text). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (does not assess executive function/cognitive control using a task-based paradigm), I6 (task does not fall within specified executive function domains such as working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). No exclusion criteria (E3-E6) apply. Because key inclusion criteria I5 and I6 are not satisfied and the full text is incomplete, the study is excluded.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of visual working memory and attention (executive domain). It reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (random-effects GLM, FDR-corrected maps) and provides within-group task contrasts (e.g., WM load 3 vs. 1; difficult vs. easy search) with coordinates and figures. Participants are healthy adults; results are reported as whole-brain statistical maps and tables. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext is complete.

This is an fMRI task-based study of working memory (n-back), an executive function domain, meeting the meta-analysis objective. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses using SPM5 (random-effects two-sample t-tests and group-level contrasts), with peaks and figures (coordinates and tables) described. Crucially, within-group/task contrasts are reported: pooled within-subject contrasts across all participants (Group High_M + Group Low_M [correct 3-n vs. correct 1-n]) and main effect of errors vs. corrects for all participants (Group High_M + Group Low_M [errors vs. corrects]) provide within-group task activation maps suitable for inclusion. Participants are healthy adults (acceptable per I9). Results are reported as voxelwise maps and coordinate tables (I10). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, empirical human neuroimaging data). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (1-back) — an executive function domain — reporting voxelwise, whole-brain mixed-effects analyses and within-group contrasts (sustained and transient activity; task vs baseline). It provides group-level, voxelwise statistical maps (thresholds, cluster sizes) and reports results in text/tables/figures for younger and older adult groups. The full text includes Intro, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and includes within-group contrasts). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective and is included.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function) using an event-related paradigm. Methods report whole-brain, voxelwise analysis (SPM2 random-effects, voxelwise thresholding and cluster extent) and report within-group contrasts (patients: within-subject paired t-tests pre/post; controls: within-group analyses/test-retest). Results include voxel coordinates and descriptions of whole-brain activation patterns. The task falls squarely within executive function (verbal working memory). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not connectivity-only; not only between-group contrasts; not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an event-related fMRI empirical study that examines action selection/preparation and working memory processes modulated by reward expectation — fitting executive function domains (planning, working memory, vigilance). It reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses using SPM99 (main effects and within-group contrasts: specific vs non-specific preparation; reward vs no-reward; interaction), with coordinates/tables and figures. Participants were healthy volunteers (within-group contrasts are reported). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that includes an executive function task (2-back working memory) and recognition (episodic) tasks (I5,I6). Analyses are whole-brain, voxelwise group-level GLM contrasts with voxelwise thresholds and cluster correction and reported coordinates/ROIs (I7,I10). Within-group contrasts (task vs fixation and material contrasts) are reported (I8). Participant groups are healthy adults (acceptable per I9). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This paper reports task-based fMRI experiments (N Back working memory and episodic memory paradigms) with group-level, voxelwise analyses (SPM99 random-effects) reporting whole-brain results and peak coordinates. Within-subject contrasts (Two Back vs Zero Back; encoding vs rest) were computed and used in second-level analyses. Results include SPM maps and coordinates for activations in prefrontal and medial temporal regions. Participant groups include healthy controls (and cognitive data include schizophrenia patients), satisfying applicability across groups. Therefore all inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function fMRI with whole-brain, within-group voxelwise contrasts are met; no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using the Tower of London planning task (an established executive function domain: planning). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (cluster-level inference corrected across the whole brain) and presents activation results in figures and tables. Within-subject contrasts for planning and movement execution were computed and entered into random-effects group analyses, satisfying the requirement for a within-group task contrast. Participants are healthy adults but the review accepts any participant group. The full text includes introduction, methods (task paradigm, imaging, preprocessing, statistics), results, and discussion, so the provided full text is complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is a task-based PET investigation of reaching that explicitly contrasts immediate pointing versus pointing to a previous (memorized) target, engaging visuospatial working memory and attention processes consistent with executive function domains (working memory/cognitive control). The abstract reports group-level analyses (analysis of covariance and t statistics) identifying regional cerebral blood flow increases across cortical and subcortical regions, indicating voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked results and within-group task contrasts (motor tasks vs visual detection; immediate vs previous). Participants are healthy adults, and results are reported in the text. Therefore inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 are met. No exclusion criteria are triggered. Note: only title/abstract/metadata were provided (no full article text like methods/results/discussion), so fulltext_incomplete is set to true and confidence is reduced accordingly.

This is a task-based fMRI study using a Stroop paradigm (a canonical inhibition/cognitive control executive task). It reports within-group, voxelwise, whole-brain group-level contrasts (e.g., incongruent vs congruent; error vs correct) with coordinates and conjunction analyses. Participants are healthy adults and the paper includes full methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for meta-analysis of executive-function task activations.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of cognitive control/conflict (size-congruity Stroop-like paradigm) that reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (random-effects, p'<.05 corrected) and within-group contrasts (incongruent vs neutral; congruent vs neutral). Results are reported as coordinates, tables and figures and include functional connectivity as supplementary analyses. The task probes executive function/inhibition/conflict monitoring, satisfying the review objective. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study of conflict resolution/cognitive control (executive function). It reports within-group voxelwise contrasts (e.g., incongruent vs congruent; high vs low conflict resolution) at the group level, provides whole-brain and ROI analyses with reported coordinates, and includes healthy adult participants. All inclusion criteria are met (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of cognitive control/executive function (cued global/local selective attention/conflict task) in healthy adults. The paper reports within-group, voxelwise, group-level analyses (SPM'99 random-effects ANOVA; voxelwise F-map used to define dACC ROI), and contrasts isolating conflict (incongruent vs congruent targets) and cue-related activity (cue-only vs cue-plus-target). Whole-brain voxelwise results are described and illustrated. Thus it satisfies all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

The study is an empirical PET task-based investigation of the Perceptual Maze Test (PMT), which taps executive processes including planning and rule-following (meets I5 and I6). The abstract describes within-subject contrasts (PMT vs SHAM motor control and rest) and reports task-evoked cerebral activations (meets I8 and I9). Whole-brain activation patterns are described extensively (occipital, parietal, prefrontal, ACC) consistent with group-level voxelwise task maps being reported (I7, I10), but the full article text (methods, results, statistical map details, coordinate tables) is not provided here to fully verify voxelwise/group-level analysis details. Because the available content is limited to title/abstract/metadata, fulltext_incomplete is set to true. I recommend inclusion pending verification of voxelwise, group-level statistical map reporting in the full text.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of the cognitive process 'refreshing', framed as a minimal executive-function/working-memory component. It reports within-group, voxelwise random-effects contrasts (e.g., Refresh > Repeat; Face > Scene) using whole-brain SPM2 analyses and group-level cluster results with coordinates and thresholds. Participants were a within-group sample of healthy adults. The full-text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function), I6 (task maps onto executive/WM processes), I7 (group-level voxelwise/whole-brain analyses reported), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (acceptable participant group), and I10 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study that directly investigates cognitive control/executive processes (strategic ordering, selection, working memory, monitoring) during temporal context retrieval and non-memory ordering tasks, using task-based paradigms. The authors report whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level random-effects SPM2 analyses (with coordinates/tables and ROI follow-ups) and multiple within-group task contrasts (e.g., recency > ordering; stimulus number and response number manipulations). Participants are healthy adults. Results are reported as voxelwise activations and coordinate tables. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is an event-related fMRI study of the antisaccade task, which probes inhibitory control (an executive function). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise GLM contrasts (e.g., correct antisaccades vs prosaccades; correct vs error antisaccades) with stereotaxic coordinates and cluster thresholds, satisfying whole-brain voxelwise evidence despite partial slice coverage. Within-group task contrasts are explicitly reported. Participant group (healthy adults) is acceptable. Results and methods (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are present in the provided full text. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study of working memory (simple working memory tasks) meeting the review objective. It reports task-based fMRI (group-level spatiotemporal PLS) with whole-brain voxelwise analyses and tables of local maxima, describes within-group task contrasts and main effects (e.g., modality, task demands, interactions), includes healthy adult participants, and presents activation results in figures/tables. Although slice coverage used 18 axial slices, the methods and group-level voxelwise analyses are reported and partial-brain coverage is acceptable per criteria. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion, so the article appears complete for screening.

This is an empirical, task-based PET study of executive control processes (semantic retrieval, monitoring, working memory). It uses group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM99) with multiple within-group task contrasts (e.g., SemSp – SylSp; SemVoCo – SemSp) reported with peak coordinates and figures. Tasks target working memory/controlled semantic processing (an executive domain). Results include whole-brain corrected statistical maps and coordinate reporting. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-group contrasts, empirical data present). Thus the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical PET study using a task-based paradigm (random number generation, RNG) that probes executive control (suppression of habitual counting/response suppression). The paper reports within-subject, within-group contrasts (RNG vs COUNT) and describes significant regional cerebral blood flow activations across multiple brain regions (left/right DLPFC, anterior cingulate, parietal cortices, cerebellum), indicating voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked results. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10. However, the provided “full text” here appears to be limited to title/abstract/metadata (no full methods/results/discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=true and this reduces certainty; confidence is therefore moderate. If the full article confirms voxelwise group-level statistical maps (as implied by the abstract), it should be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses and multiple within-group task contrasts in healthy adults (meets I5, I7, I8, I9, I10). However, the tasks probe visuospatial and temporal prediction, speed estimation and perceptual judgments rather than established executive function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Although the discussion refers to working memory involvement, the primary task demands are perceptual/anticipatory/sensorimotor, so criterion I6 is not met. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore excluded.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (executive function) using delayed-response tasks with parametric memory-load manipulation. The paper reports within-group task contrasts and random-effects, map-wise (voxelwise) group analyses and whole-brain acquisition, and presents methods, results, and discussion in full. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I10. No exclusion criteria apply (it is not ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI task study of visuospatial working memory/attention shifting (executive function). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise task activation analyses (random-effects model) with whole-brain (cluster-level corrected) results and coordinates/tables/figures, and presents within-group task contrasts (Rotation+Arrow, Rotation, Arrow, and Rotation+Arrow vs Rotation/Arrow). Although SEM connectivity is also reported, activation maps are clearly provided. Participant sample and methods are described in full. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for task-based whole-brain fMRI executive-function activations and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study with group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (SPM) reporting within-group contrasts (CA minus FR, FR minus CA) and tables/figures of activation. Although the paradigm is framed as category learning, the tasks explicitly involve maintenance and application of learned rules, working memory and attentional/control processes (rule maintenance, target monitoring, selection), which fall within established executive function domains (working memory/cognitive control). Participants are a healthy adult group and within-group contrasts are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article appears complete.

This is an event-related fMRI study of verbal working memory (Sternberg task) in healthy adults that reports group-level, random-effects, voxelwise analyses. The paper provides within-group task contrasts (phase-specific encoding/maintenance/retrieval regressors and high vs low load contrasts), uses conjunctions to identify phase-and-load-sensitive voxels, and presents whole-brain/partial-brain voxelwise maps and coordinate tables/figures. These satisfy inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function), I6 (working memory), I7 (voxelwise group analyses; partial coverage allowed), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (within-group healthy adult sample), and I10 (results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and includes within-group contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an event-related fMRI study reporting whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level task contrasts of tactile object discrimination that explicitly probe working-memory and discrimination processes. The paper reports within-group contrasts (P2 vs P1, P1 vs spheres, delay vs baseline), voxelwise statistical maps/coordinates with cluster- and voxel-level correction, and tables/figures of whole-brain activations. Participant group (healthy adults) is reported. Thus it satisfies the meta-analysis requirements for task-based executive function activations.

This is an fMRI task-based empirical study but it does not probe established executive function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). The tasks are sensory categorization and self-introspection/emotional judgment, which do not meet I5/I6. The study does provide whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level within-group contrasts (meets I7 and I8), includes healthy participant group (meets I9), and reports whole-brain results in text/figures (meets I10). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete. Conclusion: EXCLUDED because inclusion criteria I5 and I6 are not satisfied; included criteria met: I7, I8, I9, I10; inclusion criteria not met: I5, I6. No exclusion criteria applied.

This is an empirical PET study using a task-based paradigm that probes working memory and central executive processes (digits forward/backward). It reports group-level, voxelwise SPM contrasts (digit span tasks vs sensorimotor control; DF vs DB; linear contrast across difficulty), meeting whole-brain analysis requirements. At least one within-group task contrast is reported. Participant group (healthy adults) is acceptable. Full article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of analogical reasoning that explicitly manipulates and measures working memory and relational-integration processes. It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM99) and within-group contrasts (e.g., ANA > CAT, ANA > SEM) with tables/figures of activation, satisfying whole-brain reporting. Participants are healthy adults and within-group task contrasts are provided. The manuscript includes full methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5–I10 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study reports an event-related fMRI experiment using a delayed-saccade (working memory) task, isolating response selection and maintenance — an executive function (working memory) paradigm. The methods describe voxelwise GLM analyses and statistical parametric maps, selection of task-responsive voxels, and group-level within-group contrasts (reported t-tests across 14 subjects) for task epochs (delays, selection, response). Figures and statistical maps are reported in the text/supplementary figures. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text is complete. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function), I6 (working memory domain), I7 (voxelwise task-evoked analyses/statistical maps), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (healthy participant group; within-group contrasts reported), and I10 (results reported in figures/text). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an event-related fMRI study using a delayed face recognition (working memory) task, which falls within executive function domains (working memory). The paper reports within-group, voxelwise statistical contrasts (match vs nonmatch) and a whole-brain random-effects analysis with Talairach-normalized t maps (voxelwise thresholding), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Participants are a within-group sample of healthy adults. Results are reported in both ROI and whole-brain maps/coordinates. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only analyses, connectivity/rest-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met.

The study reports original task-based fMRI data using an oddball target detection/counting task that the authors explicitly link to working memory processes. It reports group-level, voxelwise analyses (spatially normalized, group-averaged voxel segments with thresholded activated clusters) despite partial-slice coverage, and presents within-group contrasts of targets versus baseline/noise (target-synchronized vs randomly synchronized control segments). Participants are neurologically normal volunteers. Results are described in text and figures as voxelwise activation clusters. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I5–I10 and violates no exclusion criteria. Partial brain coverage is acceptable per I7.
